category: metering/money-correctness
summary: The A2A delegating hop is metered (billed) and audited as OUTCOME_APPLIED at lines 2085-2098, but the pre-flight gates that can still abort the hop before any socket opens (route::hop_facts at 2119-2154, credential-lease minting at 2160-2183, binding resolution at 2201-2229, and the pooled walk's own refusal/pin-mismatch verdicts captured earlier at 1903-1904 but only acted on at 2261-2275) all run AFTER that charge. Any of those five exits returns an error response (502/refuse_hop_early/refuse_hop 503+Retry-After/render_pin_mismatch) having made zero bytes of contact with the backend agent, yet the caller's key was already charged and the audit trail already says APPLIED.
failure_scenario: A registered agent starts failing (e.g. answers 401/times out). The circuit breaker trips on the first failed hop (relay.rs record_hop_outcome/classify_hop). The caller submits a second task to the same agent: admitted() runs select_member, which sets walk_refusal = Some(BreakerOpen{..}) at line 1903 because the pool's breaker is open -- busbar has already decided NOT to attempt this hop. Execution nonetheless reaches meter_request (2085-2090), charging admitted.dispatch.billed_key_id one request, and audit_emit (2092-2098) records OUTCOME_APPLIED. Only then, at line 2261 (`if let Some(refusal) = walk_refusal { return refuse_hop(&hop_ctx, &refusal); }`), does the handler return 503 Service Unavailable + Retry-After and mark the task 'rejected' in the store. Net effect: the caller is billed for, and the ledger records as APPLIED, a hop busbar's own code explicitly refused to make -- with the ledger overcounting the operator's real backend traffic. This is exactly the scenario the module's own doc justifies charging a flat fee for locally-answered verbs 'with nothing priced on a hop that did not happen' (receive.rs:715) -- but the walk-refused/pin-mismatched/hop_facts-failed/credential-failed/binding-unspeakable exits are precisely hops that did not happen, and they ARE priced.
positive_control: grep -n 'BreakerOpen\|walk_refusal' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/tests/breaker_fastfail_tests.rs crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/tests/refusal_leak_tests.rs finds the exact scenario under test (breaker_fastfail_tests.rs::battery, submission 2, asserting 503+Retry-After and task.state=='rejected'), proving the scenario is real and reachable through the real router -- but grep -n 'meter\|charge\|billed\|MeteringRow\|list_metering' on that same file returns zero hits, so no test asserts what happens to the ledger on this path. The negative is not a search-path failure: the identical grep pattern against crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/tests/metered_verbs_tests.rs DOES match (it defines an `a2a_rows` helper against `list_metering` and asserts ledger rows for GetExtendedAgentCard and ListTasks), proving the method finds metering assertions where the authors wrote them and the absence on the breaker-refusal path is a genuine gap.

category: swallowed error / durable state drift
summary: Inside the streaming relay sink, a failed durable write of the resubscribe resume point (artifact_cursor) is discarded with `let _ =` -- no log, no metric, no error-once latch -- even though the comment at 2734-2737 states this exact cursor 'is the number a resubscribe reads', and the structurally identical adjacent failure (the state `transition` call at lines 2760-2797, six lines above) IS handled with an error-once-latched diag_error/diag_debug warning.
failure_scenario: A multi-chunk streaming A2A exchange is delivering artifacts to the caller; the taskstore has a transient outage on chunk N's advance_cursor call. The caller has already received chunk N over the live stream, but the durable artifact_cursor row is not advanced past N-1 because the Err(..) from advance_cursor is silently dropped. The stream then drops (remote agent fails partway through the multi-hop exchange, or busbar restarts) and the caller issues tasks/resubscribe. Resubscribe resumes from the stale durable cursor (N-1) and redelivers chunk N a second time to the caller -- a duplicate artifact -- with no diagnostic ever emitted that would let an operator explain why, unlike every other failure on this same code path which logs via diag_error/diag_debug with an error-once latch.
positive_control: grep -n 'A2A_RELAYED_OUTCOME_UNRECORDED\|STREAM_OUTCOME_UNRECORDED_WARNED' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/receive.rs matches the adjacent `transition` failure arm (lines 2780-2797) which DOES log the equivalent condition for the task-state write, proving the codebase's own convention on this exact code path is to surface a store-write failure rather than swallow it, and that the advance_cursor call six lines later breaks that convention rather than following a documented exception.

quote: /// The component a [`Usage`] scalar measures. Opaque to the engine, which meters the money scalar the
category: money / ABI contract contradicted by its only implementation
summary: The hot ABI promises the engine meters a Usage identically for all four UsageComponents, but the only host implementation records units for Tokens alone; Bytes/Frames/Queries land in the ledger as a request with every unit counter zero.
failure_scenario: A dropped-in plane meters a governed raw byte channel: Usage::charge(UsageComponent::Bytes, 4096, 0, admission) -> meter_charge. crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/govern.rs:290 token_usage_for() returns Some(..) only for UsageComponent::Tokens and None for Bytes|Frames|Queries, and governance/state.rs:901 MeterCounts carries only {requests, tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write}. So the 4096 consumed bytes are written nowhere: the metering row is requests:1 with all four token counters 0. Money is a VIEW of ledger x ratecard, and the ledger row has no quantity for any ratecard to price, so the consumption is silently free forever. crates/plugin-loader/src/tests/plane_conformance_tests.rs:693-696 asserts exactly this shape as correct (LAST_AMOUNT=4, LAST_MONEY_NANOS=0) against an INSTRUMENTED test host, so the conformance proof cannot see that the real host discards the 4.
positive_control: grep -rn 'fn token_usage_for' -A 10 crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/govern.rs matches and shows the Tokens-only arm; the control that the same path DOES carry a component through is the line above it, component_label(), which is reached for all four components (grep -n 'fn component_label' -A 8 crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/govern.rs).

quote: /// keys through the rate card (the dlopen analogue of the LLM plane's `usage_units`); when empty
category: money / dead ABI extension (compiled-in fold != dropped-in fold)
summary: The minor-20 Usage keyed-unit tail (units_ptr/units_len) that ABI_MINOR 19->20 and POD_VERSION 2->3 were bumped for is decoded by nothing outside this crate's own unit tests; the host never reads it, so a plane's keyed units are silently dropped.
failure_scenario: A dropped-in plane builds Usage::with_units(..., pack_usage_units({'input':1200,'output':800,'cache_read':5000})) and calls meter_charge, per this doc line's promise that 'the host decodes it and prices the keys through the rate card'. crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/govern.rs:207-258 (charge) reads only component, amount, unit_cost_micros and the key_id/model/provider tail; it never touches units_ptr/units_len and never calls decode_usage_units. Every keyed unit is discarded. A plane that follows the documented contract and reports its real quantities through units while leaving amount at 0 (because units carry the counts) is billed exactly zero. The COMPILED-IN fold does the opposite: crates/busbar/src/root/units_llm.rs:696 reads usage.usage_units.get(class) and prices each class off the rate card. So the same plugin, compiled in vs dropped in, produces different money.
positive_control: grep -rn 'decode_usage_units' crates/ returns only crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/pod.rs (the definition) and crates/busbar-plugin/src/tests/lib_tests.rs (3 test call sites) - no production caller. Control that the grep and path work: grep -rn 'usage_units' crates/ matches 20+ production sites including crates/busbar/src/root/units_llm.rs:696, i.e. the compiled-in analogue IS wired.

category: soundness / plugin-attested length used without a cap
summary: decode_usage_units forms a slice over a plugin-attested units_len with no bound - the only from_raw_parts on a plugin-supplied length in the whole slice that skips the cap every sibling path enforces.
failure_scenario: A signed third-party (or merely buggy) plane fills Usage.units_ptr with a 16-byte block but stamps units_len = 1<<40, advertising a size that covers the tail. The sized-struct guard proves only that the FIELD was written, not that the range it names is real, so decode_usage_units builds a 1 TiB slice over the plugin's heap and walks it record by record inside the engine's address space: an unbounded out-of-bounds read, ending in a SIGSEGV that takes the gateway down or in fabricated unit keys/counts read out of unrelated process memory and billed. Every other plugin-supplied length in this slice is capped first - crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs:477 (MAX_PLANE_VOCAB_LEN), crates/plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:301 (response_len_ok), crates/plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:715 (open_err_is_readable), crates/plugin-loader/src/hostlog.rs:83 (MAX_LOG_LEN). This one is the exception, and it is on the money path.
positive_control: grep -rn 'from_raw_parts' crates/plugin-loader/src crates/busbar-plugin/src | grep -v tests returns 5 slicing sites; four are preceded by an explicit cap and this one is not. The control that the grep finds guarded sites too is crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs:486, which appears in the same output with its MAX_PLANE_VOCAB_LEN check nine lines above it.

category: soundness / undefined behaviour at the seam
summary: JournalReframeFn is the one PLANE-IMPLEMENTED fn-pointer in the host vtable family and it returns the bare StatusClass enum by value (line 351) instead of the RawStatus carrier this ABI invented for exactly that direction.
failure_scenario: A plane registers a reframe through journal_register and its reframe returns 7 (a bug, a newer status class, or a hostile cdylib). RawStatus's own doc at crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/pod.rs:143-151 states the consequence: 'a byte outside 0..=4 materializes an enum with an INVALID DISCRIMINANT - UB the instant core touches it, BEFORE any match'. The host does touch it immediately: crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/journal.rs:400-403 does `let o = unsafe { out.assume_init() }; match status {` - and it assume_inits the ReframeOut BEFORE the match too, so on any non-Ok status it also reads an uninitialised POD, violating this crate's own init-only-on-Ok rule (crates/busbar-plugin/src/lib.rs:273). Every other plugin-implemented slot in this ABI was converted to RawStatus (PlaneDecl's seven slots all return RawStatus); this callback was missed.
positive_control: grep -n 'RawStatus' crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/decl.rs matches on all seven PlaneDecl slot types, proving the RawStatus discipline is applied to plugin-implemented slots; grep -n 'PLANE-PROVIDED' crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/host.rs returns exactly one hit (line 332), so JournalReframeFn is the only plugin-implemented slot in host.rs and it is the one that is not converted.

quote: extern "C-unwind" fn(host: HostCtx, counterparty: *const CounterpartyRef) -> TrustVerdict;
category: soundness / append-only enums are not back-compatible in the host->plane direction
summary: The RawStatus/RawFault/RawEgressKind/RawUsageComponent/RawFraming hardening covers only plugin->host bytes; six append-only #[repr(u8)] enums still cross host->plane as bare enums, which is undefined behaviour in an older-minor plane the airlock deliberately accepts.
failure_scenario: crates/plugin-loader/src/registry.rs:89 floors a plane's manifest abi_version at 1 and check_preamble (crates/busbar-plugin/src/lib.rs:137) refuses only a MAJOR mismatch, so a plane cdylib built against airlock minor 2 loads today. TrustVerdict gained variants 4..=8 in 'append-only minor-3' (crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/pod.rs:518). The minor-21 host answers trust_evaluate with TrustVerdict::GenerationMoved = 8; the minor-2 plane's own TrustVerdict has only 0..=3, so the returned byte materialises an invalid discriminant in the plane's compiled code - UB before any match, exactly the hazard the Raw* carriers were written for, with LLVM free to take any arm (including Allow) on a TRUST decision. The same shape applies to AdmitRefusal.reason: Unavailability (pod.rs:1241), EgressFault.fail_class: EgressFailClass (pod.rs:412), VerifyVerdict.outcome: VerifyOutcome (pod.rs:1823), IdentityAdmitted.outcome: IdentityOutcome (pod.rs:1928) and VerifyDecideFn -> VerifyDecision (host.rs:463), all of which are host-written and plane-read and all documented 'append-only'.
positive_control: grep -nE 'pub [a-z_]+: (StatusClass|Decision|EgressFailClass|VerifyOutcome|IdentityOutcome|Unavailability),$' crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/pod.rs returns the five bare-enum POD fields; the control that the same grep finds the HARDENED fields as Raw carriers is grep -n 'pub component: RawUsageComponent\|pub fault_class: RawFault\|pub kind: RawEgressKind' crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/pod.rs, which matches - so the split between hardened and unhardened fields is real, not a grep artefact.

quote: let honoured_size = busbar_plugin::honoured_size(advertised, ours as usize);
category: soundness / asymmetric over-claim handling on a vtable
summary: wire_up_plane CLAMPS a PlaneDecl that attests a size larger than this build's struct, where PlaneHostVtable::check REFUSES the identical over-claim - and PlaneDecl slots are fn-pointers the host then CALLS.
failure_scenario: A plane cdylib whose real PlaneDecl ends after `start` (built at an older minor, or hand-written in C/Zig) stamps size = 0xFFFFFFFF. Nothing here refuses it: `advertised < min` is the only size check (plane.rs:390), and honoured_size clamps the claim to size_of::<PlaneDecl>() = 152. DynPlane::slot_dispatch then reads offset 144 of the peer's static - past the end of its real decl - and DynPlane::dispatch calls whatever fn-pointer-shaped bytes live there, inside ffi_guard, which catches panics and not a jump to a garbage address. busbar_plugin's own honoured_size doc (crates/busbar-plugin/src/lib.rs:179-183) states the rule this path breaks: 'a wrong POD field is bad data, a wrong vtable slot is a fn-pointer this side then CALLS', and the host vtable therefore returns VtableRefusal::SizeOverBuild (crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/host.rs:846-849) rather than clamping. The decl direction is the same hazard with the opposite answer.
positive_control: grep -n 'SizeOverBuild' crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/tests/host_tests.rs matches (the host-vtable over-claim IS tested and refused); grep -n 'advertis\|SizeOver' crates/plugin-loader/src/tests/plane_conformance_tests.rs returns only the vocabulary-length test at line 580, i.e. no decl size over-claim test exists on this side.

category: safety / the hot lane bypasses the loader's own TLS-destructor invariant
summary: Every per-LOAD hot-lane crossing (config_validate, build, hydrate, start) runs on the CALLER's thread via the inline ffi_guard, while the cold lane's identical per-load crossing (busbar_open, the plugin's constructor) is confined to a never-retiring worker.
failure_scenario: crates/plugin-loader/src/ffi_thread.rs:53-62 states the cost model as a table: dlopen, busbar_abi, busbar_plugin_kind, busbar_open, busbar_set_log_sink, busbar_close and dlclose are all routed to a permanent worker precisely because a per-load crossing is cheap to confine and is where a plugin first arms a thread_local with a destructor; only the per-REQUEST busbar_call/busbar_free stay inline. DynPlane::build is the plane's CONSTRUCTOR - the exact counterpart of busbar_open - and it is inline. A dropped-in plane that statically links a thread-caching allocator or a runtime (the module names tikv-jemallocator as a live example) arms its own pthread_key on whichever thread called build; DynPlane::drop later dlcloses the image (plane.rs:96) and when that caller thread retires, __nptl_deallocate_tsd jumps into the unmapped hole - the exact SIGSEGV backtrace reproduced at ffi_thread.rs:17-20. wire_up_plane correctly uses ffi_guard_confined for abi/kind/plane_decl, so the inconsistency is within one function's neighbours.
positive_control: grep -n 'ffi_guard_confined' crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs returns lines 335 and 362 only (abi, plane_decl); grep -n 'crate::ffi_guard(' crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs returns 178, 227, 273 and 289 - config_validate, build, dispatch and hydrate/start. Control that ffi_guard_confined IS used for the cold constructor: grep -n 'ffi_guard_confined(&display, "open"' crates/plugin-loader/src/lib.rs matches at line 668.

quote: fn ffi_guard<R>(path: &str, op: &str, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> Result<R, String> {
category: safety / the panic guard's headline claim is unproven and probably false for its stated population
summary: No test anywhere exercises ffi_guard catching a panic that actually unwinds out of a dlopened cdylib, and for the population the doc names (a Rust plugin NOT built with the busbar SDK) Rust's catch_unwind treats an unwind raised by the plugin's own statically-linked std as a foreign exception and ABORTS.
failure_scenario: lib.rs:136-142 and lib.rs:271-279 claim this catch_unwind is 'EFFECTIVE' and is 'the single seam that fails such a plugin CLOSED instead of aborting the engine', naming 'a signed third-party (trust=signature, in-process) plugin NOT built with the busbar SDK that panics outside a caught region'. crates/plugin-loader/src/ffi_thread.rs:8 states the premise that defeats it: 'A plugin cdylib statically links its OWN copy of Rust std.' std's panic_unwind guards the payload with a per-std-instance CANARY static and routes a mismatch to __rust_foreign_exception, which is an rtabort - so a panic raised by the plugin's std copy and caught by the host's std copy aborts the process rather than returning Err (toolchain pinned at 1.98.0, rust-toolchain.toml). Concretely: a third-party store plugin panics inside busbar_call on one request; the documented outcome is a fail-closed StoreError, the actual outcome is the whole gateway dying and every in-flight request with it. Even setting the foreign-exception rule aside, the claim is untested: the ONE cdylib panic test (hook_panic_status_tests.rs) drives a fixture whose SDK catches the panic PLUGIN-side and returns STATUS_PANIC, so the host-side catch never fires.
positive_control: grep -rn 'ffi_guard\b' crates/plugin-loader/src/tests/ crates/plugin-loader/tests/ returns nothing; the control that the same grep over the same directories does match real symbols is grep -rn 'free_guarded' crates/plugin-loader/src/tests/, which matches ffi_guard_tests.rs:51 - and that test's panicking fixture (panicking_free) is an extern "C-unwind" fn compiled INTO the test binary, i.e. the same std instance, never a dlopened image.

category: lifetime / the ABI's free slot is never called and the state outlives its image
summary: DynPlane unmaps the plugin image on Drop but exposes no way to free the OpaqueState its build() handed out, so a built plane's state leaks and both its ptr and its free fn-pointer dangle into unmapped memory the moment DynPlane drops.
failure_scenario: OpaqueState is Copy + Send + Sync + 'static (crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/pod.rs:2211-2224) and carries `pub free: Option<extern "C-unwind" fn(*mut c_void)>` documented as 'run by the host on config swap'. DynPlane::build returns one and nothing on DynPlane ever calls it: on a config reload the composition root would build a new plane and drop the old DynPlane, at which point (a) the old plane's state - its connection pool, its threads, its file handles - is leaked with no reachable free, and (b) if anything still holds the OpaqueState, both `ptr` and `free` now address an unmapped image, so calling free is a jump into the hole. The cold lane does not have this gap: RawPlugin::drop calls busbar_close under a guarded worker BEFORE taking _lib (crates/plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:509-521); the hot lane's Drop only unloads.
positive_control: grep -n 'free' crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs returns nothing outside the doc prose; the control that the grep and path are right is grep -n 'free' crates/plugin-loader/src/tests/plane_conformance_tests.rs, which matches at line 671 where the TEST itself calls `free(p.ptr)` by hand for the config_validate handle - i.e. the ABI's free is reachable, just never from the loader, and never for the build handle at all.

category: the two folds are not the same / kind with no drop-in path
summary: The export kind has a complete drop-in seam (ABI, DynExport, open_export, an example cdylib, conformance tests) and zero production callers; the engine's export block hard-errors on any module name that is not one of the four compiled-in exporters, so a dropped-in kind:export plugin can never be reached.
failure_scenario: An operator builds and signs a kind:export tarball, drops it in plugins.dir, and writes `export: { my-sink: { module: my-sink } }`. scan_and_validate accepts and registers it (phases 1-3 all pass for kind 'export', supported_abi returns [2,3]), --list-plugins shows it as loadable, and then crates/busbar-kernel/src/config/mod.rs:1984-1988 rejects the config at boot with "unknown exporter 'my-sink'; the built-in export modules are prometheus | request-log-webhook | request-log-file | otlp". There is no config key anywhere that routes to open_export. So for the export kind the release claim 'compiled into the binary OR dropped into the plugins/ folder - same contract, same loading path' is false in the only direction that matters: the drop-in half loads and is then unreachable. export.rs:10-12 says so itself: 'The ACTUAL wiring of a delivery to the engine's metrics/audit/logs pipelines lands separately - this seam just proves an export plugin LOADS'.
positive_control: for f in open_store open_auth open_hook open_secret open_export open_plane; do grep -rn "\.$f(" crates/ | grep -v tests; done - open_store matches crates/busbar-kernel/src/appbuild.rs:1160, open_auth matches auth/mod.rs:234, open_hook matches hooks/mod.rs:250, open_secret matches preflight.rs:923, and open_export and open_plane match nothing. The four that match are the control.

quote: //! driven through [`DynPlane`], not yet INSTALLED into `busbar_kernel::plane::registry` beside the
category: the two folds are not the same / the plane kind has two unrelated contracts
summary: There are two structurally unrelated types both named PlaneDecl - the repr(C) drop-in one and the native Rust compiled-in one - with no adapter between them, and DynPlane has no production consumer, so a dropped-in plane contributes no config section, routes, claims, admission or scope kinds.
failure_scenario: crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/decl.rs:132 declares the repr(C) PlaneDecl a cdylib exports; crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane/registry.rs:811 declares a completely different, repr(Rust) PlaneDecl of &'static strs, fn(&dyn Any) -> Vec<(String,&'static str)> claims, fn(&BuildCtx) -> Option<Arc<dyn Any>> build and PlaneAdmission - and it is the second one that install_planes seals and that the router, the audience check and config_sections_from read. crates/busbar/src/main.rs:277-310 pushes only compiled-in &'static decls; nothing scans the plugin registry for kind:plane. So an operator who drops in a signed plane tarball gets a plugin that validates, resolves, and is never opened: no `example:` config section is recognised, no path is mounted, no RFC 8707 audience is bound. The compiled-in fold and the dropped-in fold of 'a plane' share a name and nothing else.
positive_control: grep -rn 'DynPlane' crates/ | grep -v 'plugin-loader/src' returns only crates/busbar-kernel/tests/plane_abi_rider.rs (an integration test). Control that the compiled-in fold IS wired: grep -rn 'install_planes' crates/busbar/src/main.rs matches at line 311 with five &PLANE_DECL pushes above it, and grep -rn 'struct PlaneDecl' crates/ returns exactly the two declarations named above.

category: version negotiation / ten store operations have no wire on any loadable plugin
summary: speaks_new_ops(abi) requires abi_version >= 5, but supported_abi("store") is [2,4] and a bare path load assumes 4, so the predicate is structurally always false and the ten operations this release adds are answered by a node-local in-memory shim on every deployment this binary can produce.
failure_scenario: validate_structure refuses any store manifest with abi_version outside [STORE_ABI_FLOOR=2, cold::ABI_VERSION=4] (crates/plugin-loader/src/registry.rs:53 and sign.rs:657-666), and load_store's bare-path form binds abi_version = 4. So speaks_new_ops is false for every store the binary can load, and append_batch, reserve, release, heads, session_put, session_remove, sessions_for, record_put, record_get and record_scan are permanently the shim. The concrete consequence the module itself names: the sealed admin replay cache and the slice grants are node-local memory. Restart a node after a credential-minting admin verb committed its replay slot, replay the request, and the slot is gone - the verb re-mints, which store_adapter.rs:50-53 identifies as 'precisely how a credential-minting verb re-mints, which is the one thing the sealed cache exists to prevent'. That is not a store-plugin quality problem an operator can fix by choosing a better store: no store can answer these ops, because the schema at which they gain a wire is above the window the loader accepts.
positive_control: grep -n 'speaks_new_ops' crates/plugin-loader/src/ -r shows the definition plus its call sites; the control that the SAME kind of schema predicate IS reachable in this window is needs_legacy_usage_wire (crates/plugin-loader/src/legacy_usage.rs:38, abi_version < 4), which is true for the published abi_version 2 stores the registry loads every day.

quote: pub trait Secret: Plugin + Send + Sync + 'static {
category: the two folds are not the same / the declared native contract has no implementors
summary: busbar-contract declares itself 'the one base trait every plugin implements, and the closed set of kinds', but five of its seven kind traits (Store, Secret, Hook, Export, AuthScheme) have zero implementors in the workspace; every real plugin on those kinds, compiled-in and dropped-in alike, implements the older busbar_api traits instead.
failure_scenario: There are two disjoint store contracts in one binary. crates/store-memory/src/lib.rs:344 `impl Store for MemoryStore` resolves to busbar_api::Store (imported at line 9), not busbar_contract::kinds::Store, and every engine seam is typed on the busbar_api one (crates/busbar-kernel/src/appbuild.rs:1160 open_store -> Box<dyn busbar_api::Store>). A plugin author who reads busbar_contract::kinds::Store as 'the store contract' - which crates/busbar-contract/src/plugin.rs:148 tells them to - writes a store the engine has no seam to bind, in either fold. The same holds for Secret::ref_grammar, Hook::max_priced_delta and Export::receive/ExportItem: declared, never implemented, so 'one contract, two folds' is, on five of seven kinds, one contract nobody is on and a second contract everybody is on.
positive_control: grep -rn 'fn ref_grammar' crates/ returns ONLY the declaration at kinds.rs:461; grep -rn 'ExportItem' crates/ returns only busbar-contract's own src and tests. The control proving the method-name search finds real out-of-crate implementors is grep -rn 'fn epoch' crates/ | grep -v busbar-contract/src, which matches crates/plugin-loader/src/store_adapter.rs:801 (impl SliceStore for StoreAdapter, line 769) - a busbar-contract trait that IS implemented outside the crate.

quote: let cstr = unsafe { std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(ptr as *const std::os::raw::c_char) };
category: soundness / the one ABI value passed without a length
summary: busbar_plugin_kind() returns a bare *const u8 with no length and the loader walks it with CStr::from_ptr, so a plugin that returns a non-NUL-terminated pointer causes an unbounded out-of-bounds read at the very first crossing of every load - the one plugin-supplied buffer in this ABI that skips the cap every other one gets.
failure_scenario: The trap is spelled out at crates/busbar-plugin/src/cold/mod.rs:82-86: 'the obvious hand-written busbar_plugin_kind() { kind::EXPORT.as_ptr() } compiles cleanly and is an UNBOUNDED out-of-bounds read in the engine'. Nothing host-side bounds it. A non-SDK plugin (C/Go/Zig, or a Rust author who returns kind::EXPORT rather than kind::EXPORT_NUL) makes read_plugin_kind scan the image's rodata until it hits a zero byte or an unmapped page: either a multi-megabyte 'kind' string built from unrelated process memory, or a SIGSEGV during boot or a hot config reload. This runs BEFORE the trust-verified bytes have been proven to be a busbar plugin at all, and it runs on the fetch_status/open_hook path that a Prometheus /metrics/hooks scrape drives.
positive_control: grep -rn 'MAX_PLUGIN_RESPONSE_LEN\|MAX_PLANE_VOCAB_LEN\|MAX_LOG_LEN' crates/plugin-loader/src returns a cap for every other plugin-supplied length (response, open error text, plane vocabulary, log record); the kind pointer is the only one with no constant, because the ABI gives it no length to cap.

category: the two folds are not the same / kind with no drop-in fold at all
summary: busbar-contract declares seven plugin kinds, but supported_abi has arms for only six; a kind:transport tarball falls into the catch-all and is rejected at scan, so transport is a kind that exists only compiled in.
failure_scenario: crates/busbar-contract/src/plugin.rs:23 declares 'The closed set of plugin kinds - SEVEN of them: plane, transport, auth, store, secret, hook, export.' There is no kind::TRANSPORT constant in crates/busbar-plugin/src/cold/mod.rs:88-123 and no 'transport' arm here, so a signed kind:transport tarball is an INVALID plugin at phase 1 and boot fails naming the file. This is deliberate and documented (crates/busbar-contract/src/transport/mod.rs:4-5 'Transports are in-tree only and never dynamically loaded'; registry.rs:15-18 says the same), so it is not a bug - but it does make the release's blanket claim 'each plugin can be compiled into the binary OR dropped into the plugins/ folder' false for one of the seven kinds, and the refusal message an operator gets says nothing about transports being in-tree only.
positive_control: grep -n '"store" =>\|"secret" =>\|"auth" =>\|"hook" =>\|"export" =>\|"plane" =>\|"transport" =>' crates/plugin-loader/src/registry.rs returns six arms and no transport arm; the control that the grep spells the arms the way the file does is that the six it finds are exactly the six kind constants in crates/busbar-plugin/src/cold/mod.rs's kind module.

category: usage/token extraction (money)
summary: The primary chat-completion usage read, for all six dialects, reads input/output token counts via read_count_u64(..).unwrap_or(0) instead of the crate's own usage_count::billed_count, so a present-but-unreadable count silently bills as zero instead of refusing.
failure_scenario: usage_count.rs's own module doc (lines 1-23) names this exact hazard and provides usage_count::billed_count to fix it: absent usage is legitimately 0, but a field that IS present and cannot be parsed as a count must refuse, never silently record 0, because 'the ledger records that no work happened, every money view over that row is faithfully derived and faithfully wrong, and nothing anywhere downstream can tell.' billed_count is wired into transcription usage (openai_chat/handler.rs:513-522) and Gemini transcription/image usage (gemini/handler.rs:668-676, 899-905) -- but never into the flagship CHAT completion path, in any of the six dialects, for either the buffered or the streaming read. Concrete trigger: an Anthropic-compatible or OpenAI-compatible self-hosted backend (a real traffic class this same code explicitly anticipates, e.g. the leniency comment at anthropic/reader.rs:723-728 and openai_chat/reader.rs:1248-1253) returns `"usage": {"input_tokens": "1500", "output_tokens": 42}` -- a stringified count. read_count_u64 returns None for a string (proven live: `cargo test -p busbar-llm-codec usage_count` passes `negatives_and_non_numbers_are_refused`, which asserts `read_count_u64(&json!("27")) == None`). `.unwrap_or(0)` then silently records input_tokens=0. This flows unmodified through IrUsage::to_token_usage() (ir/types.rs:1117-1133, no re-validation) into the Billing that the same-protocol usage tap reads directly. The customer is billed $0 input tokens for a request that consumed 1500 real, paid-for upstream tokens, with no error, warning, or refusal anywhere in the path, for every one of anthropic/openai_chat/openai_responses/gemini/bedrock/cohere, on both the buffered and streaming read paths. Identical pattern also confirmed at: openai_chat/reader.rs:1265-1279 (buffered) and :920-941 (streaming chunk), openai_responses/reader.rs:1572-1585, gemini/mod.rs:1701-1747 (gemini_usage(), shared by buffered and streaming per its own doc comment), bedrock/reader.rs:1149-1156 (streaming metadata frame) and :1373-1381 (buffered), cohere/reader.rs:1271-1282. All six dialects' ProtocolReader::read_response already returns Result<IrResponse, IrError> and already constructs Err(IrError{class: StatusClass::ClientError, ..}) elsewhere in the very same function for other malformed-body conditions (e.g. anthropic/reader.rs:670, openai_chat/reader.rs:1064-1068), so the refusal mechanism was available and already idiomatic at the exact call site -- this is a reachable, fixable gap, not an architectural constraint.
positive_control: cargo test -p busbar-llm-codec usage_count (run in the pinned worktree) -> 18 passed, including negatives_and_non_numbers_are_refused, proving read_count_u64 genuinely refuses a string-spelled count rather than silently accepting it, so the .unwrap_or(0) collapse at the sites above is reachable, not hypothetical. Contrast showing billed_count is not dead code and its absence on the chat path is a real gap: `grep -n usage_count::billed_count crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/openai_chat/handler.rs crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/gemini/handler.rs` matches 6 call sites, all on transcription/image leaf operations; `grep -n usage_count::billed_count crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/*/reader.rs` (the buffered chat read path for all six dialects) matches zero.

category: usage/token extraction (money) -- captured-then-discarded billed count
summary: RerankResp.search_units is correctly read off the wire from Cohere's meta.billed_units.search_units (and shared by Bedrock rerank), but RerankResp::billing() -- the one method both dialects' rerank IrHandle delegates to for the actual money signal -- discards it and always returns Billing::Flat, so every rerank call is billed identically regardless of how many search units it actually consumed.
failure_scenario: RerankResp carries `pub search_units: Option<u64>, // Cohere meta.billed_units.search_units` (rerank.rs:93) and it IS populated: cohere/reader.rs's read path and cohere/handler.rs:546 read it via crate::usage_count::read_count_u64 off meta.billed_units.search_units; bedrock/handler.rs:586-596 shares the same RerankResp type via read_rerank_response. But RerankResp::billing() (rerank.rs:97-102) is a hardcoded Some(Billing::Flat) that never reads self.search_units. Contrast with every sibling leaf op on the exact same pattern: EmbeddingsResp::billing() (ir/embeddings.rs) forwards the real usage field, ImageResp::billing() (ir/image.rs) forwards real token/image counts, and ModerationResp correctly returns Billing::Flat because moderation genuinely has zero usage-based cost (Billing::Flat's own documented use case) -- rerank is the one operation where a real, variable, provider-metered quantity is captured on read and then thrown away on the money path. Concrete scenario: a customer reranks 5,000 documents against one query (many Cohere search_units, a materially larger provider bill than a 1-document rerank); busbar's billing() call for that response returns the exact same Billing::Flat as a 1-document rerank -- busbar pays Cohere/Bedrock proportional to search units consumed but has no mechanism in this crate to charge the operator proportionally: the cost scales with usage, the charge does not. The doc comment's own excuse -- 'flat until the 1.3 pricing engine prices search units' -- does not hold up against the crate's own version context: this pinned tree is 1.6.0 (see docs/design/1.6.0-* and the neighboring 'Cohere billed_units (1.6.0 M1)' comment in ir/types.rs, which correctly cites its own current milestone). A gap deferred to '1.3' in a codebase now three minor versions past 1.3 is not an active, tracked, in-flight decision the way the 1.6.0 M1 Cohere billed-units note is -- it is a stale TODO that outlived its own deadline while the read side was built out around it.
positive_control: grep -n search_units crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/cohere/reader.rs crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/cohere/handler.rs -- 8+ matches showing the field genuinely traverses parse -> struct, proving the read side works; the zero-claim is specifically about the write/billing side of the SAME quantity: grep -n search_units crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/ir/rerank.rs shows the field declared (line 93) but billing() (lines 97-102) never mentions search_units at all. Positive-control contrast within the same file/pattern: ir/embeddings.rs's billing() DOES forward its usage field for the analogous case.

category: streaming chunk assembly -- cross-protocol content-block index collision
summary: Anthropic's streaming block-index DoS hardening clamps any index above 1023 down to 1023 instead of rejecting it, and at least the Gemini egress writer treats a repeated index as "the same block re-opening" -- so two distinct out-of-range tool_use blocks in one Anthropic-shaped stream collide into one Gemini tool accumulator, silently wiping the first tool call's already-accumulated arguments and losing one of the two tool calls entirely from the output stream.
failure_scenario: anthropic/mod.rs:558 defines MAX_ANTHROPIC_BLOCK_INDEX = 1023 and mod.rs:567's read_clamped_block_index clamps every content_block_start/delta/stop index to it before the value enters the IR, reasoning only about unbounded downstream allocation from a hostile huge index -- it does not consider index collision. gemini/writer.rs:829-848 (IrStreamEvent::BlockStart for IrBlockMeta::ToolUse) looks up the entry by IR index: if found, it OVERWRITES the name and CLEARS the accumulated args buffer (`entry.1 = name.clone(); entry.2.clear();`, lines 835-836) -- documented as intentional re-open behavior for a legitimately-reused index (comment at line 825: 'Re-opening the SAME index resets its accumulator'); only a genuinely NEW index gets a fresh entry (line 848). Concrete sequence on an Anthropic-shaped upstream (a non-standard/buggy Anthropic-compatible backend, or an adversarial one -- the same threat model the clamp itself defends against) egressing to Gemini: (1) content_block_start{index:1500, type:tool_use, id:toolA, name:lookup} -> clamped to 1023, BlockStart pushes a new entry (1023,'lookup',''); (2) content_block_delta{index:1500, partial_json:'{"q":'} -> clamped to 1023, appends to that entry -> (1023,'lookup','{"q":'); (3) BEFORE toolA closes, content_block_start{index:2000, type:tool_use, id:toolB, name:other} arrives -> ALSO clamped to 1023 -> BlockStart finds the EXISTING entry at 1023 and resets it to (1023,'other',''), silently destroying toolA's accumulated '{"q":' fragment; (4) toolA's content_block_stop{index:1500} -> clamped to 1023 -> flushes whatever is currently at 1023, i.e. tool 'other' with empty args {} -- toolA's real call is gone, replaced by a wrong name and empty arguments; (5) toolB's own deltas and stop, now clamped to the SAME index 1023, find the entry already removed by step 4's flush -- toolB's arguments are silently dropped (no matching entry) and its BlockStop finds nothing, so no functionCall frame is ever emitted for tool B at all. Net effect: one real tool call is corrupted (wrong name, empty args) and the other is completely missing from the stream the client receives, with no error surfaced anywhere. The precondition (a distinct content-block index >= 1024 in one stream) is explicitly called 'far above any legitimate block count' by the crate's own comment, so this does not fire on ordinary traffic from genuine Anthropic servers -- it requires a non-conforming Anthropic-compatible backend or a hostile one, which is exactly the threat model the clamp itself was written to cover.
positive_control: grep -n MAX_ANTHROPIC_BLOCK_INDEX crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/anthropic/mod.rs confirms the constant is 1023 (line 558) and is the only bound applied before the index reaches the IR (line 570). grep -n MAX_GEMINI_TOOL_FRAMES crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/gemini/mod.rs shows Gemini's OWN concurrent-tool-block cap is 4096 (gemini/mod.rs:241) -- four times higher than Anthropic's 1024 distinct index values (0-1023) -- so the Anthropic-side clamp is the binding, colliding constraint on this cross-protocol path, not Gemini's own (much looser) limit; this proves the collision window is real and not already closed by Gemini's own guard.

category: atomics-ordering / torn read of a two-atomic invariant
summary: `breaker_verdict` reads the (cooldown_until, breaker_state) pair in the SAME order every writer writes it, so a reader can pair a stale cooldown with a fresh state — the exact inversion the sibling FSM at busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs:246-254 documents as "an obligation, not a style choice".
failure_scenario: Every writer stores cooldown FIRST then state (cell_open_locked, breaker.rs:621-623; cell_closed_locked, :708-709; record_hard_down_all_cells' `trip` closure, availability.rs:560-564). `breaker_verdict` loads cooldown at :400 and state at :401, so its two Acquire loads are in writer order and a concurrent transition can land entirely between them. (a) Lane 0 is Closed, cooldown 0. Thread A takes a 401 and runs record_hard_down_all_cells -> stores cooldown = now+1800, then state = ST_OPEN. Thread B, mid-`select_weighted_for` (in_memory/mod.rs:909 -> cell_ready_breaker -> breaker_verdict), reads cooldown = 0 (pre-store) and then state = ST_OPEN (post-store): `now >= 0` -> ProbeWinnable -> `cell_ready_breaker` returns TRUE, so the just-hard-downed lane is admitted into the healthy set, consumes an SWRR pick, and is reported `usable: true` / `availability: available` by /stats and /healthz (snapshot, availability.rs:779/789) while it is benched for 30 minutes. (b) The mirror is worse: thread A's recovery `cell_closed_locked` stores cooldown = 0 then state = ST_CLOSED; thread B reads the OLD 30-minute cooldown then the NEW ST_CLOSED and decodes `Open { until }` -> `cell_ready_breaker` false -> `select_weighted_for` drops the just-recovered lane from `healthy`; if it was the only member left, `select_weighted_for` returns None and the request is shed as no-upstream-left even though the lane had recovered. The mutating admit path is separately guarded (cell_acquire_breaker re-reads under the transition lock), so the damage is confined to selection and to every /stats and /healthz reader — which is precisely the surface an operator uses to decide a lane is healthy.
positive_control: `grep -n -A1 'cooldown_until().load(Ordering::Acquire)' crates/busbar-kernel/src/store/in_memory/breaker.rs` over the whole file returns 6 pair-reads; 5 are either state-first (:775+:779, :785+:786, :865+:868) or taken under the transition lock (:681, :688-689, :795-796), and only :400-401 is both cooldown-first AND lock-free. The control that the method finds correctly-ordered code is `sed -n '253,254p' crates/busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs`, which matches `self.breaker_state.load` before `self.cooldown_until.load` in the same-named decoder.

category: check-then-act / race refuses a healthy cell
summary: `cell_acquire_breaker`'s under-lock re-check treats "no longer ST_OPEN" as Denied, so a cell a peer's recovery probe just CLOSED (ST_CLOSED, cooldown 0 — admissible) is refused instead of returning `ReadyNoProbe`.
failure_scenario: Request B calls try_admit (availability.rs:253). breaker_verdict at :265 reads ST_OPEN with an expired cooldown -> ProbeWinnable, so B proceeds, acquires a concurrency permit (:280), and calls cell_acquire_breaker (:290). Between B's lock-free pre-check at breaker.rs:775 and B taking the transition lock at :794, peer A's half-open probe SUCCEEDS: cell_record_success wins the HalfOpen->Closed CAS and cell_closed_locked stores cooldown = 0 and state = ST_CLOSED. B's re-check at :795 sees `state != ST_OPEN` and returns ProbeAdmit::Denied — even though the cell is now Closed and ready and the ST_CLOSED arm at :776-783 would have returned ReadyNoProbe. availability.rs:293-295 then drops B's permit and returns `Unavailable::ProbeInFlight`, so a request is failed over (or, if this was the last member, shed) against a lane that had just fully recovered. The sibling FSM does not have this hole: busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs:498-527 decodes ALL THREE states under the transition lock, so its ST_CLOSED arm yields ProbeAdmit::ReadyNoProbe.
positive_control: `grep -n 'ST_CLOSED =>' crates/busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs` matches line 502 (`ST_CLOSED => { if now >= until { ProbeAdmit::ReadyNoProbe }`) INSIDE `acquire`'s `let _tx = lock_recover(&self.transition_lock);` scope — proving the search names a real ST_CLOSED-under-lock arm and that its absence from in_memory's under-lock re-check is a real difference, not a grep artifact.

category: race-reason collapse / wrong Retry-After
summary: `ProbeAdmit` in the in_memory FSM carries no refusal reason, so every Denied — including one caused by a cooldown a peer armed between the verdict read and the CAS — is reported as `ProbeInFlight`, whose recovery hint is 250 ms instead of the cell's real (up to 30-minute) cooldown.
failure_scenario: A queued request holds a lane permit and calls try_admit_breaker (availability.rs:324). breaker_verdict at :343 says Ready. Before cell_acquire_breaker runs at :354, a concurrent 401 on another request drives record_hard_down_all_cells, arming cooldown = now + hard_down_cooldown_secs (default 1800). cell_acquire_breaker's under-lock check (breaker.rs:796, `now < cooldown_until`) returns Denied, and :355 maps it to `Unavailable::ProbeInFlight`. `Unavailable::recovery_hint_ms` (store/vocab.rs:82) answers PROBE_RETRY_FLOOR_MS = 250 for ProbeInFlight, versus `until.saturating_sub(now) * 1000` = 1_800_000 for BreakerOpen. The exhaustion terminal therefore emits a 250 ms Retry-After / recovery_hint_ms gauge for a lane that is benched for 30 minutes, and the client retry-storms a dead credential. The same collapse is on the main dispatch path at availability.rs:293-295. The sibling FSM fixed exactly this: busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs:185-193 splits `DeniedBy::Cooling { until }` from `DeniedBy::ProbeInFlight`, and lib.rs:467-468 maps them to `LaneState::Suppressed { until }` vs `LaneState::ProbeInFlight`.
positive_control: `grep -n 'DeniedBy::Cooling' crates/busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs crates/busbar-kernel-breaker/src/lib.rs` matches cell.rs:188/:506/:511/:525 and lib.rs:467 — the reason-carrying variant exists and is consumed; `grep -n 'enum ProbeAdmit' -A 12 crates/busbar-kernel/src/store/in_memory/breaker.rs` (line 284) shows the in_memory twin has a bare `Denied` with no payload, so the collapse is structural rather than a missed match arm.

category: mutex poisoning / inconsistent poison policy
summary: The egress pool mutex is the only lock in the slice that is NOT poison-recovering: 5 production sites take it with `.expect("engine pool lock")` while `DialGuard::drop` alone silently skips on poison, so one panic under the guard would both brick every later checkout AND permanently leak the dial budget.
failure_scenario: TRACED VERDICT ON THE LEAD: the eight `.expect("engine pool lock")` sites are real (pool.rs:317/580/723/738/779 production, :845/:864/:876 `#[cfg(test)]`, plus a ninth at client.rs:139, test-only), and the house pattern is `lock_recover` at store/mod.rs:64 (45 call sites across store/ and busbar-kernel-breaker/), mirrored by session/mod.rs:88, busbar-kernel-breaker/src/cell.rs:42 and the inline form at egress/mod.rs:368. If the guard ever poisoned, the cascade is exactly as claimed and is worse than symmetric: `deliver_dial_outcome` sets `guard.armed = false` only AFTER acquiring the lock at :580-581, so a panic at :580 leaves the guard ARMED, and `DialGuard::drop`'s `if let Ok(..)` at :467 then silently no-ops — `inflight_dials` is never decremented, the coalescing invariant `inflight_dials == min(waiters.len(), bound)` is permanently over-counted, and every parked waiter on that authority is abandoned (deliver_dial_outcome is a detached `tokio::spawn`, so the panic is swallowed with no log). BUT I could not reach the initial panic: I enumerated every statement inside the five production critical sections and the only panicking constructs are (1) `pm.map.get_mut(key).expect(..)` at :329, guarded by the `contains_key`/`insert` two lines above under the same hold; (2) the two `unreachable!()` in `deliver_h1_locked` at :693 and :698, both provably dead (the walk only ever sends `Ok`, and the value is constructed as `CheckedOut::H1`); (3) `Instant + Duration` overflow at :793 and :806 in `reap_loop`, unreachable because `pool_idle_timeout_secs` is never operator-configurable — every production EngineSpec is built with a literal (`EngineSpec::pooled_webpki(4, 300, ..)` at busbar-voice/src/mount.rs:1129, `EGRESS_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 4s` at egress/mod.rs:144); and (4) `tokio::spawn` in `ensure_dials` (:433) and `maybe_spawn_reaper` (:772), which panics only outside a runtime context — and every caller (`checkout`, `return_h1_conn` from client.rs:208/218, `clear_h2_generation`, `DialGuard::drop`) is inside a tokio task or a spawn_blocking thread, both of which carry the handle. So: the blast radius is confirmed and the outlier is real, but the trigger is not reachable in this tree — a resilience/consistency defect, not a live outage.
positive_control: `grep -rn 'lock_recover(' crates/busbar-kernel/src/store/ crates/busbar-kernel-breaker/src/ | grep -v 'fn lock_recover' | wc -l` returns 45 (the house pattern exists and is used), while `grep -n 'expect("engine pool lock")' crates/busbar-kernel/src/egress/engine/pool.rs crates/busbar-kernel/src/egress/engine/client.rs` returns 9 lines — so the zero-claim ("pool.rs uses no poison-recovering helper") is backed by a search that matches everywhere else.

quote:
other => errors.push(format!(
                "export.{name}.module: unknown exporter '{other}'; the built-in export modules are \
                 {}",
                EXPORT_MODULES.join(" | ")
            )),
category: plugin drop-in / config-boot correctness
summary: resolve_export() matches export.<name>.module against the closed 4-entry EXPORT_MODULES list (sections.rs:435-439) with no fallback arm to the plugin registry, so a kind:export plugin can never be named in config at all -- unlike every sibling plugin kind (secret, auth, hook, store), whose config-resolution paths all delegate an unrecognized module name to the loaded plugin registry.
failure_scenario: An operator builds, signs, and drops a real kind:export plugin (busbar ships an in-tree reference one: crates/export-example-plugin/src/lib.rs) into the plugins directory, then references it as `export.my-sink: { module: my-export-plugin, settings: {...} }` in config.yaml. config::resolve() (mod.rs) calls resolve_export() (mod.rs:1913) which `match def.module.trim()`s against exactly {prometheus, request-log-webhook, request-log-file, otlp} (sections.rs:425-439) and for any other value unconditionally executes the arm quoted above, pushing an 'unknown exporter' string into the accumulated errors Vec. resolve() then returns Err(errors) whenever errors is non-empty (mod.rs: the `if errors.is_empty() { Ok(RootCfg{...}) } else { Err(errors) }` tail), so boot, --validate, and every hot config-apply/reload that reaches build_app_from_config (appbuild.rs:480) fails outright with 'unknown exporter', never reaching the plugin loader at all. Nothing downstream ever gets a chance to load the plugin: appbuild.rs:518 captures only the typed 4-built-in ExportCfg (`let cfg_export = cfg.export.clone();`) and appbuild.rs:1394-1406 feeds only that typed struct into `crate::export::route_decls(&cfg_export)` to build the plugin HTTP route table; appbuild.rs's own comment at line 1396 describes routing for 'a future loaded export/hook plugin' as aspirational, confirming no such wiring exists yet for export. Independently, plugin-loader/src/registry.rs:398 defines a fully-implemented `open_export()` (verifies kind=="export", loads the plugin over the ABI, per registry.rs:72-80's version negotiation) but it has ZERO callers anywhere in the tree -- not in appbuild.rs, not in any production module, not in any test. The same closed vocabulary recurs in the offline migration tool: migrate_export.rs's migrate_one_export_projection (lines 189-204) can only infer a `streams:` projection for the same 4 built-ins and leaves a TODO ('is not a built-in export module in this build') for anything else, so even the config-upgrade tooling has no concept of a third-party export module. Net effect: kind:export is fully specified and implemented at the plugin ABI layer (trust verification, version negotiation, a complete ExportHandler SDK in plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs, an in-tree reference plugin) but is structurally impossible to activate through config -- an entire plugin kind is non-functional for anyone but the 4 in-tree built-ins, directly contradicting the release's central claim that core is a thin engine and every plugin kind (store, secret, auth, hook, export, plane, transport) is equally drop-in. sections.rs's own doc comment even states the restriction as apparently deliberate ('module: prometheus | request-log-webhook | request-log-file | otlp ... An unknown module is a boot error'), showing this was written as a closed enum rather than as a plugin-registry reference, unlike every sibling kind's doc comments in the same file tree.
positive_control: Every sibling plugin kind's config-resolution path DOES delegate an unrecognized module name to the plugin registry, proving the correct pattern exists and export is the outlier: config/secret.rs's SecretResolver::resolve (~line 80-99) has `module => match &self.plugin { Some(f) => ..., None => Err(...) }` -- any non-built-in module delegates to a loaded kind:secret plugin, never a hard 'unknown module' at config-resolve time. config/mod.rs's own resolve_auth (line 612) and hook_cfg_from_def (line 2039) both accept ANY non-empty module string with no closed-list match at all, deferring existence/kind checks to the plugin registry (documented explicitly in auth.rs:45-47's and hooks.rs's doc comments as 'resolved through the validated plugin registry'). Real callers confirm the deferred check actually runs for the siblings: `grep -rn "open_auth(" crates` matches busbar-kernel/src/auth/mod.rs:234 and :322; `grep -rn "open_hook(" crates` matches busbar-kernel/src/hooks/mod.rs:250 and :797; `grep -rn "open_secret" crates` matches busbar-kernel/src/preflight.rs:923; `grep -rn "open_store" crates` matches appbuild.rs:1160 (`plugin_registry.open_store(&g.module, &cfg_json)`). The identical search `grep -rn "open_export" crates` matches ONLY the function's own definition and its doc-comment mention in plugin-loader/src/registry.rs:73 and :398 -- zero call sites in busbar-kernel, busbar-mcp, busbar, or any test in the tree, which is the same grep methodology that found real callers for all four siblings. This gap is independently corroborated by an in-tree design document, docs/design/1.6.0-config-surface.md:888, which already records `plugins.yaml kind: export` as 'DOCUMENTED-NOT-IMPLEMENTED' because the separate scripts/plugin-registry-check.sh also hard-enums its KINDS set without 'export' -- a second, independent mechanism blocking the same plugin kind.

quote: It cannot take one out of its cell, because there are exactly two callers who can — the exit
category: doc-vs-code conformance: miscounted call sites / unenforceable completeness gate
summary: hold.rs asserts HoldCell::take has exactly two legitimate callers ('the exit path and the node's sweep'), but the crate's own construction-gate spec (caps/fixtures/lint_rules.rs:95-96) says there are three ('the exit path, the sweep and the tick'), the real kernel code has three distinct call sites (busbar-kernel/src/teller.rs:1207, teller.rs:1305, tick.rs:289), and the CI gate that is supposed to make 'no fourth anywhere' true cannot actually see the third (tick.rs) site at all because it scans for a literal substring that site's own code does not contain.
failure_scenario: A hold is the accounting reservation behind an admitted unit -- hold.rs's own module doc says 'a hold that goes away without a posting is a bug' and the sibling lint doc says 'a hold that vanishes is money that vanishes' (caps/fixtures/lint_rules.rs:38-39). The only automated guarantee that HoldCell::take is called from nowhere else is qa/construction.toml's [rules.seal-sites.symbols.hold-cell-take] gate (max_sites=0 outside teller.rs/tick.rs), implemented in xtask/src/gates/construction/rules2.rs's symbol_table_scan as `Regex::new(&rx::escape(symbol))` over the literal string "take(&Grant::<Exit>::mint(". That literal matches busbar-kernel/src/teller.rs:1207 and :1305 (2 hits) but produces ZERO hits against busbar-kernel/src/tick.rs, even though tick.rs:288-289 contains the crate's own documented THIRD legitimate take site (`let exit = Grant::<Exit>::mint(kernel.seal()); let taken = slot.cell().take(&exit);`) -- spelled with a local variable instead of the inline `Grant::<Exit>::mint(...)` the regex demands. If a future change adds a genuinely unauthorized fourth take call anywhere in the kernel using this same two-statement style (mint into a local, then `.take(&local)`), the seal-sites gate will report green (0 offending sites found) while a hold is being pulled out of its cell -- and possibly double-taken or taken without a matching posting -- from a site nobody reviewed. Both the doc's headcount (two) and the gate's coverage claim ('the literal that finds every take site', lint_rules.rs:91-92) are demonstrably false against the crate's own code.
positive_control: grep -n 'take(&Grant::<Exit>::mint(' crates/busbar-kernel/src/teller.rs matches lines 1207 and 1305 (2 hits), proving the literal CAN and does match a real take call when spelled inline. The identical grep against crates/busbar-kernel/src/tick.rs returns 0 hits (exit code 1) even though tick.rs:289 contains a third genuine HoldCell::take call — proving the zero is a blind spot in the scan's method, not an absence of a third site. hold.rs:55-56 ('exactly two callers') and caps/fixtures/lint_rules.rs:95-96 ('three take sites') also directly disagree with each other within the same crate.

category: budget-cap bypass / silent zero
summary: The live budget gate derives spend through a fixed four-element RESERVED_UNITS fold, while every other operation on the same ledger cell (accrue, total_tokens, flush, hydrate) is open-keyed, so any meter class a plane declares outside input/output/cache_read/cache_write prices at exactly zero against a `budget:` cap and can never move it.
failure_scenario: The enforcement cell is a name-keyed map: `BudgetCell::accrue` (governance/mod.rs:204-210) inserts EVERY key it is handed, `BudgetCell::total_tokens` (governance/mod.rs:236-239) sums EVERY key, `flush_budgets` (state.rs:2158) writes the delta over the UNION of keys, and `hydrate_budgets` (state.rs:1559) restores `m.usage_units.clone()` whole. Only the money derivation narrows: `cost.derive_spend_cents` -> `RateNanos::reserved_nanos` (cost.rs:199-205) folds `RESERVED_UNITS` (busbar-contract/src/records.rs:601 = ["input","output","cache_read","cache_write"]) and `RateNanos::reserved_rate` (cost.rs:175) answers `_ => 0` for everything else. The classes the planes actually declare and that are NOT in that four are, by name and file: `bytes` (busbar-plane-a2a/src/meta.rs:38, busbar-plane-mcp/src/meta.rs:43), `tool_calls` (busbar-plane-mcp/src/meta.rs:35, busbar-plane-streaming/src/meta.rs:179), `audio_seconds_in` (busbar-plane-streaming/src/meta.rs:172), `audio_tokens_in`/`audio_tokens_out`/`text_tokens_in`/`text_tokens_out`/`cached_tokens` (busbar-plane-streaming/src/meta.rs:134-165), `decision` (busbar-plane-decision/src/meta.rs:31), and — the sharpest instance — the LLM plane's OWN declared `tokens_in`/`tokens_out` (busbar-plane-llm/src/meta.rs:61,63), which are not the gate's `input`/`output`. Concretely: group g carries `budget: 500` per day; a plane reports `{"cache_read":1000,"tokens_in":5_000_000,"tokens_out":2_000_000}` through `GovState::record_usage`. `total_tokens()` counts all 7,001,000 so a `tokens:` cap sees them, but `derive_spend_cents` prices only the 1000 cache_read units: the 7M prompt/response tokens contribute ZERO cents and the 500-cent cap is never reached. The invoice pricer is structurally the opposite: `busbar_kernel_ledger::cost::price_exact` (cost/view.rs:354-364) iterates EVERY class in the entry and REFUSES (`MoneyError::ClassUnpriced`) on one the card does not name — its own doc at cost/view.rs:248-250 names exactly these classes and says 'this is the arm every reserved-four derivation in the tree is missing'. So the gate and the book cannot agree about any class outside the four, by construction, and the gate's disagreement is always in the caller's favour.
positive_control: Zero-claim is that `reserved_rate` prices nothing outside the four. Control showing the method and the path: `grep -n 'UNIT_INPUT => self.input' crates/busbar-kernel/src/cost.rs` matches line 171 (a key that IS priced) under the same read, while `grep -n '_ => 0,' crates/busbar-kernel/src/cost.rs` matches line 175 (the arm every other key falls to). Class-name enumeration: `grep -rn --include="*.rs" 'MeterClassId::new(' crates/busbar-plane-*/src/meta.rs` returns the 14 declared classes cited above, of which only `cache_read` and `cache_write` appear in `RESERVED_UNITS`.

category: budget-cap bypass / usage class omitted from the spend figure
summary: MCP and A2A traffic never accrues a single unit into the budget token ledger, so the only thing their traffic contributes to a `budget:` cap is `price_per_request_cents x billable_requests` — and that fee defaults to 0, which makes a spend cap unreachable by those planes entirely.
failure_scenario: `GovState::record_usage` is the only door into the enforcement token ledger; its single production caller is `plane_host/mod.rs:981` inside `MeteringHost::meter_ledger`, and `meter_ledger` is called from exactly two places, both LLM/voice: `busbar-llm/src/engine/usage.rs:93` and `busbar-voice/src/runtime/metering.rs:75`. The MCP and A2A planes call neither. What they do instead: `charge_round` (busbar-mcp/src/mcp/method.rs:2585-2612) admits through `govern_admit_reason` -> `GovState::try_admit` (which charges +1 `requests` and +1 `billable_requests` on every chain bucket) and then meters with `busbar_plugin::hot::UsageComponent::Queries` at amount 0 (method.rs:2604); A2A's `meter_request` does the identical thing (busbar-a2a/src/a2a/receive.rs:730). Host-side, `token_usage_for` maps that component to `None` (plane_host/govern.rs:298), so `record_metering` writes a row with requests=1 and all four token fields zero. Concrete scenario: group `agents` has `limits: [{metric: budget, amount: 500, per: day}]` and the deployment leaves `per_request_fee` at its default 0 (config/mod.rs:1722-1724). A caller issues 10,000 `tools/call` rounds that each proxy a multi-megabyte tool response. Every round is admitted; `cell.model_views()` stays empty for those buckets forever, so `derive_spend_cents(empty, billable, true)` = 0 + 0*10000 = 0 cents; the 500-cent cap is never approached and no `tokens:` cap ever leaves zero. The A2A plane nonetheless renders 'this key's budget is spent' (busbar-a2a/src/a2a/receive.rs:1544) as the only thing it can say about a cap that its own traffic cannot reach, and `charge_round`'s doc (method.rs:2552-2555) claims 'the key's budget and governance policy applies — a claim implemented by calling the same two functions rather than asserted' when only one of the two carries consumption.
positive_control: Zero-claim: `grep -rn --include="*.rs" -e 'meter_ledger' -e 'record_usage' crates/busbar-mcp/ crates/busbar-a2a/` returns NOTHING (exit 1). Control proving the identical command matches where the call does exist: the same pattern over `crates/busbar-llm/ crates/busbar-voice/` returns 9 files including busbar-llm/src/engine/usage.rs and busbar-voice/src/runtime/metering.rs. Second control proving the MCP/A2A paths are the ones I searched and are live: `grep -rn --include="*.rs" 'meter_charge' crates/busbar-mcp/ crates/busbar-a2a/` matches method.rs:2612 and receive.rs:738.

category: dead accrual path / token caps read zero
summary: `Door::record_usage` and `Door::record_usage_unchained` have no caller outside this crate's own tests, so every unit built on the new admission door charges requests at the door and then ledgers nothing — leaving all five token caps and the token half of every budget cap on that stack permanently at zero.
failure_scenario: `Door::try_admit` (decide.rs:252) is production-reached — `AdmissionUnit::admit` calls it at lib.rs:290, and `AdmissionUnit::new` is constructed at crates/busbar/src/root/units_mcp.rs:914, units_a2a.rs:1400/1509 and units_voice.rs:1350/1606 — and it charges `cell.requests += 1` / `cell.billable_requests += 1` (decide.rs:431-432). `Door::record_usage`, the only function in the crate that writes `cell.accrue(model, units)` (decide.rs:573), is never called by any of them. So on that stack `cell.model_views()` is empty for the life of the process: `bucket.tokens_cap`, `tokens_input_cap`, `tokens_output_cap`, `tokens_cache_read_cap` and `tokens_cache_write_cap` all compare against 0 at decide.rs:333-356 and can never block, and `pricer.derive_spend_cents(cell.model_views(), cell.billable_requests, true)` at decide.rs:359 reduces to `fee x billable_requests`. Configure a group with `tokens: 1000 per: day` on a unit served through this door and it admits unlimited tokens; configure `budget: 500 per: day` with the default zero fee and it admits unlimited spend. `budget_headroom_cents` (decide.rs:467) reads the same empty cell, so `AdmissionUnit::headroom_nanos` also reports the full cap as available to every hold top-up.
positive_control: Zero-claim: `grep -rn --include="*.rs" '\.record_usage(' crates/ | grep -v '^crates/busbar-kernel-budget/src/tests/'` leaves only `GovState::record_usage` sites (plane_host/mod.rs:981 plus comments and busbar-core-admin tests) — no `Door::record_usage` caller at all. Control proving the same grep does find live callers of the sibling method on the same type: `grep -rn --include="*.rs" 'AdmissionUnit::new' crates/busbar/src/root/` returns 5 production call sites, each of which reaches `Door::try_admit` through lib.rs:290.

category: budget-cap bypass / silent zero on an unpriced model
summary: The enforcement pricer the live door actually calls still drops a model the present rate card does not name, deriving that model's entire accrued consumption as free — the exact arm its own sibling in busbar-kernel-budget documents as a budget-cap bypass and replaced with a fail-closed refusal.
failure_scenario: `rate_for` returns `None` only when a rate card is PRESENT and the model is absent from it (cost.rs:692-696); this loop then skips that model entirely, so its whole token ledger contributes zero cents. `GovState::try_admit` calls this at state.rs:1970, so it gates admission. Scenario: `rate_card:` prices `gpt-4o`; group `eng` carries `budget: 500 per: month` and has accrued 480 cents of `gpt-4o` tokens this month. The operator retires the model — removes `gpt-4o` from `models:` and `rate_card:` and adds `gpt-4o-2025` — and reloads. The in-memory cell (and the hydrated durable ledger, state.rs:1559) still holds the `gpt-4o` ModelCell; `derive_spend_cents` now skips it, the derived spend for `eng` drops from 480 to 0, and the group gets a fresh 500 cents for the rest of the month. Nothing warns: there is no diagnostic on this arm, despite cost.rs:684-689 asserting 'the derive paths price it at 0 with a warn'. The sibling implementation of the same function in busbar-kernel-budget/src/price.rs:230 does `if self.model_unpriced(model) { return i64::MAX; }` and its doc (price.rs:206-214) states the reason verbatim: 'a present card with no entry for a model dropped that model's whole consumption, and the bucket derived as free ... that arm admitted a model against a `budget:` cap it never accrued against'. The fix landed on the copy that no production path calls (see the finding above) and not on the copy that gates every governed request.
positive_control: Control that the fixed twin exists and differs: `grep -n 'model_unpriced(model)' crates/busbar-kernel-budget/src/price.rs` matches line 230 inside its `derive_spend_cents`, while the same grep over `crates/busbar-kernel/src/cost.rs` matches only the definition at line 729 and no call site inside `derive_spend_cents`/`derive_spend_micros` (cost.rs:747-796). Control that cost.rs:755 is the arm the live door reaches: `grep -n 'cost.derive_spend_cents' crates/busbar-kernel/src/governance/state.rs` matches 1613, 1625 and 1970, the last being PASS 1 of `GovState::try_admit`.

category: money / gate counts a NAME, not the THING
summary: `no-float-money:count-read-shape` — the row whose title is 'a count is read with a silent zero default instead of a refusal (#81)' — only recognises silent-zero defaults spelled through a serde_json accessor, and every billed token count in this tree is now read through the crate's own `read_count_u64` helper, which the scanner has no needle for.
failure_scenario: `crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/anthropic/reader.rs:422-425` is `input_tokens: u.get("input_tokens").and_then(crate::usage_count::read_count_u64).unwrap_or(0)`. `read_count_u64` (crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/usage_count.rs:44) returns None for a value that is PRESENT and unreadable — a string-encoded int64 (Google's protobuf-JSON mapping encodes int64 as a JSON string), a non-integral float, a negative, anything >= 2^53. Anthropic returns `"input_tokens": "1200000"` for one turn; the ledger records input_tokens = 0 for real work, money is a view over ledger x ratecard so every downstream figure is faithfully derived and faithfully wrong, and nothing downstream can tell. `scan_count_reads` (line 991) iterates NUMBER_ACCESSORS only, so all 32 live production sites of this idiom are invisible and the row reports PASS. The crate itself documents the defect at usage_count.rs:93 ('# Why this exists rather than `.and_then(read_count_u64).unwrap_or(0)`') and the gate's own module header at line 91 claims the opposite: 'The eight billed reads in the LLM codec's own handlers were fixed to REFUSE rather than default (#81/#42) and their allowances are gone.' The allowances are gone because the detector went blind, not because the sites did.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM (the detector sees none of them): re-ran the gate for real — `./target/debug/xtask gate --all` line 468 prints `PASS  no-float-money:count-read-shape   no count is read with a silent zero default`. POSITIVE CONTROL that the search path and method are right: `perl -0777 -ne 'my $c=0; $c++ while /read_count_u64[^;]{0,120}?unwrap_or\(0\)/gs; print "$c\t$ARGV\n" if $c' $(grep -rl read_count_u64 crates)` -> 34 occurrences across usage_count.rs(1, a doc comment), cohere/reader.rs(6), gemini/mod.rs(6), gemini/reader.rs(2), tests/usage_count_tests.rs(1), anthropic/reader.rs(6), bedrock/reader.rs(4), openai_responses/reader.rs(4), openai_chat/reader.rs(4) = 32 live production sites; and the NEEDLE THE GATE DOES LOOK FOR does occur in the same files — `grep -rnw as_u64 crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/gemini/mod.rs` -> 1 hit — so the scanner reaches these files and simply cannot see the shape.

category: gate derives its yardstick from the thing it is judging
summary: `conformance:freshness` claims 'every armed passing verdict's `commit` equals the release commit — a pass carried over from an older sha is RED (§5.2)', but the release commit is computed as the MODE of those same verdicts' commits, so the all-stale case the row exists for is structurally incapable of failing — and it is failing to fail on HEAD right now.
failure_scenario: LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. All ten files in `conformance/verdicts/` carry `"commit": "67ee7910305068c2c86ccd1811d4bd189973b45b"`, which `git rev-list --count 67ee79103..HEAD` puts 647 commits behind HEAD (aad82a03e). `assess` (render.rs:299-313) counts the armed passing verdicts' commits and takes the most common one as the anchor; with all ten agreeing, `stale` is empty and the row reports PASS. Concretely: the release pipeline's artifact step silently re-uses the previous run's conformance artifacts, or the three `qa-conformance-*.yml` workflows are simply never re-run for 1.6.0. Every verdict agrees on the old sha, the anchor moves to the old sha, freshness is GREEN, `conformance/manifest.json` publishes `"release": "1.6.0"` against that commit, and the README ships green 'MCP conformant' / 'A2A conformant' badges attesting to bytes nobody ran the suites against. The only shape the row can catch is a MINORITY of stale verdicts, which is the selftest's single plant (conformance_sync/selftest.rs sets one verdict to 0000...).
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM (nothing in this gate consults git for the release sha): `grep -rn 'rev-parse\|GITHUB_SHA\|HEAD' xtask/src/gates/conformance_sync/` -> exit 1, no output. POSITIVE CONTROL, identical command over the parent directory: `grep -rn 'rev-parse' xtask/src/` -> 5+ hits (audit.rs:238 `Ok(self.run(&["rev-parse", "HEAD"])?...`, audit_cmd.rs:836, :967, :1295), so the pattern and the method both work. LIVE VERDICT: `./target/debug/xtask gate --all` prints `PASS  conformance:freshness   every armed passing verdict is about the release commit`.

category: rule structurally incapable of failing against its pinned baseline
summary: `refusal_findings` — the arm that catches a hand-written `Deserialize` quietly accepting an input form it used to reject — returns before doing anything whenever the BASELINE node has no `refused` key, and the pinned `v1.5.3` baseline the release actually uses has zero `refused` keys on any node, so the arm can never emit a finding.
failure_scenario: A developer relaxes `SecretRef`'s hand-rolled `Deserialize` so an inline literal secret now parses where the type existed to reject it — the exact defect classify.rs:288-291 names ('for a secret reference the widened form is an inline literal, the exact shape the type exists to reject and the one that ends up in a boot log'). `config-schema:snapshot-drift` reds once; `--write` re-pins the snapshot and clears it. `additive-only` then compares the fresh node against a v1.5.3 node that carries no `refused` key at all, hits this early return, emits nothing, and the row reports PASS. The inline-literal secret ships. CI pins this baseline by default: `mod.rs:115` is `pub const DEFAULT_BASELINE_REF: &str = "v1.5.3"` and no workflow or script sets `CONFIG_SCHEMA_BASELINE_REF`. Two selftest GREEN cases lock the dead behaviour in as correct ('a baseline with no `refused` key predates the arm and does not fire it').
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `git show v1.5.3:crates/busbar/src/config/config-schema.snapshot.json > /tmp/base.json; grep -c '\"refused\"' /tmp/base.json` -> 0. POSITIVE CONTROL on the identical file with the identical command form: `grep -c '\"fields\"' /tmp/base.json` -> 57 and `grep -c '\"kind\"' /tmp/base.json` -> 77, so the file is present (30652 bytes), readable and grep-able; the key genuinely is not in it. The CURRENT snapshot has 10 `refused` keys, so the two sides are not comparable by construction.

category: rule structurally incapable of failing against its pinned baseline
summary: `container_flag_findings` — the arm that catches `deny_unknown_fields` or `transparent` being flipped, i.e. WHICH OPERATOR DOCUMENTS PARSE — `continue`s on every node, every flag, every run, because the pinned v1.5.3 baseline records neither key anywhere.

category: vocabulary covers a minority of the taxonomy it claims
summary: The one constant that drives three of plane-purity's six category rules (SYMBOL at scanner.rs:249, KEY at :274, PATH-INCLUDE at :530) names three of the tree's five live plane keys plus one key that belongs to no crate, so two shipped planes are outside every vocabulary ban the gate enforces.

category: money/double-ledger
summary: On the live (default-on, root-llm) request path, a delivered LLM response's token usage is posted to two independently-priced money ledgers for the same event: the legacy synchronous accrual (`ledger_and_meter` -> `EngineHost::meter_ledger`/`meter_series`, fired inside `FirstByteBody`/`deliver_buffered` at stream end) and the new asynchronous `LateAccrual` posting in `busbar/src/root/units_llm.rs` (`Posting::from_usage` + `Posted::settle_late`, fed by `Walk::reported_after_terminal` reading the SAME `TapCell`).
failure_scenario: A governed key sends a normal chat completion (streamed or buffered) to a pool with a rate card. At stream end, `crate::engine::response_body.rs`'s `Poll::Ready(None)` arm calls `crate::engine::usage::ledger_and_meter` (engine/usage.rs:80-123), which charges `host.meter_ledger(...)` (the key's $ budget chain) and `host.meter_series(...)` -- explicitly documented in the same file as "the billing-facing usage ledger" (engine/usage.rs:107). Separately, `units_llm.rs::attach_late_accrual` wraps the SAME response body in `LateBody`; when it drains, `LateAccrual::post()` calls `walk.reported_after_terminal(&tap)` (walk.rs:474-501) -- reading the identical `TapCell`/`UsageSink` data -- prices it via `busbar_kernel_ledger::cost::price` and posts it with `Posted::settle_late` into the durable "book". `busbar-kernel-ledger`'s own module doc states it "hands each posting to the previous release's rows so nothing reading them notices a change," i.e. it writes into the SAME rows `meter_series` already populated. Both accrual sites run unconditionally for every delivered, governed, priced request. If both postings land in the same customer-facing usage/spend surface, every billable request is counted (and billed) twice; if they land in different surfaces, the operator's real-time budget/rate-limit view (old ledger) will permanently disagree with the durable invoice book (new ledger) for every request, violating the "money is never wrong" invariant. Verifying which of these two outcomes is true requires code in `crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host` and `crates/busbar-kernel-ledger` (both outside this slice); within this slice the call-graph shows both accrual paths firing for the same event with no coordination between them.
