The one-shot spend that the module header at consent.rs:31-34 says exists to stop "one an attacker had arranged to be in flight" therefore does not discriminate between two in-flight requests that differ only in where the credential goes.
positive_control: Zero-claim (the approval resolver never reads the redirect URI): `grep -n "redirect_uri" crates/busbar-oauth2/src/consent.rs` -> exactly 1 hit, line 267, inside a comment about `access_denied`; no code reads `request.redirect_uri`. Positive control, same file and same command shape for a field that IS read: `grep -c "client_id" crates/busbar-oauth2/src/consent.rs` -> 4 (including the live read at line 228).

category: CSRF / destructive state change on an unauthenticated GET
summary: `GET /auth/token?method=X&refresh=1` is an unauthenticated, exact-match-bypassed route that starts a login whose completion ROTATES the caller's issued busbar key (the prior token stops verifying); the destructive `refresh` flag is chosen by the query string and nothing binds the request to user intent.
failure_scenario: The victim is a developer who obtained a self-serve key through the hosted login and has it configured in Cursor/VS Code, and still holds a live session at the operator's IdP. An attacker gets the victim's browser to perform one top-level navigation to `https://gw.example.com/auth/token?method=corp-oidc&refresh=1` (a link, a 302 from an attacker-controlled page, an `<a target=_blank>`). `browser()` routes to `begin(app, "corp-oidc", true)`, which mints PKCE/state/nonce, writes `LoginCookie { refresh: true }` and 302s to the IdP. With a live IdP session the IdP redirects straight back with a code; `callback` completes the hop loop and calls `issue_and_render(..., cookie.refresh)` with `refresh = true`, which takes `SelfMintOp::Refresh` - documented at self_keys.rs:51 as "the prior token stops verifying". The victim's configured key is silently invalidated and every tool using it starts failing. `begin` reads no cookie and no CSRF token (the `__state` field exists only for the credential-form POST), so there is nothing between the navigation and the rotate. The same `?refresh=1` link is rendered on the key-issued page (`render_key_issued`, token.rs:1346) and that page carries no `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, so the link is also clickjackable.
positive_control: Zero-claim (no CSRF/state material is consulted anywhere in `fn begin`, token.rs:369-474): `sed -n '369,474p' crates/busbar-kernel/src/auth/token.rs | grep -c "FORM_STATE_FIELD\|read_cookie\|cookie_raw"` -> 0. Positive control, same symbol in the same file where it IS used: `grep -c "FORM_STATE_FIELD" crates/busbar-kernel/src/auth/token.rs` -> 4.

category: money-loss / audio-second accounting
summary: A Twilio call that ends (caller hangs up, sending the Media Streams `stop` event) while a duplex turn is still open discards that turn's accumulated inbound-audio milliseconds and tool-call count instead of reporting them, so real relayed audio goes unbilled.
failure_scenario: In `decode_twilio_frame`'s `TwilioEvent::Stop` arm (plane.rs:1036-1043), `state.close_turn()` (which zeroes `VoiceSessionState.turn` and returns the `TurnCounters { audio_ms_in, tool_calls }` accrued since the turn opened — see session.rs:117-125, 'Returns the counters as they stood at close, which is what feeds the response facts the meter step reads back out') is called and its return value is thrown away with `let _ =`. The `Ingress::Close` this arm returns then carries `facts: Box::new(Facts::new())` — empty. Every OTHER close path in this file (`IrServerEvent::Usage` at line 1341, `IrServerEvent::Error` at line 1395) takes the SAME `close_turn()` return value and writes it into `FACT_AUDIO_MS_IN`/`FACT_TOOL_CALLS`, which `meter()` (plane.rs:613-637) sums into the `audio_seconds_in` `UsageLocator` that prices the turn. Concretely: a caller places a phone call through the Twilio topology, speaks for several seconds mid-turn (each `media` frame after the opening one adds to `state.turn.audio_ms_in` via `encode_ingress_frame` at plane.rs:330-333), then hangs up before the upstream ever emits a `response.done` usage report or an error for that in-flight turn. Twilio sends `stop`; busbar relays/transcodes all of that caller audio to the upstream (real compute cost incurred) but the `audio_seconds_in` meter class for everything after the turn's first frame is never emitted for that turn — served, not billed. Because callers hang up mid-turn routinely (it is one of the two most common ways a phone call ends), this is not an edge case but a systematic under-count on every telephony deployment.
positive_control: grep -n "FACT_AUDIO_MS_IN\|close_turn" crates/busbar-plane-streaming/src/plane.rs shows the SAME `close_turn()` call correctly folded into billable facts at the Usage arm (line ~1341, feeding `meta::FACT_AUDIO_MS_IN` at line 1368) and the Error arm (line ~1395, feeding it at line 1410) — proving the intended pattern exists and is exercised elsewhere in this same file; only the Stop arm (1038) and the barge-in arm (1130, see next finding) discard it.

category: money-loss / audio-second accounting
summary: A client-authored barge-in (`conversation.item.truncate`) that arrives while a turn is already open closes that turn and discards its accumulated inbound-audio milliseconds and tool-call count the same way the Twilio `stop` path does, with no `Ingress::Close` ever emitted to carry the lost counters forward.
failure_scenario: In `open_or_relay` (plane.rs:1113-1163), when `interrupt_ms` is `Some` (the client sent `IrDuplexControl::ItemTruncate`, decoded at plane.rs:1097-1099), the function calls `state.close_turn()` at line 1130 and discards the result, then immediately falls into the `!state.turn_open` branch (true, since `close_turn` just set it false) and mints a brand-new turn via `Ingress::Open` — there is no `Ingress::Close` returned for the superseded turn at all, so its facts (including whatever `FACT_AUDIO_MS_IN` had accumulated since it opened) never reach `meter()`. Concretely: a caller on an OpenAI-Realtime or Gemini-Live duplex session speaks (turn opens, uplink audio accrues in `state.turn.audio_ms_in` frame by frame per plane.rs:365-378/1085-1095), the assistant begins responding, and the caller barges in — a normal, expected interaction in any voice app with client-side interrupt handling. The interrupted turn's uplink audio, already relayed to the upstream and paid for there, is billed at zero on busbar's own `audio_seconds_in` meter every single time this happens, silently under-counting spend on any deployment where the client (not the server-detected `SpeechStarted` path, which correctly stays `Partial` and keeps the turn open — see plane.rs:1260-1277) implements barge-in.
positive_control: The sibling `IrServerEvent::SpeechStarted` handling in `progress_from_server_event` (plane.rs:1260-1277) reads the SAME kind of interrupt signal but returns `Progress::Frame`/`FinishClass::Partial` WITHOUT calling `close_turn()`, correctly leaving the turn's counters intact — proving the codebase knows how to preserve a turn's accrued counters across a barge-in when the server detects it; only the client-authored ingress path (line 1130) discards them.

category: resource-leak / session-leak
summary: Every production call site that opens a voice `SessionHandle` discards it (`_handle`) without ever calling `settle_terminal()`/`close()`, and the plane's own idle-abandon callback is a hard-coded no-op, so every voice session's durable row stays ACTIVE in the in-process `DurableHandleEngine` working set forever, regardless of whether the client closed cleanly or vanished.
failure_scenario: `SessionHandle::close()` (runtime/scope.rs:227-229) only evicts a row that is both owner-matched AND already `terminal`, and `settle_terminal()` (scope.rs:211-222) is the only thing that sets `terminal = true`. A repo-wide search shows `settle_terminal(` has ZERO non-test call sites (only crates/busbar-voice/src/runtime/tests.rs:489 and src/tests/mount_tests.rs:371 call it), so no production session is ever marked terminal. Every place a session is actually opened and served discards the handle instead of settling+closing it: crates/busbar-voice/src/topology/telephony.rs:209 (`handle: _handle,` in `TelephonyProxy::run`'s destructure — the field is bound and simply drops when `run()` returns), crates/busbar-voice/src/mount.rs:1544 and :1572 (`if let Ok((core, _handle, _guard)) = open_admitted_session(...)`, the sideband and provider-less serving paths). Separately, `SessionHandle::open` (scope.rs:141-163) passes `|_id, _row, _pos, _now| None` (scope.rs:159, 'No sweep-time abandon transition for a voice session; teardown is explicit') as the engine's idle-abandon callback; `DurableHandleEngine::sweep`'s rule (0) (busbar-kernel/src/plane/handle_engine.rs:858-870) treats a `None` verdict as 'this handle was not abandoned' and does nothing, and rules (1)/(2) only ever evict TERMINAL rows. The result: a `VoiceSessionRow` is created for every voice session (WebRTC sideband, telephony proxy, or Gemini thin-duplex) and NEVER transitions out of ACTIVE and NEVER gets evicted by any code path that exists — not on a client vanishing mid-call, not on a clean hangup, not on the idle sweep. Over the life of a long-running busbar process the `voice_session` working set grows without bound (rule (2)'s `max_retained` cap only removes terminal rows, of which there are never any), which is an unbounded memory leak that will eventually degrade or crash the process under sustained voice traffic. The design's own playbook (docs/design/playbook/t2-runtime-session.md:127, 'Teardown: `handle.settle_terminal(now)` then `handle.close()`') documents this exact sequence as the intended teardown, confirming it is a gap rather than a deliberate design.
positive_control: grep -n "close_guard()" crates/busbar-voice/src/topology/mod.rs shows the SIBLING lifecycle method (the D2 lease's close guard, opened at the same call site as the handle) IS correctly captured and used (`let guard = lease.close_guard();` at topology/mod.rs:404, then held and dropped deterministically in every `run()`), proving the method-has-callers grep methodology finds real call sites when they exist; `settle_terminal(` returns none outside test files under the identical search.

category: backpressure / resource-exhaustion
summary: The downlink audio path (and the matching upstream-write funnel in the telephony proxy) uses unbounded mpsc channels with no queue cap and no stall detection, so a client or provider socket that stops draining lets busbar buffer arbitrarily much audio in process memory for the life of the session, with no backpressure signalled anywhere upstream.
failure_scenario: `Carrier::send_downlink` (carrier.rs:82-90) forwards every relayed downlink frame into an `UnboundedSender<Vec<u8>>` (carrier.rs:33, constructed at telephony.rs:84-85/141-142); callers (`session.rs:540`, `SessionCore::on_server_frame`'s caller) ignore the returned bool. `TelephonyProxy::run` (telephony.rs:229-238) similarly funnels both the downlink and the provider-write path through `unbounded::<Vec<u8>>()` channels drained by `forward(provider_out)`/`forward(client_out)` tasks. None of these channels has a capacity bound, and nothing in the session loop monitors how large the backlog has grown or hard-closes a session whose downlink consumer has stalled. Concretely: a telephony client whose TCP receive window fills (a stalled network path, a slow/broken client, or a deliberately non-reading peer) never causes `client_out`'s sink to be applied backpressure back onto the frame-decode loop — `send_downlink`/`unbounded_send` always succeeds immediately and audio keeps queuing in heap memory for as long as the model keeps producing it and the metering lease keeps the session open. With many concurrent long-lived sessions each pinned to a stalled peer, this is an unbounded-memory growth path with no operator-visible signal until the process is under memory pressure.
positive_control: grep -n "unbounded" crates/busbar-voice/src/topology/telephony.rs crates/busbar-voice/src/runtime/carrier.rs crates/busbar-voice/src/runtime/session.rs shows the SAME unbounded-channel pattern used consistently across all three audio-relay sites (as opposed to, say, the D2 metering lease's `AtomicU64`, which is a bounded, backpressure-free-by-design counter for a different reason) — the search reliably surfaces real matches, confirming the absence of any bounded/`try_send`-based channel anywhere on this crate's audio path is a genuine gap rather than a miss in the search.

category: architecture / duplicate metering pipelines
summary: The old `busbar-voice` plane (key `"voice"`) and the new `busbar-plane-streaming` plane (key `"streaming"`) both ship compiled-in and registered by default and both implement overlapping capability (OpenAI-Realtime and Gemini-Live duplex sessions) through two completely independent, non-communicating metering pipelines with no shared cap or rate-card key — an unfinished-rename split, not merely a naming issue.
failure_scenario: `busbar_voice::PLANE_DECL` (key `"voice"`) is installed at crates/busbar/src/main.rs:300 and `StreamingPlane` (key `"streaming"`, `PlaneMeta::KEY` at meta.rs:286) is registered at crates/busbar/src/root/registry.rs:463 — both gated by the SAME default-on `plane-voice` Cargo feature (crates/busbar/Cargo.toml:192 lists `plane-voice` in `default`; :221 `plane-voice = ["dep:busbar-voice", ..., "busbar-voice?/runtime", ...]`), so any build that ships voice at all ships BOTH. `StreamingPlane` claims the bare path `/v1/realtime` on transport `ws` for its OpenAI-Realtime dialect (claims.rs:150) and a Gemini-Live dialect matching `PathContains("BidiGenerateContent")` (claims.rs:158) — I verified these do not literally collide with `busbar-voice`'s own concrete mounted sub-paths (`/v1/realtime/client_secrets`, `/v1/realtime/calls`, `/v1/realtime/sideband/{call_id}`, `/v1/realtime/telephony/{call_id}`, `/v1/realtime/gemini/{call_id}`, mount.rs:322-351), so this is not a literal routing collision. But it means an operator's realtime-voice traffic is split, invisibly from the plane-key names alone, across two disjoint billing surfaces: `busbar-voice`'s D2 nanodollar reserve-then-settle lease (runtime/metering.rs, capped per session via `SessionBudget.cap_nanos`) for anything dialed through busbar-voice's own sub-paths, versus `busbar-plane-streaming`'s `UsageLocators`/meter-class rate-card path (`CLASS_AUDIO_SECONDS_IN` etc., meta.rs:84-127) for a client connecting straight to `/v1/realtime` or a Gemini `BidiGenerateContent` URL. A budget cap or rate card an operator configures believing it bounds 'voice' spend end-to-end only bounds whichever of the two pipelines their traffic actually transits, and the two pipelines share no code, no meter-class vocabulary, and (per this finding's evidence) no combined accounting — the exact 'two rosters disagree' consequence this round's brief asked about, arising from the crate still named `voice` sitting alongside the newer `streaming` plane rather than having been retired into it.
positive_control: grep -n "PLANE_KEY\|const KEY" crates/busbar-voice/src/lib.rs crates/busbar-plane-streaming/src/meta.rs confirms the two DIFFERENT plane keys ("voice" via busbar_voice_codec::PLANE_KEY re-export, "streaming" via StreamingPlane's PlaneMeta::KEY) that a correctly-merged single plane would not have; grep -n "installed.push(&busbar_voice::PLANE_DECL)\|StreamingPlane::EMPTY" crates/busbar/src/main.rs crates/busbar/src/root/registry.rs confirms both are actually registered, not just present in the crate graph.

category: untested / unreachable error branch (ledger integrity check)
summary: Finding::AnchorHeadDiffers -- the reconciliation check documented as catching 'the anchored history and this node's do not agree' -- is declared with a Display arm but is never constructed anywhere: verify() (crates/busbar-kernel-ledger/src/verify.rs:113-161) takes only (since: &Checkpoint, now: &BTreeMap<...>, windows: &dyn WindowState) with no anchor argument at all, so nothing in the current implementation can ever produce this variant, and no test exercises it because there is no path to exercise.
failure_scenario: A node's local checkpoint chain is replaced with an edited-but-internally-consistent history (e.g. rolled back to before a batch of settlements, or swapped for another node's chain) whose body_hash still verifies against its own stored figures. verify(since, now, windows) runs its residual/imbalance checks against that (now-wrong) `since` checkpoint and, because the two sides were edited together, returns an empty Vec<Finding> -- no CheckpointEdited, no Imbalanced. The rollback -- which un-settles real money and could let an already-consumed hold be replayed -- reads as a clean verification because the one Finding whose whole job is to compare against an externally anchored head is never actually computed.
positive_control: Every OTHER Finding variant verify() declares is both constructed and tested: `grep -n "CheckpointEdited\|Imbalanced\|Retired\|SequenceNotMonotonic\|ClosedWindowMoved" crates/busbar-kernel-ledger/src/tests/checkpoint_tests.rs` matches real assertions for all five (e.g. checkpoint_tests.rs:85 `.any(|f| matches!(f, Finding::CheckpointEdited { .. }))`, :217 `Finding::Imbalanced(i) => assert_eq!(i.residual.amount(), 5)`, :237 `[Finding::ClosedWindowMoved(c)] => ...`, :261 `[Finding::Retired { key: k, window }] => ...`, :309 `[Finding::SequenceNotMonotonic { node, was, now }] => ...`). Running `grep -rn AnchorHeadDiffers --include="*.rs" .` from the crate root returns exactly two lines in the whole repository -- the enum declaration (verify.rs:35) and its Display arm (verify.rs:76) -- confirming by the identical method that this is the one variant with zero constructors and therefore zero possible test.

category: concurrency invariant with no concurrent test
summary: The per-group concurrent-admission gauge's lock-free compare-and-swap loop -- the module doc at decide.rs:19-21 claims 'N racing admissions can never jointly overshoot' the configured `concurrent` cap -- is verified only by single-threaded, sequential tests; no test anywhere in busbar-kernel-budget spawns more than one thread against Door::try_admit.
failure_scenario: If the fetch_update's read-modify-write were weakened -- e.g. split into a separate load-then-compare-then-store, or an Ordering relaxed past what the CAS needs -- two threads could each observe `v < cap` and both increment, admitting N+1 (or more) concurrent requests against a group configured with `concurrent: N`. Each of those extra admissions is a real, billed upstream call the operator's concurrency cap exists to bound. No test in the suite would go red: every existing case (ported.rs::concurrent_gauge_holds_and_releases, ::rejected_admission_releases_concurrent_holds, and everything in mod.rs/leases.rs/cells.rs/price.rs/hold.rs) drives admissions one at a time on a single thread, so a race that only manifests under genuine concurrent contention has no way to surface.
positive_control: `grep -rln 'thread::spawn\|thread::scope' crates/busbar-contract/src/caps/tests/mod.rs crates/busbar-kernel-breaker/src/tests/mod.rs` both match real multi-threaded races over an equivalent lock-free/CAS structure: caps/tests/mod.rs:264 `two_threads_racing_the_take_produce_exactly_one_hold` spawns 8 threads racing HoldCell::take and asserts exactly one winner; breaker/tests/mod.rs:1038 `a_refusal_never_reports_a_state_that_would_have_admitted` runs 4 threads for 40,000 rounds against the breaker's single-flight probe. Running the identical search, `grep -rl 'thread::' $(find crates/busbar-kernel-budget -name '*.rs')`, returns no files -- confirming by the same method that the budget crate's own CAS-based concurrency claim is the one with no thread-based test anywhere in its tree.

category: SSRF / DNS rebinding (TOCTOU)
summary: HttpTransport::dial() accepts any string that parses as an http::Uri authority (including a DNS hostname) with no requirement that it already be a resolved IP literal, unlike the sibling busbar-transport-tls::split_address, which hard-refuses anything that does not parse as a SocketAddr.
failure_scenario: busbar_contract::transport::dest::UpstreamAddress::Socket.authority is documented (crates/busbar-contract/src/transport/dest.rs:54-55) as 'the dial target AS CONFIGURED (host:port, or a URL...)', and crates/busbar-llm/src/unit/route.rs:198-199 constructs it directly as `UpstreamAddress::Socket { authority: lane.authority, ... }` from the operator's configured lane data, with no visible DNS-resolve-and-pin step in that plane code. VerifiedDestination::seal() (busbar-contract/src/dest.rs:155-166) is a pure wrapper that stores whatever `facts`/`address` it is handed; it does not itself resolve or rewrite the authority. If the authority that ultimately reaches HttpTransport::dial() is ever a hostname rather than a pinned IP (whether via a bug in the out-of-slice trust/egress unit, a fallback path, or a deployment that names a plaintext http:// upstream by DNS name), the actual TCP connection is established by hyper_util's HttpConnector (default GaiResolver), which performs its OWN independent DNS lookup at connect time -- and again on every future reconnect drawn from this crate's pooled egress client (pool_idle_timeout / connection errors both trigger fresh connects). An attacker who controls the DNS answer for that name can let it resolve to a public IP at whatever moment the trust unit's allow/deny check runs, then rebind it to 169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1 / an RFC1918 address by the time (seconds, or hours later via the connection pool) hyper actually dials -- a classic DNS-rebinding SSRF bypass that defeats any IP-range judgement performed earlier. busbar-transport-tls closes exactly this hole for TLS-dialled destinations by requiring authority to already be a literal SocketAddr (crates/busbar-transport-tls/src/lib.rs:445-447: `let addr: SocketAddr = authority.parse().map_err(|_| TransportError::AddressRefused)?;`); busbar-transport-http has no equivalent backstop.
positive_control: grep -n 'SocketAddr = authority' crates/busbar-transport-tls/src/lib.rs matches (line 445-447: the sibling transport DOES enforce this), proving the search/read method finds this pattern when present; crates/busbar-transport-http/src/transport.rs and lib.rs contain zero occurrences of `SocketAddr` or any IP-literal check applied to the dial authority (confirmed by full read of both files).

category: Missing connect/handshake timeout -> resource exhaustion
summary: The gRPC transport's HTTP/2 connection preface has no timeout on either side: client.rs's handshake_h2 awaits hyper's http2 client handshake unbounded, and server.rs's serve_connection awaits hyper's http2 server connection unbounded -- unlike the sibling busbar-transport-tls (HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, 10s, wraps both TCP connect and the TLS handshake) and busbar-transport-ws (HANDSHAKE_BUDGET, 10s, wraps the WS upgrade) crates in the same slice.
failure_scenario: A peer (or an SSRF-reachable/misbehaving upstream on the dial side) completes the lower-layer TCP/TLS handshake -- which IS bounded by the composed tcp/tls layer -- and then never sends the HTTP/2 client preface or a SETTINGS frame. On the accept side, crates/busbar-transport-grpc/src/server.rs:88 (`let conn = builder.serve_connection(io, svc);`) is awaited with no timeout and the hyper::server::conn::http2::Builder has no keep_alive_interval/timeout configured (confirmed: zero occurrences of 'keep_alive' or 'timeout' in server.rs, client.rs, conn.rs), so the spawned per-connection task, its ConnState, and the accepted socket are held alive for the life of the process. On the dial side, GrpcTransport::dial (transport.rs:241) awaits `client::handshake_h2(stream, authority).await?` with the same absence of a bound, so a configured or reachable upstream that stalls after the transport handshake hangs the dial future forever, tying up whatever caller is waiting on it and the socket underneath. Repeating either from many connections is unbounded resource exhaustion (sockets, tasks, memory) purely at the gRPC layer, even though the identical class of risk is explicitly defended against one layer down (TCP/TLS) and one crate over (WS).
positive_control: grep -n 'tokio::time::timeout' crates/busbar-transport-tls/src/transport.rs matches 3 times (handshake_timeout wraps TCP connect and both accept/dial TLS handshakes) and crates/busbar-transport-ws/src/transport.rs matches HANDSHAKE_BUDGET/PONG_BUDGET/CLOSE_BUDGET usages, proving the search method finds this pattern where it exists; the identical grep across crates/busbar-transport-grpc/src/{client.rs,server.rs,conn.rs} returns zero matches for 'timeout|keep_alive' (confirmed by direct grep and by full read of all three files).

category: Missing read timeout -> resource exhaustion
summary: The egress HTTP exchange (waiting for the response head once a request has been sent) has no timeout of its own. The egress client sets a 10s connect_timeout and an HTTP/2 keep-alive ping (30s interval / 10s timeout), but those only bound the TCP handshake and detect a truly dead HTTP/2 connection; an HTTP/1.1 upstream (the default unless upstream_h2_prior_knowledge negotiates otherwise) that completes the TCP/TLS handshake and then never writes a response has no bound at this layer at all.
failure_scenario: A slow, hung, or hostile upstream (reached via ordinary configuration or an SSRF-adjacent path) accepts the TCP connection instantly, satisfying connect_timeout, then never sends any response bytes. `client.request(req).await` at transport.rs:275 blocks indefinitely -- there is no tokio::time::timeout wrapping it anywhere in lib.rs or transport.rs (confirmed by full read and by grep for 'timeout' across both files, which only matches the connect_timeout/pool_idle_timeout/http2_keep_alive_timeout constants). Each such call also holds the ExchangeGuard/resp_tx machinery and, per the crate's own doc, 'the caller's write deadline is a deadline on the exchange STARTING, not on an upstream choosing to stop talking' -- i.e. this transport explicitly delegates the read-timeout responsibility upward rather than enforcing one itself, unlike its own connect-timeout handling and unlike the sibling tls/ws crates' explicit handshake budgets.
positive_control: grep -n 'tokio::time::timeout' crates/busbar-transport-tls/src/transport.rs and crates/busbar-transport-ws/src/transport.rs both match (handshake budgets), proving the method detects this pattern when present; the identical search across crates/busbar-transport-http/src/{lib.rs,transport.rs} (excluding the tests/ subdirectory, which does use tokio::time::timeout in test code only) returns zero matches, confirmed by full read of both files.

category: security/spend control fails open on a live path
summary: AgentRegistration::registered (the only constructor) initializes the anomaly breaker's observation Window to all-zero, and nothing in production code ever writes to it again, so anomaly::evaluate's own floor check (`window.observations == 0 || ... < thresholds.min_observations`, busbar-plane-a2a/src/a2a/anomaly.rs:168) returns None before reading a single configured threshold, on every re-verification pass, forever -- including the egress_budget_ratio threshold, which is a spend control. The feature is inert a second, independent way: no operator config surface for the thresholds exists at all (they are always `anomaly::Thresholds::default()`), so nobody could switch it on even deliberately.
failure_scenario: An operator approves agent `planner`. `planner` later degrades or is compromised: it keeps serving its byte-identical, correctly-signed card (so the JWS/pin/drift machinery stays silent by design) while failing every dispatch and spending 10x its normal egress budget. Every delegated call runs the live chain receive.rs:2473 -> A2aPlane::reverify_agent (plane.rs:456) -> verify::reverify_once (verify.rs:316) -> `registration.apply_anomaly_breaker()` (verify.rs:375) -> `anomaly::evaluate(&self.window, &self.thresholds)` (registry.rs:187). Because `self.window.observations` is still the 0 it was constructed with, evaluate() returns None at anomaly.rs:168 without reading any threshold; the registration is never suspended, and the agent keeps serving and spending indefinitely. The module's own header calls this 'the ONLY remaining mechanism for correcting an approved agent that under-delivers' and 'a security control, not a ranking, so it has no soft form' -- and the control is inert. This is distinct from the live per-hop transport circuit breaker in relay.rs (`breaker_record_success`, relay.rs:1513, confirmed fed on every hop outcome): that one trips on connection failure; this is the only thing watching quality and SPEND on an agent that keeps answering successfully.
positive_control: `grep -rn '\.window\s*=\|window\.observations\|window\.errors\|window\.terminal_failures\|window\.latency_p95_ms\|window\.egress_spend_ratio' --include='*.rs' crates/busbar-a2a crates/busbar-plane-a2a` returns, across the whole slice, exactly: the field declaration (registry.rs:110), the one initializer (registry.rs:135), the read-only uses inside anomaly::evaluate's own body, and four test-only assignments -- no production writer. `struct Window` (anomaly.rs:95) has no `impl` block anywhere, so there is no mutator a field-grep could miss. The identical grep style finds real production mutations of sibling accumulation fields on the same struct in the same function: `registration.cached_card = Some(verified.document);` (verify.rs:349), `registration.sighting = settled.sighting.clone();` (verify.rs:371). Separately, `grep -n 'thresholds\|min_observations\|error_rate\|egress_budget_ratio' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/config.rs` returns zero -- confirmed directly -- proving no config surface exists. `grep -n 'allow(dead_code)|UNMOUNTED|DORMANT|not yet|no caller|unwired' crates/busbar-plane-a2a/src/a2a/anomaly.rs` returns zero hits, whereas the same grep finds explicit dormancy markers in 10+ sibling modules across both crates -- so this is not the codebase's documented-dormant pattern; the module presents itself as live and load-bearing while being inert.

category: money / hop consumed but never metered, and never breaker-gated
summary: Busbar-originated hops (busbar calling a fronted backend on its own behalf, not on a caller's relayed request) dial the backend for real over the same relay executor and transport, presenting a genuinely leased outbound credential -- but write zero ledger rows and zero audit rows anywhere in the file, and explicitly pass `breakers: None`, which both exempts them from breaker admission and stops their outcomes from ever being recorded against that agent's health.
failure_scenario: A caller with open tasks against agent `vendor-x` repeatedly calls `tasks/list`. receive.rs:1575 awaits `originate::refresh_listed_tasks`, which issues a REAL outbound LIST_TASKS hop to vendor-x via `issue_originated` -> `relay::relay` (originate.rs:150), presenting busbar's own leased credential (minted at originate.rs:81). The same shape fires on every push-config verb: receive.rs:1666 awaits `mirror_push_config`, whose read hop (originate.rs:255) and drift-repair write hop (originate.rs:283) are each a further real hop. Nothing on this path ever calls `meter_request` or `engine_host.audit_emit`, so these hops are invisible to the ledger; the caller pays only the one flat local-verb fee posted afterward at receive.rs:1690 -- identical to what a side-effect-free verb costs. This runs against the plane's own documented rule (meter.rs:13-16): 'DELEGATING, the chain TERMINATES AT THE HOP. busbar meters the hop it made ... against the INITIATING key.' Compounding it, `breakers: None` (this line, under a comment conceding 'None admits everything and records nothing') means these hops are not gated even when the breaker for that exact backend is already open from failing relayed traffic, and their own failures never feed the health signal either. A caller issuing a cheap, flat-priced verb in a loop can therefore generate unbounded, unpriced, un-circuit-broken real network traffic against a third-party backend busbar has already decided is unhealthy -- the mirror image of the already-confirmed receive.rs:2085 defect, which bills a hop that never went out; this lets a hop go out that is never billed.
positive_control: `grep -n 'meter_request\|meter_charge\|audit_emit\|Attribution' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/originate.rs` returns zero hits. The method is proven sound by the matching control `grep -rn 'meter_request(' crates/busbar-a2a/src/ | grep -v /tests/`, which DOES match the real charge sites (receive.rs:721 definition, :1232, :1690, :2085) -- so the grep finds metering exactly where the authors wrote it, and its total absence from this file is a genuine gap. The hop is proven real by reading the chain `issue_originated` (originate.rs:133) -> `relay::relay` (originate.rs:150) -> `prepare()` -> `seam.transport().send(...)`. Caller-reachability is confirmed directly: `grep -rn 'refresh_listed_tasks\|mirror_push_config' crates/busbar-a2a/src/ | grep -v /tests/` matches receive.rs:1575 and receive.rs:1666, both on the ordinary request path.

category: state-loss / trust-state regression on live config apply
summary: A2aPlane::from_config_carrying, which builds the A2A registry on EVERY config generation -- not only at boot, but on every admin config apply, since busbar_kernel::appbuild's plane-build loop (`plane_decls().iter().filter_map(|decl| (decl.build)(&ctx)...)`, appbuild.rs:1459-1461) calls every plane's build closure unconditionally regardless of which config section changed -- constructs a brand-new fail-closed-Pending AgentRegistration for every named agent, discarding the prior generation's approval, pin, sighting, cached card and reverify ledger; `carried_a2a_gates` (mod.rs:256-268) carries forward only the verify-on-call coalescer and boot-resolved card transports, nothing about trust state.
failure_scenario: Agent `planner` is fully Approved and serving normally with a cached card. An operator makes a completely unrelated admin write -- edits an MCP tool server, changes an LLM price, rotates a governance credential -- routed through `busbar_kernel::build_app_from_config` with the current App as `prior` (live call sites: busbar-core-admin/src/v1/json/handlers.rs:1563, :2278, :2524, :3064, named_map.rs:507). That rebuilds the whole App including the A2A plane; `from_config_carrying` rebuilds `planner`'s registration into `Approval::registered()` -- pin `None`, `Sighting::Never`, no cached card, a fresh reverify ledger -- regardless of the fact nothing about `planner` or even `agents:` changed. Because `TrustState::state()` (busbar-kernel/src/trust/mod.rs:298-299, `if self.pin.is_none() { return TrustState::Pending; }`) checks the pin BEFORE the sighting/observation match, no automatic re-verification can heal this -- the pin was an operator act and only an operator act restores it. The very next delegation request naming `planner` is refused at admission's own catalogue check (403, 'the agent is not in this caller's catalogue') before any metering -- every previously-approved A2A agent stops being delegable the instant any unrelated admin write happens, until an operator manually re-runs connect+approve for each agent again. A narrower, money-relevant instance: a request admitted a moment before the config apply lands can reach relay.rs's `prepare()` (`call.gate.still_delegable(...).map_err(RelayRefusal::Demoted)?`, relay.rs:1594-1596) AFTER receive.rs's meter_request/audit_emit OUTCOME_APPLIED (receive.rs:2085-2098, round 2's finding) -- so that in-flight hop is billed and then refused as Demoted, exactly like the already-reported breaker-open case, but triggered by mass config-apply demotion of every agent at once.
positive_control: `grep -n 'from_config_carrying\|carried_a2a_gates' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/tests/*.rs` returns zero hits -- no test drives a second config generation and asserts an existing agent's approval/sighting/cached_card survives it (the neighbouring tested properties are the floor-at-boot property, plane_tests.rs:91, and in-place-mutation via `with_registrations_mut`, plane_tests.rs:203 -- config-re-apply-preserves-approval is the untested gap). A gRPC caller hitting the same refusal goes through `status_for_error(error, parts.status)` (grpc.rs:226): `parts.headers` -- where Retry-After lives -- is never read anywhere in the file, and no `google.rpc.RetryInfo` detail is ever constructed. The refusal's code maps to `tonic::Code::Unimplemented`, which defines no backoff behaviour. A gRPC client that retries any non-OK status on a fixed short interval hammers the tripped breaker with no throttle -- and because of the separately-confirmed receive.rs:2085 ordering defect, every one of those refused attempts is billed before the walk-refusal check aborts it.
positive_control: `grep -n 'RetryInfo\|retry_after\|Retry-After\|parts.headers' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/grpc.rs` returns zero hits. The search term is proven correct by the matching control `grep -n 'Retry-After\|retry_after' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/receive.rs`, which DOES match receive.rs:2260, :3135, :3144, :3186 -- so the identical grep finds the cooldown where the authors wired it, and its absence from the gRPC binding is genuine.

category: wrong destination / wrong lane / misattributed cost (latent -- dormant plane implementation)
summary: In the busbar-plane-a2a crate's successor `Plane` implementation, `upstream_destination()` resolves the hop target by taking `self.agents().first()` rather than the agent the request actually named, and `approve()` (line 800) picks the `ResourceLocator` the same way -- so with more than one agent configured, every hop-carrying operation would be dialled, scoped and lane-priced against the first configured agent regardless of which one the caller addressed. Confirmed dormant today: the crate's own `tests/conformance.rs:5-7` states 'the composition root does not yet hand a request to this plane -- the existing engine still answers every one of them.'
failure_scenario: Latent rather than live. If this plane is ever flipped onto the live loop: an operator configures `alpha` (lane `a2a-a`, cheap) and `beta` (lane `a2a-b`, expensive). A caller sends `message/send` addressed to `beta`. `upstream_destination()`/`approve()` both resolve via `agents().first()` -- `alpha` -- so the request is dialled to the wrong backend, scope is recorded against `agent:alpha`, and the lane carried into pricing is `alpha`'s. Every call to every agent past the first is charged against the first agent's lane and ratecard.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'FACT_AGENT_ID' crates/` returns exactly two hits -- its declaration and its listing in `SESSION_FACTS` -- and nothing that sets or reads it. The identical search for its sibling on the same list, `FACT_VERSION`, finds a genuine consumer at plane.rs:557, proving the search shape finds facts that ARE plumbed and that the agent-id zero is real. The live sibling does this correctly by contrast: busbar-a2a's own plane.rs resolves per-agent state with `.find(|r| r.agent_id == agent_id)` in `fetch_policy_for`, `pin_for`, `reverify_agent` and `verify_state_of`.

category: duplicate push delivery on a backend retry
summary: When a backend re-reports a state busbar already holds, the handler correctly skips the durable transition (recognizing it as a retry) but the onward caller-facing delivery is gated only on `moved.push_callback.is_some()`, unaffected by that decision -- so a real outbound POST to the caller's webhook still fires and another delivery event is appended to the task's durable chain for an event that moved nothing.
failure_scenario: A task is non-terminal with a caller webhook registered. The backend POSTs the same status twice. The second POST passes the token/rate checks, takes the `reported == task.state` branch so no transition is recorded, but the delivery block still fires, re-notifying the caller of a state change that did not happen. Severity is held at LOW because the authors demonstrably considered and bounded this exact mechanism twice: `token_live` closes the terminal case, and a per-task fixed-window limiter (60 req/60s) caps the non-terminal case -- what remains is the residue those two controls leave.
positive_control: `sed -n '496,534p' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/pushback.rs` shows the `reported == task.state` branch binding `moved = task` unchanged, and the delivery block testing only `push_callback.is_some()` with no reference to whether a transition occurred. `grep -n 'idempot\|dedup\|already_deliver\|last_delivered' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/pushback.rs crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/pushdeliver.rs` returns zero hits, while `grep -rln idempot crates/` matches busbar/src/root/kernel.rs, vocabulary.rs and durability.rs -- proving the vocabulary is one this codebase uses and its absence here is a genuine gap.

category: conditional cleanup -- caller credential retained past its designed lifetime
summary: `forget()` -- the only path that clears a task's entry from the process-local map holding the caller's plaintext webhook delivery credential -- sits after the `?` on the transport send, so a CONNECTION-level transport failure (as opposed to the HTTP-status failure covered by the finding above) on a terminal task's final delivery returns early and the credential is never dropped, contradicting the module's own stated lifetime for that material ('does not survive a restart').
failure_scenario: A caller registers task T with a webhook and a bearer-token delivery credential. T reaches a terminal state; the receiver is unreachable at the socket level (connection refused, TLS failure, timeout), so `seam.transport().send(..)` returns `Err`, propagating `PushRefusal::Transport` before `remember`/`forget` ever run. T's entry stays in the credential map for the remaining lifetime of the process -- a slow retention/growth defect rather than an attacker-drivable one.
positive_control: `forget()` is reachable and genuinely clears both maps on other paths -- called from the push-config delete verb at `local.rs:756`, and `a2a/tests/pushdeliver_tests.rs` asserts the clearing in `a_terminal_delivery_drops_the_credential_as_well_as_the_pin`. That test drives delivery through a `RecordingTransport` whose `send` always returns `Ok`, so it cannot produce a `PushRefusal::Transport` -- the transport-failure-on-terminal-delivery case is unexercised, which is why the gap survives a green suite.

category: observability / diverges from in-crate convention
summary: After the first retention-sweep abandon failure, every subsequent one is entirely silent for the rest of the process's life -- this error-once latch has no `else` branch, unlike three sibling latches in this same crate (`DISPATCH_UNRECORDED_WARNED`, `PUSH_CALLBACK_UNPERSISTED_WARNED`, `STREAM_OUTCOME_UNRECORDED_WARNED`) which keep emitting at debug after the first occurrence.
failure_scenario: During a durable-store outage lasting longer than one sweep tick, the retention sweep's abandon rule fails for many idle tasks per tick. The first failure in the process's life emits one `diag_error`; every failure after that -- across every task, for the rest of the process -- emits nothing at any level. An operator cannot tell from logs whether one task or ten thousand are currently stuck, nor whether the condition is ongoing or resolved.
positive_control: `grep -n -A 6 'DISPATCH_UNRECORDED_WARNED' crates/busbar-a2a/src/a2a/receive.rs` matches receive.rs:2040-2046, which uses the identical `AtomicBool` swap pattern but adds `} else { diag_debug!(...) }`; the same shape appears again at receive.rs:2059-2065 and :2782-2796. Three in-crate siblings keep emitting after the first; `report_abandon_fail` alone has no `else`.

category: version negotiation accepting an incompatible ABI / memory-unsafety at the seam
summary: The 20->21 airlock bump RESIZED an INTERIOR field (BuildCtx.host_ctx, 8 -> 16 bytes) and shifted the four fields after it by 8 bytes, but ABI_MAJOR stayed 1 and check_preamble refuses only magic and MAJOR -- so a dropped-in plane built at any older minor is ACCEPTED and then reads config_ptr/config_len/resolved_refs_* from the wrong offsets.
failure_scenario: PROVEN BY THE GOLDEN'S OWN DIFF. `git show ec21d27f0 -- crates/busbar-plugin/tests/golden/abi-layout.golden` is exactly: `-BuildCtx.config_ptr=32 / -BuildCtx.config_len=40 / -BuildCtx.resolved_refs_ptr=48 / -BuildCtx.resolved_refs_len=56 / -BuildCtx.__size=64` replaced by `+BuildCtx.config_ptr=40 / +config_len=48 / +resolved_refs_ptr=56 / +resolved_refs_len=64 / +__size=72`; the SAME commit's only other change to busbar-plugin/src/lib.rs is `-pub const ABI_MINOR: u32 = 20; +pub const ABI_MINOR: u32 = 21;` and ABI_MAJOR is untouched. crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/decl.rs:74 `pub host_ctx: HostCtx,` sits BEFORE config_ptr, and hot/host.rs:45-57 states the change outright ('the previous `HostCtx = *mut c_void`' becoming a `#[repr(C)]` handle with a u32 generation + u8 kind => 16 bytes at align 8). crates/busbar-plugin/src/lib.rs:30-31 says the rule: 'New fields may ONLY be appended ... Reorder/resize/insert = a MAJOR airlock bump', and the golden gate's own assert message (crates/busbar-plugin/tests/layout_golden.rs:596-597) says 'If it is a REORDER/RESIZE/INSERT, that is a MAJOR airlock break -- do not re-seed without bumping ABI_MAJOR.' It was re-seeded. CONCRETE PATH: an operator drops in a `kind: plane` tarball whose manifest says `abi_version: 20`. sign::validate_structure passes it (registry.rs:89 `"plane" => &[1, busbar_plugin::ABI_MINOR]` = [1,21]). plane.rs:380 check_preamble sees magic OK, major 1 == 1 -> Ok. DynPlane::build (plane.rs:212-223) stamps a 72-byte BuildCtx with config_ptr at offset 40; the minor-20 plane, compiled against the 64-byte layout, reads config_ptr from offset 32 -- which now holds HostCtx's `generation: u32 | kind: u8 | 3 pad` -- and reads config_len from offset 40, which holds the host's REAL config_ptr (a heap address around 2^47). The plane then does slice::from_raw_parts(~0x0000_0001_0000_0005, ~1.4e14) on its config: segfault in the gateway, or an arbitrary-memory read presented to the plane as its config. resolved_refs_ptr/resolved_refs_len (the PRE-RESOLVED SECRET references) are shifted the same way. The sized-struct guard cannot help: read_sized_field! bounds on `size` and the field's offset in THIS build, so it protects appended tails and nothing else. Separately, HostCtx is the by-value first argument of all ~45 PlaneHostVtable slots, so on SysV x86-64 it went from one INTEGER register to two, shifting every subsequent argument of every host callback an older-minor plane makes. REACHABILITY CAVEAT, stated honestly: registry.rs:440 `pub fn open_plane` has no in-tree production caller today (r2 found the same for DynPlane), so this is not yet on a live serving path -- but it IS public API of a published crate, plane-example is loaded through crate::load_plane in-tree, and the breach is of the one contract the crate calls 'FROZEN FOR ALL TIME'.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM (nothing compares the minor): `grep -rn 'abi_minor' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '/tests/'` returns ONLY lib.rs:25 (a doc), :85 (a doc), :97 (the field declaration) and :105 (an assignment) -- no comparison anywhere. POSITIVE CONTROL, identical command shape: `grep -rn 'abi_major' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '/tests/'` returns lib.rs:141 `if peer.abi_major != ABI_MAJOR {` and :144 `theirs: peer.abi_major,` -- a real comparison, proving the command and path are right. Second control: `crates/plugin-loader/src/tests/plane_conformance_tests.rs:540-544` asserts build_status == StatusClass::Ok for a table stamped `abi_minor: ABI_MINOR.saturating_sub(1)` with the message 'an older MINOR is compatible by the sized-struct discipline, never a refusal' -- the behaviour is deliberately pinned by a test, and that test stamps a lower NUMBER on CURRENT-layout bytes, so it cannot see the resize.

category: money / compiled-in fold differs from dropped-in fold
summary: MeteringDelta/MeteringRow gained `priced_from_ms` -- which the engine makes part of the metering ACCRUAL KEY -- with no abi_version bump and no legacy adapter, while supported_abi("store") still admits abi_version 2; a published store plugin has no such column, so it merges a rate-card-split day back into one cell and the whole day is then re-priced at the midnight card.
failure_scenario: crates/busbar-kernel/src/governance/state.rs:893-900 builds the MeterKey as `(key_id, metering_bucket(now), model, provider, priced_from_ms)` where `priced_from_ms = rate_apply::effective_from_at(store::now_ms())`, so a card edit at noon opens a SECOND in-memory cell for the day. The flusher (state.rs:971 `self.store.add_metering(&delta)`) ships both cells across the ABI through the line quoted above -- which, unlike its sibling add_usage at lib.rs:1018, consults NO adapter. A published first-party store plugin (cold/mod.rs:171-172: 'every published first-party store plugin (sqlite/postgres/mysql/valkey, all abi_version: 2)') was compiled against a MeteringDelta that has no priced_from_ms, so serde silently ignores the field and the plugin upserts on the four columns it knows: both halves of the day COALESCE into one row. On read, list_metering returns a MeteringRow whose priced_from_ms is absent and therefore `#[serde(default)]`s to 0 (busbar-contract/src/records.rs:904-905), and crates/busbar-core-admin/src/v1/service_operations.rs:1476 computes `row_priced_at_ms(window.start, r.priced_from_ms)` = `window.start*1000` (service.rs:202), i.e. the card in force at MIDNIGHT. CONCRETE: an operator publishes a corrected rate card effective 12:00. On the compiled-in store (store-memory/src/lib.rs:506-517, which DOES key on priced_from_ms 'so a card edit inside a UTC day opens a SECOND row for that day and each half keeps the card it was earned under (DECISION #79)') the afternoon's tokens price at the new card. On every store this binary can actually load, they price at the morning card -- silently, with no error, no log line and no version refusal. registry.rs:47-52 asserts the opposite in so many words: 'v3 and v4 changed the source contract a plugin is COMPILED against, not a byte on the wire, so a v2 artifact keeps behaving exactly as it did under 1.5.5.' priced_from_ms IS a byte on the wire, and behaving-exactly-as-1.5.5 is now the mis-pricing.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM (no metering adapter exists): `grep -n 'legacy_usage_wire' crates/plugin-loader/src/lib.rs` returns 822 (the definition) and 951/988/1018 -- get_usage, put_usage, add_usage. It does NOT appear in add_metering (1045-1050) or list_metering (1052-1057). POSITIVE CONTROL that the adapter mechanism exists and is reachable: the same grep matching at lib.rs:1018 inside `fn add_usage`, whose own comment at :1019-1021 reads 'THE MONEY PATH on a published 1.5.x store: sending the unit map here is what made the flush fail ... Encode the four priced tiers the way that plugin was built to read them.' Reachability control: `grep -rn 'add_metering' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '/tests/'` matches busbar-kernel/src/governance/state.rs:971 -- a live production caller, unlike the plane kind.

category: ABI field added and never read on the other side
summary: The hook half of the endpoint ABI has a plugin side and no host side: HookRequest::Routes/Endpoint, HookReply::Routes/Endpoint, HookHandler::routes() and HookHandler::handle_http() all exist and the SDK answers them, but DlopenPolicy never emits either op, so a dropped-in hook's declared HTTP routes are collected by nobody.
failure_scenario: cold/endpoint.rs:10-12 names the two motivating cases: '/metrics (a pull exporter's exposition) and a routing hook's /feedback (external -> plugin input) are the SAME shape', and cold/hook.rs:67-69 documents `Routes` as 'asked ONCE at load: which HTTP Routes does this hook serve (a routing hook's inbound /feedback, confined to /hooks/<name>/*)'. crates/busbar-kernel/src/plugin_routes.rs:84-85 even carries the confinement rule as `RouteKind::Hook` ('A `kind: hook` policy (confined to /hooks/<name>/*)'). But crates/plugin-loader/src/hook.rs's DlopenPolicy implements exactly decide/name/transform/configure/describe/status/notify (lines 170-275) and has no routes() and no handle_http(); nothing in the workspace ever constructs HookRequest::Routes or HookRequest::Endpoint. CONCRETE: an operator installs a signed `kind: hook` plugin whose HookHandler::routes() declares `POST /hooks/smart-router/feedback` with `auth: RouteAuth::Key`, and whose handle_http() serves the training feedback the router needs. Every step the ABI documents succeeds on the plugin side and the route is never asked for, never collision-checked, never mounted; every POST to it 404s from the base router's fallback, forever, with no diagnostic naming the plugin -- the hook silently runs as decide-only.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'HookReply::Routes|HookReply::Endpoint|HookRequest::Routes|HookRequest::Endpoint' crates/ conformance/ examples/` matches ONLY two doc lines in cold/hook.rs (:68, :72) and the two SDK dispatch arms (plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:816, :817) -- no host-side emitter. POSITIVE CONTROL, the identical pattern on the sibling kind, same command: `grep -rn 'ExportResponse::Routes|ExportRequest::Endpoint' crates/` matches crates/plugin-loader/src/export.rs:49 (`let req = ExportRequest::Endpoint {`) and export.rs:138 (`Ok(ExportResponse::Routes(r)) => r,`) -- the export kind's host side DOES ask, retains the answer on DynExport.routes, and dispatches through DynExport::handle_http. So the method and the paths are right; the hook half is simply absent.

category: ABI field added and never WRITTEN on the other side
summary: The SDK was changed so SecretRequest::Resolve's `deadline_ms` finally reaches the module via resolve_with_deadline, but the ONLY host-side producer of that request hardcodes None, so the field is still dead -- the fix closed the plugin half of the seam and left the host half exactly as it was.
failure_scenario: crates/plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:610-621 documents the repair in the past tense: 'The old comment described a seam where the module reads it from the request before this dispatch runs: there is no such seam ... dropping it meant a module that CAN bound its own upstream call was never told what bound to apply', and now calls `module.resolve_with_deadline(&settings, deadline_ms)`. But DynSecret -- the one type that builds a SecretRequest::Resolve for a loaded secret plugin -- writes the line quoted above, and DynSecret implements only `resolve` (plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:1439-1457), never resolve_with_deadline, so even a caller that had a deadline could not get it across. CONCRETE: an operator points `secrets.vault` at a HashiCorp Vault plugin and a network partition makes the Vault endpoint accept connections and never answer. The plugin's HTTP client would bound its own call if it were told a deadline; it is told None on every call, so it blocks its caller for the client's own default (commonly 30s or none). Boot secret resolution stalls with nothing in the log naming a deadline, and the busbar-api doc that promises the bound (crates/api/src/secret.rs:103-113) describes a capability that no busbar build can exercise.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'resolve_with_deadline' crates/ --include='*.rs'` returns exactly five sites -- plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:620 (the plugin-side call), plugin-sdk/src/tests/lib_tests.rs:127, api/src/secret.rs:114 (the defaulted trait method), and api/tests/mutation_hardening_secret_contract.rs:92-109. Zero host-side callers. POSITIVE CONTROL, same command shape on a method that IS called from the host: `grep -rn 'deadline_ms' crates/ --include='*.rs'` matches plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:1445 -- so the grep does reach the loader and does find the field; it is only ever `None` there.

category: ABI declared universal, implemented on one kind
summary: The #85 observability envelope is documented as 'the ONE response shape, every kind' and the host decoder is genuinely kind-neutral, but drain_observations exists only on ExportHandler -- the other four cold kinds' SDK dispatchers return the bare response and have no trait method on which a plugin could report anything at all.
failure_scenario: cold/observe.rs:15-19 states the mandate: 'One kind having a back-channel and another not is exactly the divergence DECISIONS #3 bans: a plugin is a plugin -- two universal rules, identical for every kind', and cold/export.rs:50-52 asserts 'the envelope TYPE and the host seam that folds it are kind-NEUTRAL and already carry every kind'. The host half is real (plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:361-366 and :374-381 fold an Envelope for ANY Resp, and busbar-kernel/src/metrics.rs:751 installs the kernel observer at boot). The PRODUCER half is not: store_dispatch (plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:250-263), auth_dispatch (:352-363), secret_dispatch (:632-662) and hook_dispatch (:827-838) all serialize the kind's bare response; only export_dispatch (:977-988) goes through dispatch_export_enveloped. CONCRETE: an author writes a `kind: store` plugin whose Postgres pool sheds a connection and whose WAL write is refused. Both are facts an operator must see. The plugin can neither report a counter nor raise a catalogued BUSBAR-NNNN diagnostic, because busbar_api::Store has no drain_observations; its only channel is busbar_set_log_sink, which observe.rs:289-296 explicitly says is 'a LOG, and it is not this'. The one kind that CAN fill the envelope is the export kind, which r2 already showed has no production caller -- so the whole #85 back-channel reaches nothing on any deployment this binary can produce.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'drain_observations|into_envelope|Observations' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '/tests/' | grep -v 'cold/observe.rs'` matches only crates/export-example-plugin/src/lib.rs:53-58, plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:860/915/967, and one busbar-kernel doc comment -- every one on the export kind. POSITIVE CONTROL that the host half genuinely is kind-neutral and reachable (so the absence is on the plugin side, not mine): `grep -rn 'observe::fold' crates/plugin-loader/src/` matches lib.rs:364 and lib.rs:379 inside `fn decode_response<Resp: DeserializeOwned>` -- a generic used by store, secret, auth, hook and export alike; and `grep -rn 'install_plugin_observer' crates/` matches busbar-kernel/src/observe.rs:241, called unconditionally from metrics.rs:751.

category: vtable slots with no host-side reader / compiled-in fold differs from dropped-in fold
summary: DynPlane has slot readers for config_validate, build, hydrate, start and dispatch and NONE for admin_routes or openapi, so the two PlaneDecl slots the ABI reserved for a plane's admin and OpenAPI contribution -- and attached a documented 'non-vacuity invariant' to -- are read by nothing, while the compiled-in native decl's equivalents ARE called.
failure_scenario: crates/busbar-plugin/src/hot/decl.rs:170-173 declares `pub admin_routes: Option<AdminRoutesFn>` ('Contribute admin routes (non-vacuous if present)') and `pub openapi: Option<OpenApiFn>`, and decl.rs:102-103 states the invariant: the fn 'MUST be NON-VACUOUS if the plane declares any admin surface'. plugin-loader/src/plane.rs:149-166 is the complete set of slot readers and stops at slot_dispatch; `grep -n 'admin_routes' crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs` is empty. The compiled-in half is wired: crates/busbar-core-admin/src/v1/json/mod.rs:292 does `if let Some(admin_routes) = decl.admin_routes {` and handlers.rs:3922 does `if let Some(openapi) = decl.openapi {`, over the NATIVE Rust PlaneDecl that busbar-a2a (a2a/mod.rs:155-156, `admin_routes: Some(admin_routes)`, `openapi: Some(openapi_fragment)`) and busbar-mcp (mcp/mod.rs:163-164) fill. CONCRETE: the a2a plane, which today contributes both an admin route set and an OpenAPI fragment when compiled in, is instead shipped as a signed `kind: plane` cdylib. It loads, builds, starts and dispatches -- and contributes neither. The admin endpoints its operators use 404, and the published OpenAPI document silently omits its paths, with no diagnostic anywhere, because the host never asks. This is narrower than r2's 'two unrelated PlaneDecl types with no adapter' finding and survives it: even if that adapter were written, these two slots would still have no reader on the repr(C) side.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'admin_routes' crates/plugin-loader/src/ crates/busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/` returns nothing; same for `openapi`. POSITIVE CONTROL, same command, same directory: `grep -rn 'provided_carriers' crates/plugin-loader/src/plane.rs` matches :75, :107, :136-137, :142, :387-389 and :403-405 -- another PlaneDecl field that the loader genuinely does read through read_sized_field!, proving the file and the method are right. Second control that the slots are read for the OTHER fold: `grep -rn '\.openapi\b' crates/` matches busbar-core-admin/src/v1/json/handlers.rs:3922.

quote: //! | `busbar_set_log_sink` (installs a `tracing` dispatcher INSIDE the plugin) | per load | yes |
category: compiled-in fold differs from dropped-in fold / diagnostics lost at the seam
summary: The host log bridge is installed for the five cold kinds and for no plane: export_plane! emits no busbar_set_log_sink symbol and wire_up_plane never looks one up, so a dropped-in plane's entire tracing output is discarded -- the exact defect the bridge was written to close, left open on the one kind that serves the data plane.
failure_scenario: wire_up_raw installs the sink at plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:636-663 ('Installed BEFORE `open`, deliberately: a constructor is exactly where a plugin has something worth reporting'), and cold/mod.rs:231-237 gives the motive ('every tracing::warn! inside a loaded plugin was therefore discarded -- including auth-oidc's on a FAILED TOKEN SIGNATURE VERIFICATION'). wire_up_plane (plugin-loader/src/plane.rs:325-419) does the transport handshake, the kind check, the decl pointer and the preamble, and never touches symbol::SET_LOG_SINK; export_plane! (plugin-sdk/src/lib.rs:1204-1230) emits only busbar_abi, busbar_plugin_kind and busbar_plane_decl, so hostlog::install -- and with it install_tracing_bridge -- is never called in a plane cdylib. CONCRETE: an a2a or mcp plane built with export_plane! is dropped in and its egress starts refusing an upstream TLS handshake. Compiled in, that `tracing::error!` lands in the operator's subscriber with the plugin attributed and goes out over OTLP. Dropped in, the plane's statically-linked tracing-core has no dispatcher at all (the SDK's Forwarder is installed only from hostlog::install), so the record is constructed and thrown away -- the operator sees requests failing and nothing saying why. The line quoted above is the loader's own table asserting this crossing happens 'per load'; for the plane kind it happens never.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'intern_log_ctx|host_log_sink|busbar_set_log_sink' crates/plugin-loader/src/ | grep -v 'src/hostlog.rs'` returns lib.rs:657, lib.rs:660, ffi_thread.rs:58 (this doc line) and plane.rs:428 (a doc reference to host_log_sink's cap, not a call). No install site in plane.rs. POSITIVE CONTROL, the same grep landing on a real install: plugin-loader/src/lib.rs:657 `let ctx = hostlog::intern_log_ctx(&display);` and :660 `sink(hostlog::host_log_sink, ctx, level);`, inside wire_up_raw -- so the symbol name and the crate path are right and the cold path does install it.

category: ABI safety helper never read on the other side
summary: safe_relay_status and both its wrappers (EndpointResponse::safe_status, HttpResponse::safe_status) have zero production callers; the one real relay clamps with StatusCode::from_u16(..).unwrap_or(BAD_GATEWAY), which accepts 100..=999 where the ABI helper accepts only 100..=599, so a plugin-chosen status of 700-999 is relayed verbatim to an external client.
failure_scenario: endpoint.rs:141-143 calls this 'THE conversion a host relay must use instead of StatusCode::from_u16(self.status).unwrap()', and cold/auth.rs:259-267 duplicates it on HttpResponse for the login hop. The one relay that actually exists, busbar-kernel/src/plugin_routes.rs:563, is `let status = StatusCode::from_u16(resp.status).unwrap_or(StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);`. That closes the panic but not the range: http's from_u16 accepts 100..=999. CONCRETE: a buggy export sink answers an inbound /metrics scrape with `status: 700`. relay_response builds a response with status 700 and hands it to axum; the external scraper receives `HTTP/1.1 700` -- a status no client vocabulary defines, so Prometheus classes the scrape as an unknown failure rather than the 502 'the plugin misbehaved' the ABI helper was written to produce. The helper that would have mapped it sits unused two crates away.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'safe_relay_status|safe_status' crates/ --include='*.rs'` matches only cold/tests/endpoint_tests.rs:81/90/92/96, cold/auth.rs:260/265-266 (the wrapper defining itself), and the definition here -- no caller in busbar-kernel, busbar-core-admin or plugin-loader. POSITIVE CONTROL, same command shape over the same consumers: `grep -rn 'EndpointResponse' crates/ --include='*.rs'` matches busbar-kernel/src/plugin_routes.rs:37 and plugin-loader/src/export.rs:48 -- the type IS consumed by the host, so the grep reaches the relay; only the helper is not.

category: ABI field added and never read on the other side
summary: The `version` field every hot POD struct leads with is STAMPED in about forty places and COMPARED in zero, so POD_VERSION's own 2->3 bump signals nothing to any receiver -- the same inert state PlaneHostVtable.size was in before ::check was written.
failure_scenario: busbar-plugin/src/lib.rs:73-74 records the bump ('19->20 (1.6.0 M1): the append-only hot::Usage keyed-unit tail (units_ptr/units_len), paired with POD_VERSION 2->3'), and hot/mod.rs:20-22 states the discipline as 'every cross-boundary POD struct here LEADS with a size: u32 and a version: u16'. Every use is a write: plane.rs:214 `version: POD_VERSION`, workitem.rs:172, pod.rs:800/841/949/985/1025, and ~25 more in busbar-kernel/src/plane_host/*. Nothing anywhere reads a RECEIVED version and branches on it, so a peer cannot distinguish a POD_VERSION 2 sender from a 3 sender except through `size`, which the read_sized_field! guard already uses -- leaving `version` as two bytes of the frozen header that mean nothing. CONCRETE: the next POD change that is genuinely NOT expressible as a size delta (a reinterpretation of an existing field's units, say -- exactly the kind of change a version field exists for) will be shipped with a POD_VERSION bump and will be invisible to every receiver, because no code path can see it. hot/host.rs:800-801 has the precedent verbatim: `size` 'was written at construction (EMPTY/STUB) and, until this existed, was never read by anything: the field the guard was written for was inert.' The same is true of `version` today, and of AbiPreamble.abi_minor.
positive_control: ZERO-CLAIM: `grep -rn 'POD_VERSION' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '/tests/'` returns 45 lines; every one is a `use`, a doc, the definition, or `version: POD_VERSION` on a struct literal -- there is no `== POD_VERSION`, no `!=`, no `<`, no match. POSITIVE CONTROL that a comparison of this shape WOULD be found by this method: the same grep style over the sibling axis, `grep -rn 'TRANSPORT_VERSION' crates/plugin-loader/src/`, matches lib.rs:582 `if transport != TRANSPORT_VERSION {` and plane.rs:337 `if transport != busbar_plugin::cold::TRANSPORT_VERSION {` -- real comparisons, so the pattern and paths are right.

category: auth-design/unreachable-feature
summary: The OAuth AS plane's consent screen (`GET`/`POST {issuer}/consent`) is gated `RouteAuth::Admin`, which busbar's admin chain satisfies ONLY via an `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-Admin-Token` HTTP header (crates/busbar-kernel/src/auth/mod.rs:1499-1508, :862-868), never a cookie, query param, or WWW-Authenticate-triggered browser prompt -- so an ordinary browser following the 302 redirect that `oauth-as` itself issues from `/authorize` (the only documented way to reach `/consent`) can never present the credential, making the login/consent flow unreachable in any deployment that runs a real (non-empty) `admin_auth:` chain.
failure_scenario: An operator configures `oauth_as:` (busbar as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP clients, per busbar-oauth2/src/lib.rs's module doc) with a normal, non-empty `admin_auth: [admin-tokens]` chain -- the only posture the code itself treats as production rather than the documented 'OPEN posture (dev)' (`admin_auth: []`). An MCP client's system browser opens `GET {issuer}/authorize?...`; `oauth-as` finds no session cookie, calls `consent::approval_resolver`, and 302s to `{issuer}/consent?return=...` (busbar-oauth2/src/consent.rs). The browser follows this as an ordinary top-level GET -- it carries cookies and nothing else; it cannot attach a custom header. `run_admin_chain` (per consent.rs's own doc: 'the credential is checked by auth::run_admin_chain -- the same code, the same providers... before the handler runs') extracts the admin credential ONLY from `Authorization`/`X-Admin-Token`, finds neither, and the request is denied with a plain 401 JSON body carrying NO `WWW-Authenticate` header (crates/busbar-kernel/src/auth/mod.rs:1287-1298, `admin_unauthorized_response()`) -- so no browser-native credential prompt fires either, and `extract_bearer_token` (mod.rs:643-650) only recognizes the `Bearer` scheme, not `Basic`, ruling out a browser-native Basic-auth workaround too. The operator can never approve a client; an advertised, carefully-engineered 1.6.0 feature (registration policy, CIMD, ES256 signing, one-shot approval spend) cannot be completed by its own intended actor in any deployment that actually authenticates its admin surface -- forcing a choice between a working OAuth login screen and an authenticated admin surface on the same process.
positive_control: `grep -n "serve_with_admin_chain(" crates/busbar-oauth2/src/tests/flow_tests.rs` returns the definition, a default `serve()` wrapper calling it with `Vec::new()` (the OPEN dev posture), and exactly one call with a non-empty chain -- inside `an_unauthenticated_visitor_is_never_shown_the_consent_screen`, which asserts a 401/403 for the GET, i.e. a REFUSAL, not a successful approval. No test in the crate drives a successful authorize->consent->approve flow under a populated admin chain, because none can. `grep -n "COOKIE\|query" crates/busbar-kernel/src/auth/mod.rs` returns zero hits in the admin-chain extraction path, confirming no alternate carrier exists.

category: admin-patch-unbounded-numeric / hot-path-panic
summary: `limits.upstream_request_timeout_secs` is validated only for a floor (`< 1`, config_validate/mod.rs:1251) with NO ceiling, and reaches a raw, panicking `tokio::time::Instant + Duration` add on the LLM engine's per-attempt hot path (`crates/busbar-llm/src/engine/attempt/send.rs:66-67`, `tokio::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(client_settings.upstream_request_timeout_secs.max(1))`) -- the same overflow class as round 2's confirmed `pool_idle_timeout_secs` bug, but on the request-serving path rather than a background reaper. NOTE ON REACHABILITY: `crates/busbar-llm/src/engine/build_runtime.rs:333` (`let reuse_prior_client = prior_rt.is_some_and(|pr| pr.client_settings == input.client_settings);` ... `else { ...rebuild... }`) rebuilds the upstream client -- and therefore refreshes `client_settings` -- whenever this field changes, and `put_config_settings` (handlers.rs:2956-3070) does call `busbar_kernel::build_app_from_config` ('exactly the reload mechanism'), which is the pipeline that reaches `build_runtime`. This conflicts with this SAME file's own adjacent comment three lines above (`handlers.rs:2726-2729`), which asserts these three `LimitsPatch` fields are boot-frozen and 'a PUT that touches them changes the STORED config but not the live `reqwest::Client`' -- an internal documentation/code inconsistency I could not fully resolve without deeper tracing outside this crate's slice. What is certain regardless of which claim is right: the field is unbounded, the sink panics, and it is reachable at minimum via `POST /config/apply` / `POST /config/reload` (both confirmed to invoke the identical `build_app_from_config` -> LLM `build_runtime` path) or a config.yaml edit plus restart -- and quite plausibly via a live `PUT /config/settings` as well.
failure_scenario: An admin sends a config change (via `PUT /config/settings`, or `POST /config/apply`/`config/reload` if the PUT path turns out to be genuinely boot-frozen) setting `limits.upstream_request_timeout_secs` to a value >= ~2^63 (e.g. `18446744073709551615`). Once the LLM plane's `NativeRuntime` is rebuilt with this value (immediately on apply/reload per the confirmed `build_runtime` reuse-vs-rebuild logic, or on the next restart at the latest), every subsequent STREAMING LLM request calls `send::deadline(&hop)` (attempt/mod.rs:165), which computes `Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(...)`; `tokio::time::Instant`'s `Add<Duration>` (tokio 1.53.1, src/time/instant.rs:165-171) delegates to plain `std::time::Instant + Duration`, i.e. `self.checked_add(other).expect("overflow when adding duration to instant")`, which panics -- unlike `tokio::time::sleep`/`timeout`, which use `checked_add` with a `far_future()` fallback and do NOT panic. The panic unwinds the request-handling task; with no panic-catching layer anywhere in the workspace (round 2's own finding), every streaming call fails from that point until the value is reverted and the runtime rebuilt again -- a config-PATCH-triggered denial of service on the gateway's primary, money-generating function.
positive_control: `grep -n "upstream_request_timeout_secs" crates/busbar-kernel/src/config_validate/mod.rs` shows exactly one guard (`< 1`, line 1251) -- no ceiling -- in contrast to `request_body_max_bytes` in the SAME file, which has both a floor (line ~1305) AND a ceiling (line ~1312) check, proving the codebase does ceiling-bound fields it considers dangerous and did not do so here. `grep -n "Instant::now() + " crates/busbar-llm/src/engine/attempt/send.rs crates/busbar-llm/src/engine/health.rs crates/busbar-kernel/src/export/webhook.rs` matches all three sites reported in this file, confirming the identical unguarded-add pattern recurs in three independent subsystems.

category: admin-patch-unbounded-numeric / delayed-panic / silent-availability-loss
summary: `health.default_probe_timeout_secs`/`default_probe_interval_secs` are validated only with a floor (`< 1`, config_validate/mod.rs:1343-1347) -- next to a comment at mod.rs:1320 stating 'the pool-idle, gauge-limit, and probe defaults are all safe at any value' (true only for the zero case the comment is actually discussing, not for an overflow) -- and reach the identical raw, panicking `Instant + Duration` add via `probe_lane` (health.rs:385). CORRECTED REACHABILITY: `reload_to_apply_fields` (handlers.rs:2695-2701, `health: _,`) classifies the WHOLE `health:` section as live, but `spawn_probers` (health.rs:137) -- the only code that turns these defaults into a running prober's captured `timeout`/`interval` (health.rs:158-165, captured OUTSIDE the per-lane `tokio::spawn`, never re-read inside its loop) -- has exactly one production call site, `crates/busbar/src/main.rs:1343`, at boot only. So a live PATCH does NOT reach an already-running prober; the false 'live' classification means the operator is never told a restart is required, and the danger is a DELAYED FUSE: every lane using the process-wide default crashes its prober task on its first tick after the NEXT restart (for any reason) that happens to occur while the poisoned value is durably stored in the overlay.
failure_scenario: An admin `PUT /api/v1/admin/config/settings {"health":{"default_probe_timeout_secs": 18446744073709551615}}`. The request succeeds, is durably persisted to the overlay, and the response's `reload_to_apply` list does not name `health` (it is bound wholesale to `_`, unlike `limits`'s field-by-field destructure) -- so the operator has no signal that anything is pending. Nothing crashes yet, because the currently-running probers already captured the OLD, safe default at the last boot. Later -- a deploy, a crash-and-supervisor-restart, or an admin-triggered `POST /restart` for any unrelated reason -- the process restarts, `main.rs:1343` calls `spawn_probers` fresh, and every lane with no per-lane `timeout_secs` override captures the poisoned default and panics the first time `probe_lane` runs (health.rs:385, 'overflow when adding duration to instant'). With no panic-catching layer anywhere in the workspace, that lane's per-lane `tokio::spawn`ed prober task is gone for good; for `HealthMode::Dead` lanes (the mode that re-probes a breaker-tripped/HardDown lane, health.rs's `host.lane_store().lane_needs_probe(...)` arm), this is the ONLY recovery mechanism, so any lane that later trips can never self-recover again -- only ANOTHER restart re-spawns probers, with no operator-visible signal beyond a one-line panic on stderr at the moment it happened, potentially long after the triggering PATCH.
positive_control: `grep -rn "spawn_probers" crates/ --include="*.rs"` (excluding tests) returns exactly one production call site (`crates/busbar/src/main.rs:1343`) versus the definition at `health.rs:137` -- no call from `appbuild.rs` or from any `config/apply`/`config/reload`/`plugins/reload` handler, confirming the boot-only capture. `grep -n "default_probe_timeout_secs must be\|probe defaults are all safe at any value" crates/busbar-kernel/src/config_validate/mod.rs` shows only the floor check and the (overflow-blind) safety comment.

category: admin-patch-unbounded-numeric / falsely-live / money-durability-window
summary: `advanced.usage_flush_interval_ms` has zero validation anywhere (no floor, no ceiling -- unlike its `AdvancedPatch` sibling `rate_sweep_interval`, which IS floor-checked), AND is misclassified as 'GENUINELY LIVE' by `reload_to_apply_fields` (handlers.rs:2810, `usage_flush_interval_ms: _,`) when `spawn_budget_flusher` (governance/mod.rs:1226-1230) captures it into a local `interval` exactly ONCE, before its `tokio::spawn`ed loop, and is itself called exactly once at process boot (`crates/busbar/src/main.rs:1493-1499`, whose own comment states 'Spawned once here (not on config apply/reload...)'). The combination is a DELAYED-FUSE, unbounded widening of the durable governance-spend loss window on an ungraceful crash -- squarely inside the project's 'money is sacred' invariant (a lost flush is a lost/undercounted charge).
failure_scenario: An admin `PUT /api/v1/admin/config/settings {"advanced":{"usage_flush_interval_ms": 18446744073709551615}}` -- expecting, per the field's own doc comment ('at most this many ms of accrued spend/requests can be lost' on an ungraceful crash), to TIGHTEN the durability window, or accidentally fat-fingering an extra zero. The response reports success with no restart-required signal (the field is bound `_`, not individually pushed like `limits.pool_idle_timeout_secs`).
