category: money-correctness
summary: A successful (non-error) `systemone` decision response whose `/usage/units` field is missing, fractional, negative, or otherwise fails `u64` text parsing is billed as nothing at all — not zero, no line at all — because `meter()` only emits a usage locator when `FACT_USAGE_UNITS` happens to be set.
failure_scenario: The provider `api.typesafe.ai` answers `POST /v1/systemone` with 200 and a body carrying no `/error` member but an absent, non-numeric, or fractional `/usage/units` (e.g. the field is omitted on one response shape, or the provider reports `7.5` units the way the project's own owner-signed decision #81 says a provider CAN report a fractional count — 'output_tokens: 27.5' is the exact cited example for another plane). `codec::read_u64` (crates/busbar-plane-decision/src/codec/mod.rs:106-109) does `core::str::from_utf8(raw).ok()?.parse::<u64>().ok()`, which returns `None` for `7.5`, a negative number, a string, or an absent pointer. `decode_response` (plane.rs:281-285) then simply never calls `facts.set(FACT_USAGE_UNITS, ..)` — it does not set a zero, it sets nothing. `meter()` (plane.rs:393-415) checks `r.facts.get(FACT_HAS_ERROR)` is not `true` (it is not, this is a 200) and then only pushes a `UsageLocator` `if let Some(FactValue::Int(units)) = r.facts.get(FACT_USAGE_UNITS)`; since the fact was never set, this is `None`, so `locators` returns EMPTY. The decision plane's `route()` still opened the leg to the provider and money was presumably owed to/consumed from the upstream provider account, but busbar's kernel receives zero usage lines for this exchange, i.e. the request is served as a free success. This also collides with the project's own ruling #42 ('a value that will not fit the declared scale EXACTLY is a REFUSAL, never a rounded guess') and #81 (a fractional measurement must be preserved exactly, never dropped) — here it is silently discarded and the exchange is billed as if it never carried usage at all, on the sole reference implementation of this plane kind.
positive_control: The crate's own test suites (crates/busbar-plane-decision/tests/jev.rs:118 `billable_success_metering_surface_reports_usage_on_success_and_nothing_on_error`, tests/conformance.rs:88/112, src/tests/codec.rs:13) only assert two cases: a success WITH a valid integer usage count, and a 422 WITH no usage member at all. `grep -n usage crates/busbar-plane-decision/tests/*.rs crates/busbar-plane-decision/src/tests/*.rs` finds no fixture combining `finish=Complete`/no `/error` with a missing or fractional `/usage/units`, confirming this exact branch is untested as well as unhandled.

quote: r.id == id && matches!(r.disposition, PlaneDisposition::Active) && now <= expires_at
category: reference-plugin-drift / abi-boundary-inconsistency
summary: The two in-tree reference `Store` implementations disagree at the exact expiry instant for `plane_token_live` (the multi-use push-notification capability check): `store-memory` treats `now == expires_at` as EXPIRED, `store-example-plugin`'s durable `FileStore` treats the identical input as LIVE — and each crate's own test suite locks in its own answer, so nothing catches the drift.
failure_scenario: A push-notification callback for a task arrives at the exact second its capability token's `expires_at` is reached (a realistic boundary — timers and epoch-second granularity make `now == expires_at` a routine, not exotic, occurrence). Against the DEFAULT backend (`busbar-store-memory`, crates/store-memory/src/lib.rs:893, `now < expires_at`), `plane_token_live` returns `false` and the callback is refused. Against the reference `store-example-plugin` configured in durable mode (crates/store-example-plugin/src/lib.rs:571-577 `push_config_live`, `now <= expires_at`), the byte-identical call returns `true` and the callback is honoured for a token the other reference implementation already considers dead. Because this crate is explicitly documented as the copy-me template for third-party `kind: store` plugins (crate doc: 'the copy-me template for kind: store'), a third party who copies FileStore's boundary condition ships a store that is measurably more permissive than the shipped default at the one-second edge of every capability window, silently. Each side is deliberately tested to its own answer: crates/store-memory/src/tests/lib_tests.rs:921 asserts `plane_token_live("task","t1",1000,1000)` is false, while crates/store-example-plugin/src/tests/mod.rs:651 asserts `plane_token_live("push_config","t-1",100,100)` is true — proving the divergence is real and currently green in CI on both sides.
positive_control: Both quoted call sites and both quoted test assertions were read directly from the pinned tree at the line numbers given; `grep -n 'plane_token_live' crates/store-memory/src/lib.rs crates/store-example-plugin/src/lib.rs` returns exactly these two comparison operators as the full set of `plane_token_live`-family boundary checks in the slice, so this is not a partial reading — it is the whole of this verb's boundary logic in-tree.

category: architecture / retirement-risk
summary: `crates/api` (`busbar-api`) is documented as the legacy pre-#35 plugin-contract surface being retired, but it is still directly depended on by 20 other crates (not just third-party-shaped plugins) — including the core engine (`busbar-kernel`) and the shipped binary (`busbar`) itself — and its re-exported types sit directly on the live money path (the `MoneyBook` seam) and the live admin-auth path (the operator admin-token comparison), not only on plugin-compat shims.
failure_scenario: `grep -rl busbar-api --include Cargo.toml crates/` lists 21 crates naming it (20 besides `api` itself), including `busbar-kernel` and `busbar` (the served binary). Concretely: `crates/busbar/src/root/money_book.rs:44` — the 1.6.0 `MoneyBook` pass-through seam that is explicitly the future single point the W3 ledger fold will route billing through — imports `AuditRecord, MeteringRow, UsageDelta, UsageLedger` from `busbar_api` (not `busbar_contract` directly). `crates/busbar/src/root/auth_bindings.rs:197,287` — the operator admin-token `AuthModule` (`AdminTokens::authenticate`, the real credential comparison gating `/admin/v1/*`) calls `busbar_api::sha256_hex` and `busbar_api::constant_time_eq` directly, not a busbar-contract or busbar-kernel-identity spelling. `crates/busbar/src/root/units_a2a.rs:222` types its A2A task-store handle as `Arc<dyn busbar_api::Store>`. `crates/busbar-kernel/src/metrics.rs:413-416` and `cost.rs` read `busbar_api::UNIT_INPUT/UNIT_OUTPUT/UNIT_CACHE_READ/UNIT_CACHE_WRITE` for cost/metering. None of this is broken today — `busbar-api`'s own doc (crates/api/src/store.rs:21, 'busbar-api does NOT retire yet (that is W5.b)') says the shim is deliberate and byte-identical — but the retirement plan (#35/W5.b) as framed to this audit ('the legacy surface that #35 retires') undersells how embedded it still is: it is not only a plugin-facing compatibility alias, it is the spelling the core engine's OWN money and admin-auth code currently uses, so W5.b cannot simply delete third-party-facing re-exports without also touching busbar-kernel/busbar internals that never went through a plugin boundary at all.
positive_control: `grep -rl busbar-api --include=Cargo.toml crates/ | wc -l` returns 21 (including crates/api itself); every quoted call site above was read directly at the given file:line in the pinned tree.

category: a money column asserted against a constant 0 that is 0 on both sides by construction
summary: The one integration test that drives the shipped binary pins the served ledger view's fee-count column at 0 for every row, and it can only pass because BOTH sides of the node's own reconciliation identity hard-code that column to zero -- so `reconcile`'s `l.fee_count == g.billable_requests` is `0 == 0` on every row of every live node, forever.
failure_scenario: On the shipped binary, `NodeLedger::rows_of` (crates/busbar/src/root/units_admin/mod.rs:475-500) never assigns `entry.fee_count`, so every LedgerRow keeps `LedgerRow::default()`'s 0; and `legacy_rows_under_lock` (same file, line 537) writes `billable_requests: 0,` literally. `ledger_identity::reconcile` (crates/busbar/src/root/ledger_identity.rs:225) continues the row when `spend.holds() && l.fee_count == g.billable_requests`, so the fee-count half of the identity compares 0 to 0 on every row and can never report a discrepancy. The derivation that WOULD populate `fee_count` -- `derived_totals_rows`, units_admin/mod.rs:1427-1480 -- is unreachable on a real node, because both `LedgerView::booked_lines` impls return `Vec::new()` (the default at mod.rs:342-344 and BoundLedger's at mod.rs:602-604), so `totals_rows` always takes the `view.ledger_rows()` fallback. Concretely, with the test's own fixture -- 4 delivered responses, FEE_CENTS=3 -- `GET /api/v1/admin/ledger/totals` serves rows whose `priced_micros` demonstrably contains 4x30,000 micro-units of flat fee (the test asserts served_micros == 2_530_000 per response at line 494, which includes the fee) beside `"fee_count":0`, and `GET /api/v1/admin/ledger/reconciliation` answers `holds: true` over a column that structurally cannot disagree. An operator reconciling 'how many flat fees did this node charge' is told zero while being billed for four. The file's own doc at lines 121-124 names exactly this hazard -- 'with no fee the `sum fee_count == billable_requests` half of the identity is `0 == 0` on every row and would pass with the fee line unimplemented on either side' -- and then line 476 asserts precisely that value on the served half. The test is also the wrong way round as a gate: wiring `booked_lines` (the stated 1.6.0 landing) would make `fee_count` non-zero and turn this assertion RED, so the test now blocks the fix it was written to await.
positive_control: The RECONSTRUCTED half of the same test does assert a non-zero fee count under the identical method -- `crates/busbar/tests/ledger_identity.rs:378-383`: `let fee_total: u64 = ledger.values().map(|r| r.fee_count).sum(); assert_eq!(fee_total, total_requests, "one flat fee per billable request, and no other");` -- proving both that the column is assertable and that the test knows the right value is `requests`, not 0. Zero-claim controls: `grep -n 'fee_count' crates/busbar/src/root/units_admin/mod.rs` returns 1478 (the derivation, unreachable) and 1514-1515 (the renderer) and no assignment in `rows_of`; `grep -rn 'fn booked_lines' crates` returns exactly three impls -- mod.rs:342, mod.rs:602 (both `Vec::new()`) and units_admin/tests/units_admin.rs:3880 (a TEST double that DOES return lines, which is why the derivation is exercised by unit tests and by nothing on a real node).

category: source-scanning instrument that sees under half the sites it claims to enumerate
summary: The scan the file calls 'the only way a reason becomes a refusal' matches 57 of the 100 production `Refusal::new(` occurrences in crates/; the other 43 -- including nine in the composition root's own kernel.rs and every site that passes the reason in a variable -- are invisible, so 'OverdraftCeiling and StaleSlice are refusal reasons nothing refuses with' is asserted over a partial census.
failure_scenario: Measured by re-implementing the file's own scanner (same directory walk, same tests/target exclusions, same whitespace normalisation, same marker) over the pinned tree: 757 production files, 100 occurrences of `Refusal::new(`, 57 matched by the marker, 43 invisible. Classified: 23 are busbar-core-admin's different two-argument `Refusal::new(RefusalStep::.., ReasonCode::..)` type (governance.rs 1, mint.rs 4, posture.rs 7, refusal.rs 1, verbs.rs 10); 11 are the SAME busbar_contract::caps::Refusal built with a fully-qualified path -- crates/busbar/src/root/kernel.rs lines 1108, 1118, 1128, 1144, 1160, 1178, 1194, 1211, 1251 and crates/busbar-llm/src/unit/walk.rs 587 and 607; 9 pass the reason as a value -- crates/busbar-kernel-budget/src/lib.rs:370 `let refusal = Refusal::new(reason);` (the BUDGET gate, the one crate a money refusal would be minted in), crates/busbar-kernel-egress/src/trust/unit.rs:56, crates/busbar-llm/src/unit/verify.rs:361, crates/busbar/src/root/units_a2a.rs:994, units_admin/mod.rs:2399 and :2422, units_mcp.rs:263, units_voice.rs:1584 and :1670. So a mid-unit money end added tomorrow as `Decision::refuse(token, Refusal::new(reason))` where `reason` resolves to `ReasonCode::OverdraftCeiling` -- the exact shape units_voice.rs:1584 already ships -- leaves this test green, and the design binding it is the sole gate for ('an ADMITTED http/sse unit is never ended for money', file doc lines 6-11) is broken with no instrument that can say so. Nothing is live-wrong today: none of the 43 invisible sites currently carries a money reason. The defect is the instrument, whose whole premise (doc line 20: 'Refusal::new(ReasonCode::...) -- the only way a reason becomes a refusal') is false for 43% of the sites.

Cross-check by grep: `grep -rn 'Refusal::new(' crates --include='*.rs' | grep -v '/tests/' | grep -v '_tests.rs' | grep -v 'Refusal::new(ReasonCode::' | grep -v 'Refusal::new(busbar_contract::caps::ReasonCode::'` lists the variable-carrying sites named above.

category: mutation-hardening cell that does not kill the mutant it was written for
summary: `a_surrogate_pairs_second_escape_needs_both_the_backslash_and_the_u` exists to pin the `||` in next_json_char's low-surrogate guard against becoming `&&`, and returns `Resolved::Missing` under BOTH the correct code and that mutation, because a key that decodes to a different character and a key that fails to decode are the same answer to this pointer.
failure_scenario: crates/busbar-contract/src/json_grammar.rs:464 is `if raw.get(*at) != Some(&b'\\') || raw.get(*at + 1) != Some(&b'u') { return Decoded::Malformed; }`. The test's body is `{"\uD800\xDC00":1}` queried at pointer `/x`. Correct (`||`): the second escape's letter is `x`, so the guard fires, `next_json_char` returns `Decoded::Malformed`, `key_eq` (json_grammar.rs:409-421) hits its `_ => return false` arm, the member does not match and `resolve_pointer` answers `Resolved::Missing`. Mutated to `&&`: the first clause is false (the backslash IS there), so the guard does not fire; `hex4` then reads `DC00`, `(0xDC00..0xE000).contains(&0xDC00)` is true, and the pair combines to U+10000 -- a Decoded::Char. `key_eq` compares U+10000 against the token character 'x', they differ, it returns false, and `resolve_pointer` answers `Resolved::Missing` again. Identical value, so the assertion at line 129-132 cannot go red on the mutation, and no other test in the tree reaches that guard. Shipped consequence if the guard is ever weakened: `next_json_char` accepts a malformed second escape as a real character, so the raw keys `\uD800\xDC00` and `\uD800\uDC00` resolve as the same key. `resolve_pointer` is the JSON-pointer resolver the metering locator uses (busbar_contract::caps::QuantitySource::Locator { ptr: LocatorPtr }) to read token counts out of an upstream response body, so two distinct upstream keys collapsing into one is a locator silently reading another field's number as the billed quantity.
positive_control: The sibling cells in the same file DO discriminate, under the identical method: `a_lone_garbage_byte_is_malformed_not_an_empty_number` (mutation_hardening.rs:58-60) asserts `Resolved::Malformed`, a value the correct code produces and the mutant would not; `a_same_length_impostor_literal_is_malformed` (line 156-158) does the same for `literal`. That both of those assert Malformed and this one asserts Missing is the whole difference: Missing is what `resolve_pointer` answers for ANY non-matching key, for any reason, so it carries no information about which arm produced it.

category: fixture feeds the input, nothing reads the output
summary: `usage_ledger_applies_deltas_and_floors_at_zero`, whose doc says 'negative deltas floor every counter at 0', drives billable_requests through +2, +1 and -10 and never once asserts `l.billable_requests` -- and no test anywhere in the tree asserts that counter after a negative delta.
failure_scenario: crates/busbar-contract/src/records.rs:765-767 applies the delta with `self.billable_requests = self.billable_requests.saturating_add_signed(delta.billable_requests);`. Change that one call to `wrapping_add_signed` (leave `requests` on line 764 saturating) and this test still passes: it asserts `l.requests` at lines 468 and 502 and the per-model tiers at 502-504, and never touches `billable_requests`. Shipped: after two billable requests and a -10 over-refund the counter wraps to 18,446,744,073,709,551,609. records.rs documents this field as the flat-fee base that budget SPEND derives from, so one over-refund fabricates ~1.8e19 units of flat-fee spend for that (bucket, window) -- which either bills the customer for it or permanently exhausts their budget cap.

Zero-claim classification: `grep -rn 'billable_requests' crates --include='*.rs' | grep assert` returns 6 hits -- busbar-kernel-budget/src/tests/ported.rs:896, api/src/tests/usage_migration_tests.rs:30, plugin-loader/src/tests/legacy_usage_tests.rs:120 and :188, busbar-kernel/src/governance/tests/tests.rs:1017, busbar/src/root/units_admin/tests/units_admin.rs:2290 -- every one of them a positive accumulation or a JSON field echo, none after a negative delta. `grep -rn 'billable_requests: -' crates --include='*.rs'` returns exactly two construction sites (records_tests.rs:496 and store-memory/src/tests/lib_tests.rs:113) and neither asserts the result.

category: name promises a comparison the body never makes
summary: `an_export_access_is_recorded_the_same_way_a_hook_access_is` never records a hook access to compare against -- it checks the amendment class and that the hex digest is 64 characters -- and `Reader::Export`'s digested word is pinned nowhere in the crate.
failure_scenario: Change crates/busbar-kernel-audit/src/amend.rs:75 from `Reader::Export => "export",` to `Reader::Export => "hook",`. This test stays green (class is still AmendClass::Access, the hex is still 64 chars); `an_access_records_who_read_what_and_never_what_they_read` asserts the enum value `a.reader == Reader::Hook`, not the string; and `the_sealed_digest_of_an_amendment_is_the_frozen_hex` builds its fixture from Reader::Hook, so the frozen hex does not move. Shipped: `AmendChain::digest_of` seals the reader through `a.reader.as_str()`, so an export-plugin content disclosure and an in-process hook read now seal to the SAME digest. The amendment chain is the node's record of who read a customer's content on its way off the box; 'an export plugin shipped this prompt to a third-party sink' and 'a hook read it in-process' become one indistinguishable entry, and a stored export access can be substituted with a hook access and still verify.
positive_control: `grep -rn '"export"' crates/busbar-kernel-audit/` returns exactly one line -- amend.rs:75, the definition itself -- so nothing pins it. The identical command over the sibling vocabulary proves the method and the path: `grep -rn '"adjust"' crates/busbar-kernel-audit/` returns two lines, amend.rs:50 (the definition) AND amend_tests.rs:367 (`assert_eq!(AmendClass::Adjust.as_str(), "adjust");`). One vocabulary is pinned, the other is not, under the same search.

quote: /// `busbar_kernel::admin::v1::contract::required_scope` it claims to port, each asserted against
category: doc promises a cross-check the body never performs; two live authorization matrices, no instrument comparing them
summary: `the_scope_matrix_matches_the_enforced_one_verbatim` says its three cases are 'each asserted against the behaviour of the axum::http::Method-backed original', but the body only ever calls the port, `admin_required_scope`, against hard-coded `Scope::` literals -- the enforced matrix is never invoked, so the two matrices are never actually compared.
failure_scenario: Both matrices gate real admin requests: crates/busbar-kernel/src/auth/mod.rs calls `crate::admin::v1::contract::required_scope` for the HTTP admin door, while crates/busbar/src/root/units_admin/mod.rs and .../admin_mount.rs call `busbar_kernel_scope::admin_required_scope`. Add a row to one and not the other -- e.g. a third entry in `READ_ONLY_POST_PATHS` (crates/busbar-kernel-scope/src/lib.rs) with no mirror in crates/busbar-kernel/src/admin/v1/contract/mod.rs -- and this test stays green, because every one of its assertions compares `admin_required_scope(..)` to a literal it also wrote. The two doors then disagree about the scope a given operation requires: a read-only admin token is refused on one leg and admitted on the other for the same path, which is exactly the 'second matrix with a second opinion' that busbar-kernel-scope/src/lib.rs's own doc says a ported table may not be.

quote: // Whitespace-normalised, so a construction rustfmt broke across four lines reads the same
category: comment states the opposite of what the code does

category: contains() where the exact bytes and their order were the point (operator signature over a rate-card amendment)
summary: The only test that inspects the operator-signed rate-amendment payload says in its own comment that every signed field is 'still there, in order', and then checks each field with an unordered `contains` of the bare `key=` prefix -- so the payload's order and four of its five field VALUES have no witness anywhere in the tree.

category: instrument-cannot-produce-a-no / money invariant unenforceable
summary: The two-sided canary's identity `drafts == holds + accruals == settlements` is arithmetically unsatisfiable for every zero-hold admission and every refusal, because the loop increments `drafts` four steps before the door and `settled` for units that opened neither a hold nor an accrual.
failure_scenario: busbar-contract/src/caps/canary.rs:10 states the identity: '//! > drafts accepted == holds opened + accruals into a parent == settlements', checked at canary.rs:95 `if c.drafts == opened && opened == c.settlements {`. In teller.rs the three counters move as follows. (a) teller.rs:856 `run.canary.draft_accepted();` runs AFTER decode and BEFORE authenticate -- four steps before the door -- although canary.rs:60 documents the method as '/// A draft got through the door.' (b) `hold_opened()` runs only on the `Admission::Own` arm (teller.rs:790) and `accrual_taken()` only on `Admission::Accrual` (teller.rs:780); the `Admission::ZeroHold` arm quoted above increments NEITHER. (c) teller.rs:1364 `run.canary.settled();` runs for every unit whose cell take succeeded -- which includes every ZeroHold unit and every refused unit, because the in-flight table puts an arrival hold in the cell at inflight.rs:513 `cell: HoldCell::new(request.arrival),`. CONCRETE, ON A DEFAULT DEPLOYMENT: busbar-kernel-budget/src/lib.rs:320-324 returns `Admission::ZeroHold` whenever the door prices the unit at zero nano-units (`if nanos == 0 {`), and busbar-kernel/src/rate_apply.rs:25-26 says 'an ABSENT card prices every class at nothing' -- so on a deployment with no rate card configured EVERY admitted request is a ZeroHold. One such request leaves drafts=1, holds=0, accruals=0, settlements=1, and `Canary::balanced()` returns `Err`. A unit refused at Verify does the same (drafts=1, settlements=1); a unit refused at Arrival or Decode inverts it (drafts=0, settlements=1, because `draft_accepted` never ran but `exit` still took the arrival hold and settled). The ONE arithmetic proof the design has that no unit went missing therefore can never be wired into a running node: it would fire on the first handshake, the first unpriced request and the first refusal. The battery only asserts `balanced()` over runs made entirely of `Admission::Own` units (loop_battery.rs:361-374) plus one accrual child (loop_battery.rs:441-443); the two tests that DO exercise the broken shapes assert only one side each -- loop_battery.rs:187-191 asserts `canary.counts().holds == 0` for a challenge round and loop_battery.rs:275 asserts `settlements == 1` for each refusal -- so no test can see the break.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' '\.balanced()' crates/` matches ONLY test files: busbar-contract/src/caps/tests/mod.rs:{754,759,771}, caps/tests/what_the_record_reads.rs:142, busbar-kernel/tests/table_and_pump.rs:{885,891,897,903}, busbar-kernel/tests/loop_battery.rs:{373,443,699} -- 11 test sites, 0 production, 0 doc-comment. The identical grep form `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'run_unit' crates/busbar/src` DOES match production (harness.rs:126, transports.rs:522, units_admin/admin_mount.rs:122), proving the method reaches production code. `Admission::ZeroHold` producer classification: 3 production (busbar/src/root/units_voice.rs:1586, units_admin/mod.rs:2283, busbar-kernel-budget/src/lib.rs:323), 1 gauntlet harness (gauntlet_kernel.rs:166), 5 test, 1 doc-comment (caps/decision.rs:15).

category: money arithmetic differs from its twin
summary: The sweep's settle and the recovery settle both build a `Posted` WITHOUT first applying the accrual to the hold, so an overdraft they settle is posted as zero while the same unit through the exit path posts it in full.
failure_scenario: The exit path's twin runs one extra line before it settles: teller.rs:1323 `let _spend = hold.spend(run.meter.total(), run.meter.headroom());`. `Hold::spend` (busbar-contract/src/caps/hold.rs:239) is the only thing that calls `record_overdraft`, so it is the only thing that can make `hold.overdraft()` non-zero. `Posted::settle` reads that field directly and sets the OVERDRAFT FLAG from a SEPARATE comparison (`if overdraft > 0 || settled > reserved {`). Neither tick.rs:275-326 nor recovery.rs:69-108 calls `Hold::spend` at all, and `Hold::materialize` starts the hold at `overdraft: 0` (hold.rs:183). CONCRETE: a unit whose door reserved 100 nano-units runs up an accrual floor of 400 and its task disappears. Through `teller::exit` with zero headroom, `hold.spend(400, 0)` records an unbacked 300 and the posting carries `overdraft = 300`. Through `tick::sweep_settle` the settlement table returns the same `amount = 400` (the not-completed / nothing-located row at teller.rs:396), but the posting carries `overdraft = 0` WITH the OVERDRAFT flag set -- a posting that says, in its own two figures, 'overdrawn by nothing'. The money then moves wrong twice downstream: busbar-kernel-ledger/src/settle.rs:223 `figures.overdraft_carried_out = figures.overdraft_carried_out.saturating_add(overdraft);` adds 0 instead of 300, and busbar/src/root/durability.rs:312 `let overdraft = settlement.overdraft.as_ref().map(|note| Posting {` produces `None` (settle.rs:239 gates it on `overdraft > 0`), so the second journal record durability.rs:249-252 promises -- 'A unit that ran past everything reservable leaves two records, not one ... so the carry into the next window can be read off the chain' -- is never written. busbar-contract/src/slice.rs:693-695 states what that carry is for: 'the excess is carried into the next window, which is what makes it impossible to escape a cap by overrunning it.' Recovery has the identical shape at recovery.rs:99-104 whenever a crashed unit's last checkpoint exceeded what the door reserved. STATED SO IT CAN BE CHALLENGED: both settle sites currently have zero production callers (the sweep half being unwired is already confirmed), so this is latent -- but it is a divergence in the code, not the wiring, and it is invisible to every test because the batteries drive both paths with reservations that cover the amount.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' '\.spend(' crates/ | grep -v '/tests/\|_tests\.rs'` returns 3 Hold-spend production sites -- busbar-kernel/src/teller.rs:1323, busbar-kernel-budget/src/lib.rs:271, busbar-contract/src/caps/hold.rs:502 (the child-accrual arm) -- and ZERO in tick.rs or recovery.rs. The same grep form DOES match the sibling exit path, proving it reaches this kind of call site. `grep -rn 'Posted::settle(' crates/ | grep -v tests` gives the full production settle set: teller.rs:1344, tick.rs:320, recovery.rs:99 -- 3 production, 2 doc-comment (caps/hold.rs:29, caps/unit_end.rs:29), the rest tests.

category: prose asserts a guarantee the code does not hold / resource retired with no re-creation path
summary: `AppHandle::swap`'s doc says it re-spawns the health probers on every swap and that doing it there makes it impossible to forget; the body retires the host the probers hold a Weak to and delegates the re-spawn to a `PlaneDecl::on_swap` hook that the plane owning the probers does not implement -- so the first admin mutation kills active health probing for the life of the process.
failure_scenario: state.rs:943-948 claims: '/// hook/auth mutation). Re-spawns the health probers against `next`: probers hold a `Weak<App>` and /// exit once the App they were spawned against drops, so EVERY swap must re-attach them -- /// otherwise the first admin mutation replaces the boot App, the boot App drops as in-flight requests /// drain, its probers exit, and active/dead health probing silently STOPS ... /// Doing it in `swap` itself makes it impossible for a future swap site to forget.' The body does not re-spawn: the comment above the quoted line (state.rs:1001-1003) says 'RE-SPAWNING the probers against `next` is the fallback plane's own concern (its `PlaneDecl::on_swap` seam)', and `set_snapshot_host` (state.rs:924-926) REPLACES the Option, dropping the outgoing generation's host -- which main.rs:1465-1470 confirms is 'the only strong reference the boot probers depend on'. The plane that owns the probers declares no hook: busbar-llm/src/lib.rs:263 `on_swap: None,`. CONCRETE: boot with `health: {mode: active}` on a lane, then issue ANY admin mutation (`PATCH /api/v1/admin/hooks/x`, `POST /api/v1/admin/config/reload`, any of the hook/auth mutation swaps) -- all funnel through `swap`. Within one probe interval every prober's upgrade fails at busbar-llm/src/engine/health.rs:221 `let Some(host) = weak.upgrade() else {` and returns, logging only `tracing::debug!(... "health prober exiting: host snapshot replaced by reload")`. From that moment, for the rest of the process's life, no lane is actively probed and a `HealthMode::Dead` lane is never re-probed out of a tripped breaker (health.rs:230 `HealthMode::Dead => host.lane_store().lane_needs_probe(i, now()),` is never reached), so capacity is silently and permanently lost. busbar-llm/src/lib.rs:290 asserts the opposite in the plane's own words: 'the admin swap path re-attaches probers to each new generation.'
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'spawn_probers' crates/` returns exactly ONE production call site -- crates/busbar/src/main.rs:1343 `busbar_llm::spawn_probers(&boot_host);`, boot only -- with the rest classified as: 1 definition (health.rs:137), 1 re-export (busbar-llm/src/lib.rs:291), 4 doc/comment mentions (lib.rs:288, state.rs:1003, health.rs:67, health_tests.rs:425/459) and 6 test call sites (health_tests.rs:451, 532, 546, 618, 639). `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'on_swap: Some' crates/` returns exactly ONE hit in the whole tree: busbar-mcp/src/mcp/mod.rs:180 (the MCP plane, which retires stdio children, not probers). The identical grep form for the negative case, `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'on_swap: None' crates/`, returns 14 hits (5 production decls including busbar-llm/src/lib.rs:263, 9 test/fixture), proving the grep matches this field when it is present. `swap` itself is live: state.rs:987-994 iterates `plane_decls()` and calls each `on_swap`, so the delegation mechanism exists -- it is simply not implemented by the plane that needs it.

category: prose asserts a guarantee the code does not hold / money view divergence
summary: The sweep and recovery hard-code the kernel's own meter class while the exit path honours `Evidence.class`, so the same unit's usage line lands on a different meter depending on which of its two ends settled it -- and the constant's own doc says all three post against the same class.
failure_scenario: teller.rs:343-345 claims, in so many words: '/// Spelled ONCE. The exit path, the sweep and the recovery path all post the same figure against /// the same class, and three string literals for one class is three places a typo can put a /// settled unit on a meter nobody prices.' But the exit path does not post against that class when the plane named one: teller.rs:1324 `let class = evidence.class.unwrap_or(KERNEL_ACCRUAL_CLASS);`. `Evidence.class` is documented at teller.rs:333 as 'Which class the settled amount is reported against' and IS set on production paths: busbar/src/root/units_mcp.rs:1353 `class: Some(CLASS_BYTES),` and units_a2a.rs:1671 `class: Some(CLASS_BYTES),`. CONCRETE: an MCP unit that relayed 12,000 bytes has its exit-path usage line written as `{class: bytes, quantity: 12000}`. If the sweep settles the same unit instead (task lost mid-relay), tick.rs:303-308 writes the line under `nano_units`, and recovery.rs:85-93 does the same for a crash-recovered unit. Money is a VIEW computed as ledger x ratecard; a rate card keyed by meter class prices `bytes` and `nano_units` differently, or does not price `nano_units` at all -- so identical consumption is billed two ways, decided by which end of the unit happened to run, and the disputes report attributes bytes relayed to the kernel's own accrual meter.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'evidence.class\|\.class\.unwrap_or' crates/` matches exactly two sites: busbar-kernel/src/teller.rs:1324 (the single production read) and busbar/src/root/tests/units_voice.rs:1618 (a test asserting the plane still declares it) -- so the field has ONE production reader and it is in the exit path only. The identical grep form on the producer side, `grep -rn 'class: Some(' crates/busbar/src | grep -v /tests/`, matches units_mcp.rs:1353 and units_a2a.rs:1671, proving the method finds both halves.

category: money: a charge skipped on one branch and not its sibling
summary: All three `Close` arms of the session tick drop the checkpoint AND the outstanding priced interval, reintroducing on the close path exactly the defect the tree's own regression test says was fixed on the accrue path.
failure_scenario: `session_tick` decides `revoked` (tick.rs:83), `budget_dry` (the quoted line) and `idle_for >= SESSION_IDLE_MAX_MS` (tick.rs:91) BEFORE it reaches the priced-seconds branch at tick.rs:95, and each returns `SessionTick::Close { reason }` -- a variant with no `checkpoint` field and no `elapsed` field (tick.rs:63-67). Two things are dropped. (1) The checkpoint: `accrued_changed` is discarded, although tick.rs:58-61 states the rule the Accrue variant was built to hold -- 'Pricing an interval and recording the running figure are two jobs and not two branches: a session that does the first still owes the second, and the checkpoint is what a crash pays out on.' The tree's own test doc says what that costs, at busbar-kernel/tests/recovery_and_ticks.rs:766-768: 'Deciding them as one if/else meant a priced session NEVER checkpointed, so its journal record carried a checkpoint of zero -- and recovery, which posts the last checkpointed figure, posted nothing for a session that had been billing all along.' (2) The priced interval: the seconds since the last SETTLED tick are never accrued, although tick.rs:11-12 promises the opposite for this exact arm -- '//! that has gone quiet, and one whose budget has run dry -- priced seconds are never accrued //! unmetered.' CONCRETE: `session_tick(60_000, 60_000, 0, Some(4_200), true, true, false)` returns `Close { OverBudget }`; the 4,200 nano-units accrued since the last checkpoint are dropped so a crash before the session's own settle pays out on a stale checkpoint (recovery.rs:81 posts `record.checkpointed`), and the 60 seconds of priced session time since the last settled tick are never priced. The pinned test cannot see either loss because it passes `since_settled = 0` and `accrued_changed = None` on every Close case (recovery_and_ticks.rs:806, :812, :818). NOTE: `session_tick` has no production caller today, so this is latent.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'session_tick' crates/` matches only busbar-kernel/src/tick.rs (the definition) and busbar-kernel/tests/recovery_and_ticks.rs:{19,719,722,727,732,742,752,771,806,812,818} -- 0 production callers, 11 test sites, 0 doc-comments; `grep -rn 'SessionTick' crates/` outside tick.rs matches only that same test file. The identical grep form applied to a kernel function that IS wired -- `grep -rn 'run_unit' crates/busbar/src` -- matches harness.rs:126, transports.rs:522 and units_admin/admin_mount.rs:122.

category: an instrument that cannot produce a NO / dead branch on a money path
summary: The in-flight table's provider reserve -- which the module doc calls money -- is unreachable: its enabling input `provider_of_open_session` is never set to `true` anywhere in the tree, `reserve_for` has no production caller, and every production construction passes a literal reserve of 0.
failure_scenario: inflight.rs:12-13 says 'It is also the node's admission control on itself ... Two details matter and both are money', and names the first at inflight.rs:15-16: '//! - A share of the table is RESERVED for provider frames of sessions that are already open. A node //!   under load should shed new arrivals, not the paying conversation it is already having.' The branch that implements it is inflight.rs:434-435 (`} else if request.provider_of_open_session {` / the quoted `Some(self.cap)`), which widens the ceiling from `cap - reserve` to the whole table. Neither half is ever supplied. `Enter.provider_of_open_session` (inflight.rs:378) is `false` at all 19 construction sites in the tree and `true` at NONE, so the quoted branch is dead everywhere, production and test alike. `reserve_for` (inflight.rs:57), the only function that computes the 10% share from `RESERVE_PERCENT` (inflight.rs:52), has no production caller; every production `InFlight::new` passes the literal `0`: busbar/src/root/units_llm.rs:335 `inflight: busbar_kernel::inflight::InFlight::new(usize::MAX, 0),`, units_admin/admin_mount.rs:44 `InFlight::new(0, 0)`, gauntlet_kernel.rs:296 and :397. CONCRETE: on the only production data listener the table is opened at `usize::MAX` with reserve 0, so `ceiling()` (inflight.rs:431-439) returns `Some(usize::MAX)` for a brand-new client arrival AND for a provider frame of a paying open session, and `admits()` is `len() < usize::MAX` -- always true. A node under load sheds nothing, and when a deployment does bound the table a provider frame of the paying conversation is measured against exactly the ceiling a brand-new arrival is. The sibling exemption `zero_hold_tick` (inflight.rs:380), which inflight.rs:17-18 calls out as 'The heartbeat sweep never occupies a slot at all. A node whose table is full still runs the thing that empties it', is set to `true` at exactly ONE site in the whole tree and it is a test (busbar-kernel/tests/table_and_pump.rs:94 `tick.zero_hold_tick = true;`).
positive_control: COUNTS, CLASSIFIED. `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'provider_of_open_session: true' crates/` returns ZERO hits; `grep -rn 'provider_of_open_session: false' crates/ | wc -l` returns 19 (production: units_llm.rs:534, units_admin/admin_mount.rs:99, gauntlet_kernel.rs:{331,430}; the other 15 are test files). `grep -rn 'zero_hold_tick' crates/` returns 22 hits: 2 in inflight.rs, 1 test assignment to `true` (table_and_pump.rs:94), 19 assignments to `false`; production `true`: 0. `grep -rn 'reserve_for(' crates/` matches only inflight.rs:57 (the definition) and 8 lines of table_and_pump.rs -- 0 production callers. The identical grep form `grep -rn 'InFlight::new' crates/ | grep -v tests` DOES match four production construction sites in the very same files, so the zero is an absence, not a blind spot.

quote: //! the ONE place an admin mutation is recorded, and it feeds that mutation onto the store-backed
category: a second writer to something documented as single-writer
summary: `AuditLog::record_by` is documented twice as the ONE place an admin mutation is recorded, but a second production path -- `JournalHost::audit_emit` -- reaches the same durable admin chain from 27 plane call sites without entering `record_by`, the in-process ring, or `record_by`'s `&'static str` outcome constraint.
failure_scenario: The claim is made at the quoted line and repeated verbatim in the code at audit_ring.rs:290-291 ('`record_by` is the ONE place an admin mutation is recorded, so this ONE call ... is the durable write'). The second path is plane_host/mod.rs:706-710: `fn audit_emit(&self, action: &str, resource: &str, outcome: &str, principal: &str) { ... crate::plane::auditlog::emit_admin_hostless_now(action, resource, outcome, principal); }` -- a direct forward to the same durable seam that `record_by` feeds at audit_ring.rs:295, skipping the ring entirely. The same file knows both exist: plane_host/mod.rs:714 calls `record_by` 'the superset of `audit_emit`'s durable-only path'. TWO CONSEQUENCES, both concrete. (1) The outcome type is constrained on one path and not the other: `record_by`'s signature is audit_ring.rs:253 `pub fn record_by(&self, action: &str, resource: &str, outcome: &'static str, principal: &str)` -- a `&'static str` that in practice can only be a `crate::audit::vocab` constant -- while the trait at plane_host/mod.rs:2739 declares `fn audit_emit(&self, action: &str, resource: &str, outcome: &str, principal: &str);`, an unconstrained runtime string. `AuditEntry::outcome`'s doc at audit_ring.rs:58-59 publishes 'Stable outcome token: `applied` ... | `rejected` ...' as the admin API's own schema description (the struct carries `#[cfg_attr(feature = "openapi-schema", derive(schemars::JsonSchema))]`), so a plane passing any other string writes a value the published schema says cannot occur, with no type or runtime check to stop it. (2) The 27 plane sites never enter the in-process ring `crate::audit_ring::AUDIT`, which plane_host/mod.rs:715 says 'The egress audit-and-allow trail reads', so any control added at the documented chokepoint -- an outcome-vocabulary check, a resource redactor, a principal normaliser -- is silently not applied to them.
positive_control: COUNTS, CLASSIFIED. `grep -rn --include='*.rs' '\.audit_emit(' crates/` returns 27 hits, ALL production plane code and none under a tests path: busbar-a2a/src/a2a/receive.rs x9 (:1216,1233,1342,1429,1476,1533,1691,1716,2093), busbar-a2a/src/a2a/route.rs:297, busbar-mcp/src/mcp/tasks.rs:694, busbar-mcp/src/mcp/method.rs x16. Production sites: 27. Test sites: 0 (the one fixture, busbar-voice/src/testkit/fixture_host.rs:412, is an `impl`, not a call). category: a cleanup/restore path that runs on one branch and not its sibling / lost data
summary: Restore seeds the per-principal chain position from the DECODABLE records only, so a principal whose tail rows will not decode has its chain reopened below the store's real tail -- the forked log the same file and its journal both name as the one outcome to avoid.
failure_scenario: calllog.rs:591-608 decodes each stored body, pushing only the successes into `bodies` and counting failures into `out.unreadable` (reported per row at `diag_error!(PLANE_CALLLOG_ROW_UNREADABLE, ...)`, calllog.rs:597). The consequence is named as forbidden twice in this tree. calllog.rs:829-831: 'Chain positions are NOT reset. A purge removes the oldest records; reopening the chain at seq 1 afterwards would make every subsequent record collide with a sequence the store may still hold, which is the one thing the append contract calls a forked log.' audit/journal.rs:363-365: 'Never call it on a scope that may still be appended to -- reopening it would resume from the store tail (with a sink) or FORK at seq 1 (without one).' The next call for `p` appends a SECOND row at seq 4 into a store that still holds the old seq 4 and 5 -- two chains under one principal, neither describing what happened. WORSE SUB-CASE: if ALL of `p`'s rows are undecodable, `bodies` is empty, the position is committed as an empty chain (`next_seq = 1`) and is now cached so no resume can correct it -- and because `store_returned_nothing` is computed as `raw.is_empty()` at calllog.rs:578 and `raw` was NOT empty, the loud `PLANE_CALLLOG_EMPTY_CHAIN` error that exists for precisely 'the chain is being reopened at seq 1' (calllog.rs:617-623) does not fire. category: a resource minted with no release path
summary: One-shot permits are taken inside `dispatch` with no production release, no `#[must_use]` handle and no `Drop` -- unlike the nested-pool permit in the same file -- and exhaustion answers `Wait` on a frame that has nothing left to read, so the frame is neither served, refused, dropped nor counted.

Its release, `finish_one_shot` (pump.rs:164), has no production caller. Contrast the sibling in the same file: `NestedPermit` (pump.rs:265-273) is `#[must_use = "a permit that is never given back shrinks the pool for good"]` and is paired with `leave`. The module doc's rule at pump.rs:17-18 -- '**One-shots do not take the slot.** They run under a small fixed concurrency, so a burst of them cannot starve the open conversation or the node' -- depends on a give-back nothing performs. The exhaustion answer compounds it: `Dispatch::Wait` is documented at pump.rs:71 as 'Nothing yet: keep reading', but a `Shape::OneShot` frame is by definition a whole unit -- there is nothing more to read. It is not `Refuse` (the occupied-slot answer) and not `Drop` (which the enum says is counted into the window's aggregate), so the frame is neither answered nor counted; and because pump.rs:182-184 already called `Scheduler::made_progress(session)` for this shape, the consecutive-`NeedMore` run is reset and the `ReasonCode::Stalled` ceiling at pump.rs:189-193 can never fire for it either. CONCRETE once wired: after the fixed one-shot concurrency is reached in the process lifetime, the counter never returns to 0, `start_one_shot()` returns `false` forever, and every subsequent one-shot request is silently dropped -- no unit opened, no refusal rendered, no aggregate incremented, no stall detected, nothing metered, and the connection hangs. positive_control: Not a zero-claim: `sed -n '243,258p' crates/busbar-kernel/src/state.rs` shows the two doc blocks running contiguously into `pub hook_env` at :255 and the undocumented `pub hook_registry` at :256.

category: a resource minted with no release path / unbounded growth
summary: The per-thread telemetry bank registry is append-only with no removal path, and banked emission is reachable from tokio blocking-pool threads, so a gateway doing bursty large cross-protocol requests retains one ThreadBank per reaped blocking thread for the process lifetime and pays O(threads-that-ever-emitted) on every flush.
failure_scenario: `BANK` is a `thread_local!` created on first emission, and the quoted line pushes a second `Arc` into `registry().threads` -- telemetry.rs:765 `threads: Mutex<Vec<Arc<ThreadBank>>>,`. The retention is deliberate and the reason is sound (telemetry.rs:675-677: 'the registry keeps a second `Arc` so the aggregator can keep summing a dead thread's final totals (counters are cumulative -- dropping a dead thread's cells would make the exposed totals REGRESS, which Prometheus rejects)'), but nothing ever folds a dead thread's totals into a base and drops the bank, so the vector only grows. THE REACHABILITY IS THE POINT: banked emission is not confined to the fixed thread-per-core workers. `telemetry::translation` (telemetry.rs:381) is a banked `CounterSlot`; it is reached through plane_host/mod.rs:696-698 `fn telemetry_translation(&self, from: &str, to: &str) { crate::telemetry::translation(from, to); }` from busbar-llm/src/engine/wire.rs:456 `host.telemetry_translation(ingress_protocol, egress_name);`, which sits inside `translate_request_cross_protocol` -- and busbar-llm/src/engine/attempt/assemble.rs:167-181 runs exactly that function on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` for any body at or above `TRANSLATE_OFFLOAD_THRESHOLD`. Tokio reaps idle blocking threads and spawns fresh ones on the next burst. CONCRETE: a gateway serving bursty large cross-protocol requests creates a new blocking thread per burst; each one that emits allocates an `Arc<ThreadBank>` (the struct plus its lazily-allocated atomic counter chunk, and a histogram chunk if it records one) that is never released, and `flush_to_recorder` (telemetry.rs:925-953) clones the whole vector and iterates EVERY retained bank for EVERY registered slot -- so both resident memory and the per-flush cost grow monotonically with the number of threads that have ever emitted, on a timer rather than only on scrape.
positive_control: `grep -nE '\.retain\(|\.remove\(|\.clear\(\)|\.pop\(\)|\.drain\(' crates/busbar-kernel/src/telemetry.rs` returns NO matches -- there is no removal path of any shape in the file. Positive control under the identical command form: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' '\.retain(' crates/busbar-kernel/src` matches six sibling sites (ratelimit.rs:227, auth_cache.rs:177, auth_cache.rs:212, config/overlay.rs:294, :311, :380), proving the method finds pruning when it exists. The emit chain is four direct reads, each quoted above from the pinned tree.

quote: /// plane's v1.5.4-identical series); the mounted planes emit their own `busbar_plane_*`
category: an instrument that cannot produce a NO
summary: `busbar_plane_request_duration_seconds` can never receive a sample for the voice plane: the voice front door emits the counter itself and marks the response Counted, and the marker makes the core boundary skip `request_finished`, which is the only production caller of the duration recorder.
failure_scenario: The quoted line and telemetry.rs:114 promise that 'the mounted planes emit their own `busbar_plane_*` families from `request_finished` instead'. One mounted plane emits half of that pair and stands the boundary down for the other half. busbar-voice/src/mount.rs:794-805 `fn finish(...)` increments `PLANE_REQUESTS_TOTAL` with `"plane" => "voice"` directly and then does `resp.extensions_mut().insert(Counted);`. busbar-kernel/src/plane/observe.rs:141-143 reads that marker and returns before the emit: `if resp.extensions().get::<Counted>().is_some() { return resp; }`, so busbar-kernel/src/plane/observe.rs:144 `crate::telemetry::request_finished(` never runs for a voice front-door response. `record_plane_request_duration` (metrics.rs:267) has exactly ONE production caller -- telemetry.rs:294, inside `request_finished` -- so the histogram half is emitted nowhere for this plane. CONCRETE: every voice front-door response that passes through `finish()` increments `busbar_plane_requests_total{plane="voice"}` while `busbar_plane_request_duration_seconds{plane="voice"}` has ZERO series. A `histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) by (plane)` panel renders nothing for voice, and a p99-latency alert scoped to the voice plane can never fire -- the plane reads as healthy because its latency instrument does not exist, not because it is fast.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'record_plane_request_duration|PLANE_REQUEST_DURATION' crates/` (extended-regex form) returns one production caller (telemetry.rs:294), the definition and constant (metrics.rs:267, :829), three doc/emit-site mentions inside metrics.rs, and two test references (busbar-kernel/tests/plane_integration.rs:512, :518). `grep -rn 'histogram!' crates/busbar-voice/src` returns ZERO hits; positive control under the identical command form, `grep -rn 'counter!' crates/busbar-voice/src`, matches busbar-voice/src/mount.rs:796 plus the plane's own metrics test harness -- so the plane demonstrably emits metrics macros and demonstrably emits no histogram.

quote: /// `GovCtx`) means "all pools", so those callers see the full topology exactly as before: this
category: prose that inverts a frozen fail-closed guarantee
summary: `/stats`'s doc says an empty allowed-scopes list means "all pools"; the frozen governance primitive says an explicit empty list is NO scopes at all and names the opposite reading as fail-open. The code is correct; only the doc points the wrong way.
failure_scenario: endpoints.rs:24-26 reads '/// An empty `allowed_pools` (or `key: None` ...) means "all pools", so those callers see the full topology exactly as before'. busbar-contract/src/records.rs:389 states the frozen semantics: '/// - an explicit EMPTY list is NO scopes at all (never "all").' and records.rs:398-401 names the doc's reading by name: 'The alternative reading -- an unlisted kind is "unconstrained", therefore allowed -- is fail-OPEN ... Pinned by `scope_allowed_cross_kind_is_fail_closed` because these semantics ship in 1.5.3 and freeze with it: only an OMITTED list is a wildcard.' The implementation in endpoints.rs agrees with the primitive, not with its own header: endpoints.rs:37 `let restricted = gov.key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.allowed_scopes.is_some());` and its inline comment at endpoints.rs:35-36 ('an explicit list (even empty) restricts'). CONCRETE: a maintainer reconciling the header with the body 'fixes' the body to match line 25 -- turning a key minted with an explicit empty scope list, which today sees nothing, into a wildcard over the deployment's entire topology (pools, lanes, providers and models) on the one endpoint an operator uses to read that topology. The header also still names `allowed_pools`, a field the struct now calls `allowed_scopes`, so the two sentences do not even describe the same field.
positive_control: Not a zero-claim: both halves are direct reads of the pinned tree -- `sed -n '22,40p' crates/busbar-kernel/src/endpoints.rs` for the header and the implementation, `sed -n '385,412p' crates/busbar-contract/src/records.rs` for `scope_allowed`'s frozen doc and its `None => true, Some(list) => list.iter().any(...)` body.

category: a success line emitted on the failure branch
summary: The "OTLP tracing enabled" info line is gated on the endpoint being configured, not on a provider having been installed, so it is printed verbatim after the exporter failed to build and no spans will ever be exported.
failure_scenario: The quoted line sits under `if let Some(endpoint) = otlp_endpoint {` (observability.rs:481) -- a test that the operator supplied a syntactically valid endpoint, nothing more. The provider is built separately at observability.rs:457 `let otel = otlp_endpoint.and_then(build_otlp);`, and `build_otlp` has a failure arm that prints and returns `None` (observability.rs:811: `eprintln!("busbar: OTLP exporter init failed ({e}); continuing with stderr logging"); return None;`). When that arm is taken, `otel_provider` is `None`, no global tracer is set, and the quoted line still runs. CONCRETE: an operator points `otlp_endpoint` at a `url::Url`-valid endpoint the OTLP SDK's builder rejects. stderr then carries BOTH `busbar: OTLP exporter init failed (...)` and `INFO OTLP tracing enabled`. Anyone verifying a tracing rollout the way rollouts are verified -- grepping the boot log for the enabled line, or asserting on it in a smoke test -- concludes traces are flowing while zero spans are ever exported, and the one line that says otherwise is an unstructured `eprintln!` rather than a `tracing` event, so it is absent from any structured log sink the deployment ships.
positive_control: Not a zero-claim: `sed -n '455,460p;478,490p;805,815p' crates/busbar-kernel/src/observability.rs` shows the three regions -- the `and_then(build_otlp)` build at :457, the endpoint-gated info line at :481-485, and `build_otlp`'s `return None` failure arm at :809-812 -- in the pinned tree.

category: a hand-maintained length with no compile-time or test enforcement, guarding an unchecked index
summary: The profiler's bucket array is sized by a hand-written literal whose only guard is a comment, and `record` indexes it with the enum's position unchecked, so adding a 23rd Stage panics the first sample taken under a profiling run.
failure_scenario: The constant's doc is profile.rs:136: '/// Number of `Stage` variants (the bucket-array length). Must equal the number of enum arms above.' That sentence is the entire enforcement -- there is no `const` assertion, no `Stage::ALL` slice, and no test over it. `buckets()` allocates exactly that many (profile.rs:219 `BUCKETS.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new((0..STAGE_COUNT).map(|_| Bucket::default()).collect()))`) and `record` indexes with no bound (profile.rs:230 `b[stage.idx()].record(n);`). CONCRETE: a contributor adds a 23rd `Stage` variant and a `start()` call site for it and does not notice the literal. With `BUSBAR_PROFILE` set -- the whole point of the module -- the first sample for the new stage panics with `index out of bounds: the len is 22 but the index is 22` inside `record`, on the request path, in a build where the round-2 audit already established there is no panic-catching layer. The same file contains a SECOND hand-kept list of all 22 stages in `dump` (profile.rs:285-308), so the same omission also silently prevents a stage from ever being printed. The tree already has the closed-set idiom this needs: busbar-contract/src/grammar.rs:159 `MaskKind::ALL`.
positive_control: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'STAGE_COUNT' crates/` returns exactly 2 hits, both in profile.rs: the definition at :137 and the single use at :219. No test names it, and no `const _: () = assert!(...)` references it. Positive control under the identical command form: `grep -rn 'BUCKET_CAP' crates/` returns 4 hits including the module's own test file, proving the grep does surface a constant's test coverage when there is any.

category: resource-leak
summary: Transport::close() is reachable from exactly one branch of the whole attempt lifecycle (full success through deliver(), attempt.rs:741-742); every other exit -- a write failure (this line), an attempt-timeout, a budget-timeout, an empty/erroring frame stream, and a non-success upstream status via classify_failure (line 354) -- drops the dialled Conn without ever calling close() on it.
failure_scenario: In send() (attempt.rs:478-530): line 491 binds `conn` from a successful dial; every subsequent early return in that function (line 501 on a write error, line 510 `SendOutcome::AttemptTimeout(ms)` when the per-attempt cap elapses waiting for the first frame, line 520/522-524 when the frame stream itself errors or ends with zero frames, and line 528 `SendOutcome::BudgetTimeout` when the outer deadline fires while `work` -- which owns `conn` -- is still in flight) drops `conn` with no call to `hop.transport.close(conn, ..)`. None of the SendOutcome variants on those paths carries a Conn, so the caller in the outer function (lines 312-334, and classify_failure at line 354 for a non-success status after a successful dial) has no way to close what send() already discarded. Conn has no Drop-based release contract in this crate's design: ports.rs:262-263 states outright for the sibling Permit type that 'Dropping the handle must free the slot; nothing in this crate calls a release verb' (an explicit RAII contract) -- but no equivalent contract or Drop impl exists for Conn, and the transport crates confirm why: busbar-transport-tcp and busbar-transport-stdio (both read in full this round) keep the real socket/child-process state in a registry keyed by connection id, and only the explicit Transport::close() call removes the entry. Concretely, for a stdio-backed egress destination (busbar-transport-stdio/src/transport.rs, read in full this round): close() at line 478-506 is the ONLY place that removes the entry from `self.conns: SyncMutex<HashMap<u64, Arc<ConnState>>>` and kills the child (`child.start_kill()`), and the frame-read-error arm inside frames() (around line 357, `Err(_) => break Some(Err(TransportError::Reset))`) does not touch the registry at all. So a write failure, attempt-timeout, or a spawned tool process that errors while answering leaves ConnState -- including a live, un-killed tokio::process::Child -- in the registry forever; kill_on_drop(true) (set at spawn time, transport.rs:196) never fires because the Arc holding the Child never drops. A pool that fails over repeatedly against one flaky stdio-backed destination accumulates one live subprocess per failed attempt for the life of the node: process-table exhaustion. busbar-transport-ws and busbar-transport-grpc (both spot-checked this round) are structured identically to stdio here -- each has exactly ONE `.remove(&id)` call site in its whole transport.rs, inside its own close(), with no self-cleaning frame-error arm at all -- so every non-success attempt against a ws- or grpc-backed destination leaks the full connection state (TLS session, HTTP/2 connection) with no self-healing path whatsoever. busbar-transport-tcp is the sole partial exception: its frame-stream error arm (transport.rs:169-181) does self-clean the registry entry and fd on a READ error, narrowing (but not eliminating) its exposure to the write-failure/attempt-timeout/budget-timeout branches, which still leak.
positive_control: The same function scrupulously guards every OTHER resource on every exit including a dropped future: JournalGuard (attempt.rs:211-247, Drop calls journal.abandoned), BudgetGuard (attempt.rs:676-680/750-760, Drop refunds the budget), ProbeGuard (select.rs:199-256, Drop calls release_probe unconditionally when armed), and the plain `permit: Permit` is explicitly `drop(permit)`'d on every failure branch (attempt.rs:278, 293, 315, 320, 325, 601, 743) on top of its own Drop-based release contract (ports.rs:262-263, 'nothing in this crate calls a release verb'). Four separate resource types are correctly balanced across every exit of this exact function; Conn/Transport::close() is the one exception with no guard of any kind, which is what proves this is an omission rather than 'how the design works' -- verified directly by reading attempt.rs in full (773 lines) and cross-checking against busbar-transport-tcp/src/transport.rs and busbar-transport-stdio/src/transport.rs (both read in full this round).

category: test-coverage
summary: The 'a transport crate must never name a plane or the kernel core' architecture test exists in only 2 of the 7 sibling transport crates in this slice (busbar-transport-http and busbar-transport-grpc); busbar-transport-ws, -tls, -sse, -stdio and -tcp have no equivalent test anywhere in their trees.

This runs.' -- i.e. it exists specifically because a transport crate silently gaining a dependency on busbar-kernel, busbar-contract::caps (production, non-test-fixture use), or any busbar-plane-* / busbar_llm / busbar_mcp / busbar_a2a / busbar_voice crate is exactly the shape of defect this whole audit's project rules call out as central ('Core naming a specific protocol or a specific plugin instance is itself a defect'). For 5 of the 7 sibling crates in this slice, nothing would catch that regression: a future PR that adds `busbar-kernel = { path = "../busbar-kernel" }` to busbar-transport-ws's or busbar-transport-tcp's Cargo.toml, or that has a contributor write `use busbar_kernel::...` inside one of those crates' src/ to reach a shared helper under time pressure, compiles and ships with zero red tests specific to that violation in that crate.

Also confirmed by direct read of all 7 Cargo.toml [dependencies] sections this round: today's src/ and Cargo.toml for the 5 uncovered crates are in fact clean (busbar-transport-stdio and -tcp depend only on busbar-contract/tokio/futures; busbar-transport-ws/-tls/-sse add only tokio-tungstenite/tokio-rustls/rustls/busbar-unit-transport-key/busbar-transport-http respectively -- no plane or kernel-core crate anywhere), so this is a coverage gap, not yet an active violation.

category: test-quality
summary: In the test whose entire job is to prove the plane/core-name scanner (contains_word) is not vacuous, one assertion's second OR-arm is a compile-time-constant true (a string literal containing its own uppercase substring), so this specific assertion passes even if contains_word were deleted or always returned false. The identical line exists in crates/busbar-transport-grpc/tests/no_plane_names.rs:192.
failure_scenario: A future edit that breaks contains_word's word-boundary matching for the exact shape 'identifier with a suffix immediately after the matched word' (e.g. changes it to require a following non-word character where none exists after `A2A_MOUNT`) would silently keep this assertion green, even though the doc comment two lines above claims 'Each assertion below plants exactly what the test above is looking for and requires the matcher to fire on it.' The scanner could regress on this exact shape and the positive-control test file would still show all green.
positive_control: Every other assertion in the same test function (the_scan_would_catch_a_planted_name, lines 191-207) has no such OR-escape and does correctly exercise contains_word alone -- e.g. `assert!(contains_word("this is the a2a binding", "a2a"));` at line 193 has no fallback and would fail if contains_word broke. Reading the whole function rather than just its name is what surfaces the one weakened assertion among many correct ones; confirmed present verbatim at the same line number (192) in both crates/busbar-transport-http/tests/no_plane_names.rs and crates/busbar-transport-grpc/tests/no_plane_names.rs.

category: test-coverage
summary: The absolute-path-only guard on child-process spawn (no shell, no relative path, refusing anything that does not start with '/') has zero exercising test anywhere in busbar-transport-stdio's own test files.

The sibling crates/busbar-transport-tcp/src/tests/mod.rs:320-323 DOES exercise its own analogous AddressRefused path (`upstream_dest("not-an-address")`), confirming the method finds real coverage where it exists and that this is a genuine gap rather than a search-tooling miss.
